- [ ] **Step 4: Implement them.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js

// ===========================================================================
// Recovery and repair decisions (spec §9.14 "Recovery", "Journal replay",
// "Only drained files replay", "Unknown records"; §9.6 recovery-stalled;
// §8.4 doctor --repair; §11 P21, P24; W1-B2 Task 7). Pure: the sweep's
// recovery step (Task 25) streams the journal and applies every action
// replayStep answers, deciding nothing of its own (the tick bounds included);
// planReplay is the same order over a whole journal in memory, which O56 pins;
// Task 25's tests pin the executor's agreement with it over the cases they
// name.
// ⟦D:history-recovery-replay⟧ ⟦D:history-journal-drained-record⟧
// ⟦D:history-redaction-journaled⟧ ⟦D:history-epoch-confirmation⟧
// ⟦D:history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks⟧
// ===========================================================================

/** The recovery step's phases, in order (§9.14). `index` applies the redact records and indexes drain-time
 *  verdicts and drained files; `apply` replays the journal; `reindex` re-runs the FTS derivation when the index
 *  pass learned a pair the store lacked. B4 inserts its export phases between `apply` and `reindex` (§9.14
 *  "Export replay"): this list is that seam. ⟦D:history-b4-after-b2⟧ */
export const RECOVER_PHASES = Object.freeze(['index', 'apply', 'reindex']);

const RECOVER_JOURNAL_CURSOR_RE = /^(index|apply)(?::([0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.jsonl):(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,15}))?(\+pairs)?$/;
const RECOVER_REINDEX_CURSOR_RE = /^reindex(?::(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,15}))?(\+pairs)?$/;

/** The recovery step's cursor as derivation_state ('recover', <bind ms>) keeps it and status prints it (§9.14):
 *  `<phase>` at a phase's start, `index:<YYYY-MM>.<writer>.jsonl:<byte offset>` or `apply:…` inside the journal,
 *  `reindex:<blob_id>` inside the FTS re-derivation, then `+pairs` once the index pass learned a pair the store
 *  lacked. It is advanced in the same transaction as the records it applies. */
export function formatRecoverCursor(c) {
  if (!RECOVER_PHASES.includes(c.phase)) throw new TypeError(`formatRecoverCursor: phase outside RECOVER_PHASES: ${String(c.phase)}`);
  let s = c.phase;
  if (c.phase === 'reindex') {
    if (c.blobId !== null) s += `:${c.blobId}`;
  } else if (c.file !== null) {
    s += `:${c.file}:${c.offset}`;
  }
  return c.pairsAdded ? `${s}+pairs` : s;
}

/** The cursor back, or null when it is not one: never a guess at where to resume. A NULL column (a step just
 *  registered by a binding verb) is the step's start. */
export function parseRecoverCursor(s) {
  if (s === null) return { phase: RECOVER_PHASES[0], file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: false };
  if (typeof s !== 'string') return null;
  const j = RECOVER_JOURNAL_CURSOR_RE.exec(s);
  if (j !== null) {
    const offset = j[3] === undefined ? 0 : Number(j[3]);
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(offset)) return null;
    return { phase: j[1], file: j[2] ?? null, offset, blobId: null, pairsAdded: j[4] !== undefined };
  }
  const r = RECOVER_REINDEX_CURSOR_RE.exec(s);
  if (r !== null) {
    const blobId = r[1] === undefined ? null : Number(r[1]);
    if (blobId !== null && !Number.isSafeInteger(blobId)) return null;
    return { phase: 'reindex', file: null, offset: 0, blobId, pairsAdded: r[2] !== undefined };
  }
  return null;
}

const journalCmpText = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
const journalCmpHead = (a, b) => (a === b ? 0 : a === null ? 1 : b === null ? -1 : a - b);
const journalFileOrder = (a, b) => journalCmpText(a.month, b.month) || journalCmpHead(a.headT, b.headT) || journalCmpText(a.name, b.name);

/** The journal files' apply order (§9.14 "Journal replay"): by the month in the name, then by the head
 *  record's time, then by name (code-unit order, never the locale's: DM8). Files of one month whose
 *  [headT, lastT] ranges overlap (a store run on two boxes at once, against §6.9's rule) form ONE group, which
 *  the caller merges by record time. A file with no readable head sorts last in its month, alone. */
export function orderJournalFiles(files) {
  const groups = [];
  let cur = null;
  for (const f of [...files].sort(journalFileOrder)) {
    const hi = f.lastT ?? f.headT;
    if (cur !== null && cur.month === f.month && f.headT !== null && cur.hi !== null && f.headT <= cur.hi) {
      cur.names.push(f.name);
      if (hi !== null && hi > cur.hi) cur.hi = hi;
      continue;
    }
    cur = { month: f.month, hi, names: [f.name] };
    groups.push(cur);
  }
  return groups.map((g) => g.names);
}

/** The first pass over one record (§9.14): a `redact` pair, a drain-time verdict (one keyed to its spool line's
 *  event_key) to apply at that line, or a `drained` record naming a file whose spool records may replay. */
export function indexRecord(r) {
  if (r.kind !== 'record') return {};
  const rec = r.rec;
  if (rec.k === 'redact') return { redact: { len: rec.len, sha256: rec.sha256, t: rec.t } };
  if (rec.k !== 'verdict') return {};
  if (rec.kind === 'drained') return { drainedFile: rec.file };
  if (rec.kind === 'bind' || rec.event_key === 'none') return {};
  return { verdictKey: rec.event_key };
}

/** The second pass over one record (§9.14). It never reads $REG and never re-decides: a spool record of a
 *  drained file becomes a receipt carrying the verdicts the drain took from it, in journal order, which the
 *  executor applies through decideEpochLine and the drain's own receipt functions; a verdict keyed to a line
 *  waits for that line; a verdict keyed `none` (a later confirmation, a backfill mapping, an operator's import)
 *  applies at its own position. A spool record whose file has no `drained` record is skipped: the file is still
 *  in .draining/ with its sidecar, and the live drain decides it after the step. A tick at or before the newest
 *  tick the store held when the step began (`ticksAfter`) is already there; one at or after the step's bind ms
 *  (`ticksBefore`, when it is a number) is a recovery pass's own record, journaled after the bind
 *  ⟦D:history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks⟧. A line that does not parse, or a `v` newer than
 *  this build, counts journal_line_malformed; an unknown kind journal_record_unknown; a head naming another
 *  store journal_head_mismatch. Nothing here throws on a record. */
export function replayStep(state, r) {
  if (r.kind === 'malformed' || r.kind === 'newer') return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }] };
  if (r.kind === 'unknown') return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' }] };
  const rec = r.rec;
  switch (rec.k) {
    case 'head':
      if (rec.store_id !== state.storeId) return { state: { ...state, file: null }, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' }] };
      return { state: { ...state, file: null }, actions: [] };
    case 'file':
      return { state: { ...state, file: rec.name, recvMs: rec.t }, actions: [{ do: 'file', name: rec.name, t: rec.t }] };
    case 'spool': {
      if (state.file === null) return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }] };
      if (!state.drained.has(state.file)) return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip-undrained', file: state.file }] };
      const key = eventKey(state.file, rec.ord);
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'receipt', key, ord: rec.ord, rec: rec.rec, recvMs: state.recvMs, verdicts: [...(state.verdictsByKey.get(key) ?? [])] }] };
    }
    case 'verdict':
      if (rec.kind === 'bind' || rec.kind === 'drained') return { state, actions: [] };
      if (rec.event_key !== 'none') return { state, actions: [] };
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'verdict', rec }] };
    case 'redact':
      return { state, actions: [] };
    case 'tick': {
      const before = typeof state.ticksBefore !== 'number' || rec.t < state.ticksBefore;
      return { state, actions: rec.t > state.ticksAfter && before ? [{ do: 'tick', t: rec.t, lagMs: rec.lag_ms }] : [] };
    }
    default:
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' }] };
  }
}

/** One merge group's records by record time, each file's own order kept, a tie to the earlier file in the group.
 *  A journal block (a `file` record and its `spool` records) shares one `t`, so a block is never split. */
function mergeJournalByTime(files) {
  const pos = files.map(() => 0);
  const out = [];
  for (;;) {
    let pick = -1;
    for (let f = 0; f < files.length; f += 1) {
      if (pos[f] >= files[f].recs.length) continue;
      if (pick < 0 || files[f].recs[pos[f]].t < files[pick].recs[pos[pick]].t) pick = f;
    }
    if (pick < 0) return out;
    out.push(files[pick].recs[pos[pick]].read);
    pos[pick] += 1;
  }
}

/** The whole replay of one store's journal, in memory (§9.14; the O56 pin). A file whose head names another
 *  store is dropped, counted once. The rest run in orderJournalFiles' order, each group merged by record time. A
 *  first pass indexes every redact pair (applied before anything else: "Redaction first"), every drain-time
 *  verdict by event_key (an identical re-appended verdict once) and every drained file; the second runs
 *  replayStep over the same stream. Duplicate receipts are left to the executor's receipt upsert. `ticksBefore`
 *  (the step's bind ms) defaults to null, no upper tick bound. */
export function planReplay({ storeId, files, ticksAfter, ticksBefore = null }) {
  const skips = [];
  const kept = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    const recs = [];
    let headT = null;
    let lastT = null;
    let foreign = false;
    for (const line of f.lines) {
      if (line === '') continue;
      const read = parseJournalRecord(line);
      if (recs.length === 0 && read.kind === 'record' && read.rec.k === 'head') {
        if (read.rec.store_id !== storeId) { foreign = true; break; }
        headT = read.rec.t;
      }
      const t = read.kind === 'record' ? read.rec.t : (lastT ?? headT ?? 0);
      if (read.kind === 'record') lastT = lastT === null ? t : Math.max(lastT, t);
      recs.push({ read, t });
    }
    if (foreign) {
      skips.push({ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' });
      continue;
    }
    kept.push({ name: f.name, month: f.month, writer: f.writer, headT, lastT, recs });
  }
  const byName = new Map(kept.map((f) => [f.name, f]));
  const stream = orderJournalFiles(kept).flatMap((g) => mergeJournalByTime(g.map((n) => byName.get(n))));
  const redacts = [];
  const seenPairs = new Set();
  const seenVerdicts = new Set();
  const verdictsByKey = new Map();
  const drained = new Set();
  for (const read of stream) {
    const ix = indexRecord(read);
    if (ix.redact !== undefined) {
      const pair = `${ix.redact.len}:${ix.redact.sha256}`;
      if (!seenPairs.has(pair)) {
        seenPairs.add(pair);
        redacts.push({ do: 'redact', ...ix.redact });
      }
    }
    if (ix.drainedFile !== undefined) drained.add(ix.drainedFile);
    if (ix.verdictKey !== undefined) {
      const same = canonicalJson(read.rec);
      if (!seenVerdicts.has(same)) {
        seenVerdicts.add(same);
        const list = verdictsByKey.get(ix.verdictKey) ?? [];
        list.push(read.rec);
        verdictsByKey.set(ix.verdictKey, list);
      }
    }
  }
  let state = { storeId, file: null, recvMs: 0, drained, verdictsByKey, ticksAfter, ticksBefore };
  const applied = [];
  for (const read of stream) {
    const step = replayStep(state, read);
    state = step.state;
    applied.push(...step.actions);
  }
  return [...skips, ...redacts, ...applied];
}

/** The recovery step's unmoved-tick count, kept in meta HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks (§9.6: FAIL
 *  recovery-stalled at RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS). A moved cursor resets it; a tick the floor or history-off held
 *  leaves it; any other tick adds one. */
export function nextUnmovedTicks({ prev, moved, held }) {
  if (moved) return 0;
  return held ? prev : prev + 1;
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/plugin/lcm-doctor-rollover-splits.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const foreignKeyKey = (row) => [row.table ?? '', row.rowid ?? '', row.parent ?? '', row.fkid ?? ''].join('\0');

/** doctor --repair's foreign-key proof (§8.4, P21): the violations `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` reports at the
 *  repair's completion, against the baseline taken ONCE before its first chunk and persisted with its resumable
 *  cursor, so a resumed repair diffs against the original baseline (RB7; Task 23 runs the check twice per repair,
 *  never per chunk). A violation is keyed by (table, rowid, parent, fkid); one
 *  outside the baseline is NEW, and a repair that made one is refused. No v1 table is WITHOUT ROWID, so rowid is
 *  never NULL for a v1 row. */
export function diffForeignKeys(baseline, current) {
  const base = new Set(baseline.map(foreignKeyKey));
  const newViolations = [];
  let preExisting = 0;
  for (const row of current) {
    if (base.has(foreignKeyKey(row))) preExisting += 1;
    else newViolations.push(row);
  }
  return { newViolations, preExisting };
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/db/migration.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** Each FTS table's shadow tables, listed per table (P24): the contentless blobs_fts (content='',
 *  contentless_delete=1) has no `_content` shadow, so a list naming one for every table would read a healthy
 *  index as broken and rebuild it on every repair. */
export const FTS_SHADOWS = Object.freeze({
  blobs_fts: Object.freeze(['blobs_fts_config', 'blobs_fts_data', 'blobs_fts_docsize', 'blobs_fts_idx']),
  nodes_fts: Object.freeze(['nodes_fts_config', 'nodes_fts_content', 'nodes_fts_data', 'nodes_fts_docsize', 'nodes_fts_idx']),
});
/** Each FTS table's columns, as B1's FTS_DDL creates them. */
export const FTS_COLUMNS = Object.freeze({
  blobs_fts: Object.freeze(['body']),
  nodes_fts: Object.freeze(['gist', 'topics', 'refs']),
});

/** Whether each FTS table is whole (§8.4 doctor --repair's self-heal, P24): the table, every shadow it should
 *  have, and every column. The store adapter measures `tables` (sqlite_master) and `columns` (pragma_table_info);
 *  the repair rebuilds a table this answers false for. */
export function ftsTablesHealthy({ tables, columns }) {
  const healthy = (t) => tables.has(t) && FTS_SHADOWS[t].every((s) => tables.has(s))
    && FTS_COLUMNS[t].every((c) => (columns[t] ?? []).includes(c));
  return { blobs: healthy('blobs_fts'), nodes: healthy('nodes_fts') };
}
```

  - The `\0` in `foreignKeyKey` is the two-character escape in source, never a raw NUL byte.
  - The two `derived from lossless-claw` comments are the P21 and P24 markers. B1's `license.test.ts` pins them against Step 6's entries: one entry per (ours, upstream) pair.

```ts
export const RECOVER_PHASES: readonly string[];

  | { do: 'receipt'; key: string; ord: number; rec: Record<string, unknown>; recvMs: number; verdicts: JournalRecord[] }
  | { do: 'skip-undrained'; file: string }

  | { do: 'tick'; t: number; lagMs: number | null }

}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's, byte for byte, written again here so this task stands alone. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8' });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

```bash
]
```

    - `('transcript-forked', <transcript_pk>)`, present once that transcript is counted;
    - `('leaf-crashed', <boundary entry_id>)`, above.

**Spec:**
- §6.1: the span rule (positions from the copy holding each boundary; rows absent from it join no leaf, counted `rows_unspanned`; a copy with no uuid-superset counts `transcript_forked` once); two forks after one head (`leaf_id_forked`); node kinds.
- §6.2: `nodes`, `node_sources`, `node_refs`, `nodes_fts` (redacted gists, topics and refs); the producer of boundary N (the first non-unknown assistant row after its summary row, in the copy that holds it).
- §6.4: compact-card reuse by import plus two in-place `export` keywords; lib stays L1 with the toolkit injected.
- §7.4:
  - item 1: the summary row via `anchorUuid`; `anchor_is_boundary`; the echo row never read; a missing anchor row is `raw_leaf`;
  - item 2: blocks only with a steer receipt, otherwise `not-requested`;
  - items 6-10: caps, refs mined from the span's tool_use rows (origin `tool_use`), the native gist from the last two sections chosen by `summarizeMetadata.direction`, `directive_flag` only, and the counters stratified by producer.
- §9.2 step 6: derive.
- Pins: **PX1**, **PX7**, **PX25**, **DM25**, **DM36**, **DM37**.

  - ⟦D:history-span-per-boundary-copy⟧
  - ⟦D:history-leaf-id-fork-qualified⟧
  - ⟦D:history-summary-anchor-is-boundary⟧
  - ⟦D:history-native-gist-last-summary-open⟧
  - ⟦D:history-producer-backend⟧
  - ⟦D:history-steer-receipt⟧
  - ⟦D:history-tick-order⟧
  - ⟦D:history-node-indexes-by-derivation⟧ (NEW). v1 has no index on `nodes(boundary_entry_id)` (which "has this boundary a leaf" reads every tick) or `node_children(child_id)` (who is a node's parent). A schema migration would escalate to `snapshot-needs-op` on every real store (§6.11). So derivation creates them, IF NOT EXISTS, as it creates the FTS tables.
  - ⟦D:history-summary-direction-from-source-line⟧ (NEW). B1 stores a summary row's message only, not `summarizeMetadata`. The direction is read from the row's own line in its holding file:
    - through B1's admission (`O_NOFOLLOW`, realpath under a rostered `projects/` root);
    - at its membership byte offset;
    - bounded at `LINE_MAX`;
    - only when the line's uuid matches.
    A file gone or changed gives `null`, and the pair then follows the text.
  - ⟦D:history-native-refs-no-prlink⟧ (NEW). §7.4 item 7 also unions `pr-link` metadata refs (origin `meta`). B1 never stores uuid-less rows (G13), so there is no such row to mine. Native refs are the span's `tool_use` paths only.
  - ⟦D:history-raw-leaf-grace⟧ (Task 5's): a boundary row with no time of its own takes the newest stamped row before it in the holding copy.
  - ⟦D:history-parser-crash-recorded⟧ (NEW, RB5). §9.2's `parser_crash` rule (roll back, hold the cursor, retry next tick) is the transcript reader's; applied to node derivation it would re-parse a poison boundary every 90 s tick, grow `parser_crash` without bound and stall that copy's fan-in. A node-parser throw instead writes its leaf `parse-failed` (a NEW `PARSE_STATUS` word: none of `ok`, `degraded`, `invalid`, `absent`, `not-requested` means "the parser threw"), or a `leaf-crashed` marker when no leaf can be written; it is counted once, and only reparse retries it.
  - ⟦D:history-summary-size-counters-from-store⟧ (NEW). §7.4 item 10 also names block chars, and summary chars and duration with versus without steering. Every input is a stored column: the summary blob's `raw_len` through `nodes.summary_blob_id`, `boundaries.duration_ms`, and `steer_receipts` for the arm. Every W1 leaf is the without-steering arm, so W3 reads both arms from the store, and W1 folds no such counter.

```js
// ===========================================================================
// Leaf helpers derive.mjs composes (spec §6.1 "The copy", §7.4 items 2-8;
// W1-B2 Task 8). Pure.
// ===========================================================================

/** A summary row's `summarizeMetadata.direction` (§7.4 item 8): `from` or `up_to`, else null. derive.mjs reads
 *  the row from the line it came from, because the store keeps a summary row's message only.
 *  ⟦D:history-summary-direction-from-source-line⟧ */
export function directionOfSummaryRow(row) {
  const meta = row !== null && typeof row === 'object' && !Array.isArray(row) ? row.summarizeMetadata : undefined;
  const d = meta !== null && typeof meta === 'object' ? meta.direction : undefined;
  return d === 'from' || d === 'up_to' ? d : null;
}

 *  below lands on redacted text (§8.3, SE1):
 *  - the gist, trimmed, cut at GIST_MAX by Task 4's capText, then trimmed at its end again: the form Task 4's
 *    gistSha hashes, so a later block carrying this gist word for word is a carried copy even past the cap; empty
 *    is null;
 *  - topics: the `Expand for details about:` field split on commas, through capTopics (each once, at most
 *    TOPICS_MAX of at most TOPIC_CHARS);
 *  - refs: the `refs:` values classifyRef recognises, origin `model` (capRefs runs over the leaf's union).
 *  Both cuts are surrogate-safe. A cut sets `capped`; no marker is ever inserted. */
export function blockFields(block) {
  const gist = capText(typeof block.gist === 'string' ? block.gist.trim() : '', GIST_MAX);
  const topics = capTopics((typeof block.expand === 'string' ? block.expand : '').split(','));
  const refs = [];
  for (const v of Array.isArray(block.refs) ? block.refs : []) {
    const kind = typeof v === 'string' ? classifyRef(v) : null;
    if (kind !== null) refs.push({ kind, value: v, origin: 'model' });
  }
  const text = gist.text.trimEnd();
  return { gist: text === '' ? null : text, topics: topics.topics, refs, capped: gist.capped || topics.capped };
}

/** The steer receipt a leaf's span carries (§7.4 item 2): the receipt naming this leaf's id, else a generic one
 *  (leafId '') received after the previous boundary and no later than this one; null when neither. An epoch's
 *  first leaf has no lower bound. ⟦D:history-steer-receipt⟧ */
export function pickReceipt(receipts, { id, afterMs, uptoMs }) {
  const exact = receipts.find((r) => r.leafId === id);
  if (exact !== undefined) return exact;
  return receipts.find((r) => r.leafId === '' && (afterMs === null || r.tsMs > afterMs) && (uptoMs === null || r.tsMs <= uptoMs)) ?? null;
}

/** The copy that holds a boundary (§6.1 "The copy"): among a transcript's files that have the boundary row as a
 *  member, a live one (source_key '') before a retired or exported one, then the smallest file_id; null when no file
 *  holds it. derive.mjs measures `live` and `holds`; Task 9's fan-in splits its slots by this same answer.
 *  ⟦D:history-span-per-boundary-copy⟧ */
export function pickHoldingCopy(files) {
  let best = null;
  for (const f of files) {
    if (!f.holds) continue;
    if (best === null || (f.live && !best.live) || (f.live === best.live && f.fileId < best.fileId)) best = f;
  }
  return best === null ? null : best.fileId;
}

/** A main transcript's fork counts (§6.1), from what derive.mjs measured over its LIVE copies: each copy's row
 *  count, the rows in any of them, the rows in a copy that holds one of its leaves' boundaries, and how many copies
 *  hold one. `unspanned` is how many rows no holding copy has: they join no leaf (none while no copy holds a leaf,
 *  when every row is still live tail). `forked` is true when two or more live copies exist and none holds every row
 *  (no uuid-superset). */
export function forkCounts({ liveSizes, unionSize, coveredSize, holdingCopies }) {
  return {
    unspanned: holdingCopies === 0 ? 0 : Math.max(0, unionSize - coveredSize),
    forked: liveSizes.length > 1 && !liveSizes.some((n) => n === unionSize),
  };
}
```

  - `capText`, `capTopics` and `gistSha` are Task 4's declarations in the same module. `gistSha` hashes `capText(String(gist).trim(), GIST_MAX).text.trimEnd()` (IN-6, Task 4's side), the form `blockFields` stores; the `gistSha` case of Step 2 pins the two together.

```js

// ── W1-B2 Task 8: derivation_state steps by name (§6.2 `derivation_state`) ─────────────────────────────────────

/** One derivation step's row: its cursor (TEXT, as the step wrote it) and when it completed; null when the step
 *  has no row. */
export function getStep(db, step, version) {
  const r = db.prepare('SELECT cursor, completed_ms FROM derivation_state WHERE step = ? AND version = ?').get(step, version);
  if (r === undefined) return null;
  return { cursor: r.cursor === null ? null : String(r.cursor), completedMs: r.completed_ms === null ? null : Number(r.completed_ms) };
}

/** Upsert one derivation step's row; the caller holds the transaction. An omitted `completedMs` leaves an
 *  existing completed_ms as it is (a new row gets NULL); a number or null sets it. */
export function setStep(db, step, version, cursor, completedMs) {
  if (completedMs === undefined) {
    db.prepare(`INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL)
      ON CONFLICT (step, version) DO UPDATE SET cursor = excluded.cursor`).run(step, version, cursor);
    return;
  }
  db.prepare(`INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
    ON CONFLICT (step, version) DO UPDATE SET cursor = excluded.cursor, completed_ms = excluded.completed_ms`)
    .run(step, version, cursor, completedMs);
}
```

```ts
// server/test/history-derive.test.ts: node derivation through REAL sweep ticks (spec 2026-10-05 §6.1 span rule
// and forks, §6.2 `nodes` and the producer, §7.4 items 1, 2, 6-10; W1-B2 plan Task 8, and Task 9 appends). Each
// describe builds one fixture HOME, plants sessions and transcripts in the measured row shapes
// (historyFixtures.ts's compactionSequence), spools the SessionStart line the hook would, and runs sweep.mjs as
// the shim would; the cases then read the store read-only. Linux only (O24): it spawns the sweep.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import {
  makeHistoryBox, runSweep, plantSession, plantTranscript, spoolLine, openStoreRO, counters, skipOnDarwin,
  type HistoryBox,
} from './historyHelpers.js';
import { compactionSequence, steeredBlock, userRow, type Row } from './historyFixtures.js';
import { leafId, historyPaths, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, GIST_MAX } from '../../ccd/history/lib.mjs';
import { createStore, openWriter, closeWriter, withTx, getStep, setStep } from '../../ccd/history/store.mjs';

skipOnDarwin();

const SLUG = '-home-u-worktrees-p-quiet-basin';
const GEN = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000aa';
/** A day before now: every boundary's raw-leaf grace (lib RAW_LEAF_GRACE_MS) is long past whatever day the suite
 *  runs, so a file read to its end is final. */
const T0 = Date.now() - 86_400_000;
type Seq = ReturnType<typeof compactionSequence>;

/** One session: its registry rows, its transcript under `account`'s projects/, and the SessionStart(startup) line
 *  the hook spools. Its `reg` equals its sid, so the drain confirms the epoch on the line's own evidence. */
function plant(box: HistoryBox, id: string, uuid: string, rows: readonly Row[], account = 'claude'): void {
  plantSession(box, id, { uuid, generation: GEN, project: 'demo', workdir: '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin' });
  plantTranscript(box, account, SLUG, uuid, [...rows]);
  spoolLine(box, id, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id, sid: uuid, src: 'startup', reg: uuid, gen: GEN });
}

/** Scheduled passes, as the timer runs them. The first creates the store and renames the spool files; the next
 *  drains them (the epochs confirm) and derives; one more lets every boundary meet its readiness. */
function settle(box: HistoryBox, passes = 3): void {
  for (let i = 0; i < passes; i += 1) {
    const r = runSweep(box);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
  }
}

function q<T>(box: HistoryBox, sql: string, ...args: (string | number)[]): T[] {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try { return db.prepare(sql).all(...args) as T[]; } finally { db.close(); }
}

interface LeafRow {
  node_id: string; kind: string; status: string; gist: string | null; topics: string | null;
  summary_blob_id: number | null; span_start_uuid: string; boundary_uuid: string; ord: number;
}
const leavesOf = (box: HistoryBox, uuid: string): LeafRow[] => q<LeafRow>(box,
  `SELECT n.node_id, n.kind, n.status, n.gist, n.topics, n.summary_blob_id, n.span_start_uuid, e.uuid AS boundary_uuid, b.ord
   FROM nodes n JOIN boundaries b ON b.entry_id = n.boundary_entry_id JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = b.entry_id
   JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = n.transcript_pk
   WHERE t.cc_session_uuid = ? AND n.depth = 0 ORDER BY b.ord`, uuid);
const sourcesOf = (box: HistoryBox, nodeId: string): string[] => q<{ uuid: string }>(box,
  'SELECT e.uuid FROM node_sources ns JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = ns.entry_id WHERE ns.node_id = ? ORDER BY ns.ord', nodeId)
  .map((r) => r.uuid);
const blobOf = (box: HistoryBox, uuid: string): number | null =>
  q<{ blob_id: number }>(box, 'SELECT blob_id FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?', uuid)[0]?.blob_id ?? null;
/** Leaf k's sources by construction (§6.1; Task 5's DM5). */
const expectedSources = (s: Seq, k: number): string[] => [
  ...(k === 0 ? [] : [...s.keptUuids[k - 1]!, ...s.afterUuids[k - 1]!]),
  ...s.workUuids[k]!, ...s.unkeptUuids[k]!,
];
const firstUuid = (s: Seq): string => String(s.rows[0]!['uuid']);
const withDirection = (s: Seq, direction: 'from' | 'up_to'): Row[] =>
  s.rows.map((r) => (r['uuid'] === s.summaryUuids[0] ? { ...r, summarizeMetadata: { direction } } : r));

const UNCLOSED = (): string => [
  '<analysis>', 'Reviewing the unclosed fixture.', '</analysis>',
  '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   The unclosed fixture.',
  '8. Current Work:', '   Unclosed current work runs to the end of the row.',
  '9. Optional Next Step:', '   Unclosed next step.',
].join('\n');
/** The GPT shape (§7.4 item 8, RG12): a surviving second <analysis>, then two unclosed <summary> opens, each with
 *  both closing headings. */
const GPT_SHAPED = (): string => [
  '<analysis>', 'A first analysis, closed.', '</analysis>',
  '<analysis>', '8. Current Work:', '   ANALYSIS current work inside the surviving analysis.',
  '<summary>', '8. Current Work:', '   FIRST current work.', '9. Optional Next Step:', '   FIRST next step.',
  '<summary>', '8. Current Work:', '   SECOND current work.', '9. Optional Next Step:', '   SECOND next step.',
].join('\n');
/** Both closing pairs in one summary, so only the direction can choose (§7.4 item 8). */
const BOTH_PAIRS = (): string => [
  '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   A summary holding both closing pairs.',
  '8. Current Work:', '   CURRENT-PAIR text, which a from summary ends with.',
  '9. Optional Next Step:', '   CURRENT-PAIR next step.',
  '10. Work Completed:', '   COMPLETED-PAIR text, which an up_to summary ends with.',
  '11. Context for Continuing Work:', '   COMPLETED-PAIR context.',
  '</summary>',
].join('\n');
/** A summary QUOTING a block, at a boundary with no steer receipt (§7.4 item 2). */
const QUOTED = (): string => [
  '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   Testing the block parser on a fixture.',
  '8. Current Work:', '   Quoting a fixture block while testing the parser:',
  '<ccrc-leaf id="L0123456789abcdef0123">',
  'gist: A quoted fixture gist that is long enough to pass the forty character floor of the parser.',
  'Expand for details about: quoted, fixture',
  'refs: server/test/history-parser.test.ts',
  '</ccrc-leaf>',
  '9. Optional Next Step:', '   Keep the quoted block as data.',
  '</summary>',
].join('\n');

});

describe('forked copies: positions come from the copy that holds each boundary (DM36; spec 6.1)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-fork';
  const U = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000f1';
  let box: HistoryBox;
  let pre: Seq; let sufA: Seq; let sufB: Seq;
  beforeAll(() => {
    box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm36-');
    pre = compactionSequence({ n: 1, trigger: 'manual', unkeptBeforeBoundary: 2, seed: 0x91, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 });
    sufA = compactionSequence({ n: 1, trigger: 'auto', seed: 0x92, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 + 600_000 });
    sufB = compactionSequence({ n: 0, trigger: 'manual', tailRows: 20, seed: 0x93, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 + 600_000 });
    plantSession(box, ID, { uuid: U, generation: GEN, project: 'demo', workdir: '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin' });
    plantTranscript(box, 'claude', SLUG, U, [...pre.rows, ...sufA.rows]);      // copy A: compacts again
    plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', SLUG, U, [...pre.rows, ...sufB.rows]);    // copy B: larger, never compacts again
    spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID, sid: U, src: 'startup', reg: U, gen: GEN });
    settle(box);
  }, 240_000);

  it('DM36 CONTROL: copy A, under the first rostered home, was bound first; copy B is the larger', () => {
    const files = q<{ file_id: number; path: string; n: number }>(box,
      `SELECT f.file_id, p.path, (SELECT count(*) FROM memberships m WHERE m.file_id = f.file_id) AS n
       FROM ingest_files f JOIN file_paths p ON p.file_id = f.file_id ORDER BY f.file_id`);
    expect(files).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(files[0]!.path.startsWith(`${box.accountHome['claude']!}${path.sep}`)).toBe(true);
    expect(files[1]!.n).toBeGreaterThan(files[0]!.n);
  });

  it('DM36: each leaf reads the copy that holds its boundary: exact sources, unchanged ids', () => {
    const leaves = leavesOf(box, U);
    expect(leaves.map((l) => l.boundary_uuid)).toEqual([pre.boundaryUuids[0], sufA.boundaryUuids[0]]);
    expect(sourcesOf(box, leaves[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(expectedSources(pre, 0));
    expect(sourcesOf(box, leaves[1]!.node_id)).toEqual([
      ...pre.keptUuids[0]!, ...pre.afterUuids[0]!, ...pre.liveUuids, ...sufA.workUuids[0]!, ...sufA.unkeptUuids[0]!,
    ]);
    expect(leaves.map((l) => l.node_id)).toEqual([leafId(ID, U, firstUuid(pre)), leafId(ID, U, pre.headUuids[0]!)]);
  });

  it("DM36: rows only in the other copy's suffix are stored and in no leaf; rows_unspanned and transcript_forked are counted", () => {
    const stored = new Set(q<{ uuid: string }>(box, 'SELECT uuid FROM entries').map((r) => r.uuid));
    const inLeaves = new Set(q<{ uuid: string }>(box, 'SELECT e.uuid FROM node_sources ns JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = ns.entry_id').map((r) => r.uuid));
    for (const u of sufB.liveUuids) {
      expect(stored.has(u), u).toBe(true);
      expect(inLeaves.has(u), u).toBe(false);
    }
    const c = counters(box);
    expect(c['rows_unspanned']).toBe(sufB.liveUuids.length);
    expect(c['transcript_forked']).toBe(1);
  });

  it('DM36: rows appended later to the copy that holds no new boundary are counted too, with no leaf derived in that tick', () => {
    const entriesBefore = q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries')[0]!.n;
    const nodesBefore = q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes')[0]!.n;
    const p = path.join(box.accountHome['claude-a']!, 'projects', SLUG, `${U}.jsonl`);
    for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i += 1) {
      const row = userRow({ uuid: `000000b4-0000-4000-8000-00000000000${i}`, ts: new Date(T0 + 9_000_000 + i * 1000).toISOString(), sessionId: U, text: `a later turn in copy B ${i}` });
      fs.appendFileSync(p, `${JSON.stringify(row)}\n`);
    }
    spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: ID, sid: U });   // the hint that re-reads both copies
    settle(box);
    expect(q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries')[0]!.n, 'CONTROL: copy B was read again').toBe(entriesBefore + 3);
    expect(q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes')[0]!.n, 'CONTROL: no leaf was derived').toBe(nodesBefore);
    const c = counters(box);
    expect(c['rows_unspanned']).toBe(sufB.liveUuids.length + 3);
    expect(c['transcript_forked'], 'counted once').toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('two forks after one head: the first bound keeps the plain id, the later is boundary-qualified (DM37; spec 6.1)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-twofork';
  const U = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000f2';
  let box: HistoryBox;
  let pre: Seq; let sufA: Seq; let sufB: Seq;
  beforeAll(() => {
    box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm37-');
    pre = compactionSequence({ n: 1, trigger: 'manual', seed: 0xa1, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 });
    sufA = compactionSequence({ n: 1, trigger: 'manual', seed: 0xa2, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 + 600_000 });
    sufB = compactionSequence({ n: 1, trigger: 'auto', seed: 0xa3, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 + 600_000 });
    plantSession(box, ID, { uuid: U, generation: GEN, project: 'demo', workdir: '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin' });
    plantTranscript(box, 'claude', SLUG, U, [...pre.rows, ...sufA.rows]);
    plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', SLUG, U, [...pre.rows, ...sufB.rows]);
    spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID, sid: U, src: 'startup', reg: U, gen: GEN });
    settle(box);
  }, 240_000);

  it('DM37: all three boundary rows exist, with distinct ord', () => {
    const rows = q<{ uuid: string; ord: number }>(box, 'SELECT e.uuid, b.ord FROM boundaries b JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = b.entry_id ORDER BY b.ord');
    expect(rows.map((r) => r.uuid)).toEqual([pre.boundaryUuids[0], sufA.boundaryUuids[0], sufB.boundaryUuids[0]]);
    expect(new Set(rows.map((r) => r.ord)).size).toBe(3);
  });

  it('DM37: the first bound keeps the plain id, the second takes the boundary-qualified id; leaf_id_forked +1', () => {
    const byBoundary = new Map(leavesOf(box, U).map((l) => [l.boundary_uuid, l]));
    const head = pre.headUuids[0]!;
    const a = byBoundary.get(sufA.boundaryUuids[0]!)!;
    const b = byBoundary.get(sufB.boundaryUuids[0]!)!;
    expect(a.node_id).toBe(leafId(ID, U, head));
    expect(b.node_id).toBe(leafId(ID, U, head, sufB.boundaryUuids[0]!));
    expect(b.span_start_uuid).toBe(head);
    expect(sourcesOf(box, b.node_id)).toEqual([
      ...pre.keptUuids[0]!, ...pre.afterUuids[0]!, ...pre.liveUuids, ...sufB.workUuids[0]!, ...sufB.unkeptUuids[0]!,
    ]);
    const c = counters(box);
    expect(c['leaf_id_forked']).toBe(1);
    expect(c['transcript_forked']).toBe(1);
    expect(c['rows_unspanned'] ?? 0, 'each copy holds a boundary, so every row is in a holding copy').toBe(0);
  });

  it('DM37: a re-ingest mints neither id again', () => {
    const before = q<{ node_id: string }>(box, 'SELECT node_id FROM nodes ORDER BY node_id').map((r) => r.node_id);
    const entriesBefore = q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries')[0]!.n;
    ['claude', 'claude-a'].forEach((acct, i) => {
      const p = path.join(box.accountHome[acct]!, 'projects', SLUG, `${U}.jsonl`);
      const row = userRow({ uuid: `000000a4-0000-4000-8000-00000000000${i + 1}`, ts: new Date(T0 + 9_000_000).toISOString(), sessionId: U, text: `a later turn in copy ${i}` });
      fs.appendFileSync(p, `${JSON.stringify(row)}\n`);
    });
    spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: ID, sid: U });   // the hint that re-reads both copies
    settle(box);
    const entriesAfter = q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries')[0]!.n;
    expect(entriesAfter, 'CONTROL: both copies were read again').toBe(entriesBefore + 2);
    expect(q<{ node_id: string }>(box, 'SELECT node_id FROM nodes ORDER BY node_id').map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual(before);
    expect(counters(box)['leaf_id_forked']).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('a carried copy of an earlier gist is invalid even past the cap (spec 7.4 items 2, 5, 6, 10; IN-6)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-carried';
  const U = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000f4';
  /** One gist longer than GIST_MAX, which the next summary's block carries word for word. */
  const LONG = `Carried fixture gist that runs past the cap. ${'carried words '.repeat(110)}`.trim();
  const steered = (): string => [
    '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   A steered fixture summary.', '</summary>',
    steeredBlock({ gist: LONG, expand: 'carried, fixture', refs: 'server/test/history-derive.test.ts' }),
  ].join('\n');
  let box: HistoryBox;
  beforeAll(() => {
    box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-carried-');
    const seq = compactionSequence({ n: 2, trigger: 'manual', summaryText: steered, seed: 0xa5, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 });
    plant(box, ID, U, seq.rows);
    // Two generic steer receipts, one inside each leaf's window (the previous boundary, this boundary].
    const at = (u: string): number => Date.parse(String(seq.rows.find((r) => r['uuid'] === u)!['timestamp']));
    for (const b of seq.boundaryUuids) spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'steer', id: ID, sid: U, leaf: '', ts: at(b) - 500 });
    settle(box);
  }, 240_000);

  it('leaf 0 is steered and cut at GIST_MAX; leaf 1 carries that gist and is invalid, counted carried_copies and by its reason', () => {
    expect(LONG.length, 'CONTROL: the carried gist is longer than the cap').toBeGreaterThan(GIST_MAX);
    const [l0, l1] = leavesOf(box, U);
    expect({ kind: l0!.kind, status: l0!.status, gist: l0!.gist }).toEqual({ kind: 'steered_leaf', status: 'ok', gist: LONG.slice(0, GIST_MAX) });
    expect({ kind: l1!.kind, status: l1!.status }).toEqual({ kind: 'native_leaf', status: 'invalid' });
    const c = counters(box);
    expect(c['carried_copies']).toBe(1);
    expect(c['leaf_reason:carried-copy:anthropic']).toBe(1);
    expect(c['leaf_status:ok:anthropic']).toBe(1);
    expect(Object.keys(c).filter((k) => k.startsWith('leaf_reason:')), 'an ok leaf has no reason; both spans had a receipt')
      .toEqual(['leaf_reason:carried-copy:anthropic']);
  });
});

describe('a parser throw is recorded, counted once and never parsed again by a tick (RB5; NEW history-parser-crash-recorded)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-crash';
  const U = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000f3';
  type Kit = { HEADING_RE: RegExp; fencedRanges(t: string): unknown; mineTokens(w: string, re: RegExp | null): unknown };
  type Derived = { derived: number; waiting: number; failed: number };
  let box: HistoryBox;
  let seq: Seq;
  beforeAll(() => {
    box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-crash-');
    seq = compactionSequence({ n: 3, trigger: 'manual', seed: 0xb1, sessionId: U, startMs: T0 });
    plant(box, ID, U, seq.rows);
    settle(box);
  }, 240_000);

  type Writer = ReturnType<typeof openWriter>;
  const write = (fn: (db: Writer) => void): void => {
    const db = openWriter(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    try { withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { fn(db); }); } finally { closeWriter(db); }
  };
  /** Delete one node and what references it, as a test only does: its nodes_fts row, its refs; node_sources cascade. */
  const dropNode = (db: Writer, id: string): void => {
    if (db.prepare("SELECT 1 AS x FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'nodes_fts'").get() !== undefined) {
      db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = (SELECT rowid FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?)').run(id);
    }
    db.prepare('DELETE FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?').run(id);
    db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?').run(id);
  };
  const entryOf = (uuid: string): number => q<{ entry_id: number }>(box, 'SELECT entry_id FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?', uuid)[0]!.entry_id;
  const crashes = (): number => counters(box)['parser_crash'] ?? 0;
  const atBoundary = (entryId: number) => q<{ node_id: string; kind: string; status: string; gist: string | null; topics: string | null; summary_blob_id: number | null }>(box,
    'SELECT node_id, kind, status, gist, topics, summary_blob_id FROM nodes WHERE boundary_entry_id = ? ORDER BY node_id', entryId);
  /** One in-process derivation pass, as the tick runs it, with `kit` as the node toolkit (an in-process seam: the
   *  sweep never sets ictx.nodeKit). */
  async function derive(kit: (real: Kit) => Kit): Promise<Derived> {
    const S = (await import('../../ccd/history/sweep.mjs')) as unknown as {
      makeIngestCtx(home: string, homes: string[], nowMs: number, ids: unknown): Record<string, unknown>;
      newBudget(): unknown;
    };
    const D = (await import('../../ccd/history/derive.mjs')) as unknown as {
      nodeToolkit(): Kit;
      deriveLeaves(db: Writer, ictx: Record<string, unknown>, budget: unknown): Derived;
    };
    const db = openWriter(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    try {
      const ictx = S.makeIngestCtx(box.home, box.homes, Date.now(), null);
      ictx['nodeKit'] = kit(D.nodeToolkit());
      return D.deriveLeaves(db, ictx, S.newBudget());
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  }

  it('a throw inside the parser writes the leaf parse-failed under its own id and sources; a throw before the leaf leaves a marker; the next pass parses neither', async () => {
    const [l0, l1, l2] = leavesOf(box, U);
    expect([l0, l1, l2].every((l) => l !== undefined && l.kind === 'native_leaf'), 'CONTROL: three native leaves').toBe(true);
    expect(crashes(), 'CONTROL: the ticks crashed nothing').toBe(0);
    const src1 = sourcesOf(box, l1!.node_id);
    const [b0, b1, b2] = seq.boundaryUuids.map(entryOf);
    const forkedId = leafId(ID, U, seq.headUuids[1]!, seq.boundaryUuids[2]!);
    write((db) => {
      dropNode(db, l1!.node_id);
      dropNode(db, l2!.node_id);
      // Boundary 2's plain id now names boundary 0 and its fork-qualified id is taken: its insert can only fail.
      const plantNode = db.prepare(`INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status,
          boundary_entry_id, parser_version, created_ms)
        SELECT ?, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, 'raw_leaf', 0, 'not-requested', ?, parser_version, created_ms FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?`);
      plantNode.run(l2!.node_id, b0!, l0!.node_id);
      plantNode.run(forkedId, null, l0!.node_id);
      db.prepare("DELETE FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'leaves'").run();
    });
    const throwing = (real: Kit): Kit => ({ ...real, fencedRanges: () => { throw new Error('a planted parser bug'); } });
    expect(await derive(throwing)).toEqual({ derived: 1, waiting: 0, failed: 1 });
    expect(await derive(throwing), 'the next pass parses neither boundary again').toEqual({ derived: 0, waiting: 0, failed: 0 });
    expect(crashes(), 'each throw counted once').toBe(2);
    expect(atBoundary(b1!)).toEqual([{
      node_id: l1!.node_id, kind: 'raw_leaf', status: 'parse-failed', gist: null, topics: null,
      summary_blob_id: blobOf(box, seq.summaryUuids[1]!),
    }]);
    expect(sourcesOf(box, l1!.node_id), 'its own sources, as derived before').toEqual(src1);
    expect(q<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?', l1!.node_id)[0]!.n).toBe(0);
    expect(atBoundary(b2!), 'no leaf at the boundary whose insert failed').toEqual([]);
    expect(q<{ cursor: string }>(box, "SELECT cursor FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'leaf-crashed' AND version = ?", b2!))
      .toEqual([{ cursor: String(NODE_PARSER_VERSION) }]);
    const [leaves] = q<{ cursor: string }>(box, "SELECT cursor FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'leaves' AND version = ?", NODE_PARSER_VERSION);
    expect(Number(leaves!.cursor), 'the cursor moved past both').toBe(b2);
    expect(Object.keys(counters(box)).filter((k) => k.includes('parse-failed')), 'a crash is no compliance outcome').toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a summary row stored but unreadable (a tombstoned blob) makes a raw leaf that still names its summary, counted summary_unreadable (spec 6.1)', async () => {
    const id0 = leafId(ID, U, firstUuid(seq));
    const b0 = entryOf(seq.boundaryUuids[0]!);
    const blob0 = blobOf(box, seq.summaryUuids[0]!)!;
    const doomed = atBoundary(b0).map((n) => n.node_id);   // leaf 0, and the node the case above planted there
    write((db) => {
      for (const n of doomed) dropNode(db, n);
      db.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET z = NULL, pruned_ms = ? WHERE blob_id = ?').run(Date.now(), blob0);
      db.prepare("DELETE FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'leaves'").run();
    });
    expect(await derive((k) => k)).toEqual({ derived: 1, waiting: 0, failed: 0 });
    expect(atBoundary(b0)).toEqual([{ node_id: id0, kind: 'raw_leaf', status: 'not-requested', gist: null, topics: null, summary_blob_id: blob0 }]);
    expect(counters(box)['summary_unreadable']).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('the derivation toolkit and the derivation_state helpers (in-process)', () => {
  it("nodeToolkit hands lib the card's own heading rule, fence scanner and token miner", async () => {
    const D = (await import('../../ccd/history/derive.mjs')) as unknown as {
      nodeToolkit(): {
        HEADING_RE: RegExp;
        fencedRanges(t: string): { ranges: Array<[number, number]>; closed: number };
        mineTokens(w: string, re: RegExp | null): Array<{ token: string; tag: string }>;
      };
    };
    const kit = D.nodeToolkit();
    expect(kit.HEADING_RE.flags).toBe('gm');
    expect([...'8. Current Work:\n'.matchAll(new RegExp(kit.HEADING_RE.source, kit.HEADING_RE.flags))].map((m) => m[1])).toEqual(['Current Work']);
    expect(kit.fencedRanges('a\n```\n1. x\n```\nb')).toEqual({ ranges: [[2, 15]], closed: 1 });
    const line = JSON.stringify({ type: 'assistant', message: { content: [{ type: 'tool_use', name: 'Read', input: { file_path: '/home/u/a.ts' } }] } });
    expect(kit.mineTokens(line, null)).toEqual([{ token: '/home/u/a.ts', tag: 'touched' }]);
  });

  it('getStep and setStep: one derivation_state row per (step, version), the cursor kept apart from completed_ms', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-step-');
    createStore(box.home);
    const db = openWriter(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    try {
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 1)).toBeNull();
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setStep(db, 'leaves', 1, '41'); });
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 1)).toEqual({ cursor: '41', completedMs: null });
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setStep(db, 'leaves', 1, '42', 1_700_000_000_000); });
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 1)).toEqual({ cursor: '42', completedMs: 1_700_000_000_000 });
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setStep(db, 'leaves', 1, '43'); });
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 1), 'an omitted completedMs leaves it').toEqual({ cursor: '43', completedMs: 1_700_000_000_000 });
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setStep(db, 'leaves', 1, null, null); });
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 1)).toEqual({ cursor: null, completedMs: null });
      expect(getStep(db, 'leaves', 2), 'another version is another row').toBeNull();
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  });
});
```
