- [ ] **Step 8: Write `ccd/history/derive.mjs`.** Create it with exactly this content:

```js
// ccd/history/derive.mjs: node derivation inside the sweep's tick (spec 2026-10-05 §6.1 span rule and forks,
// §6.2 `nodes` and the producer, §6.3, §7.4; W1-B2 plan Tasks 8 and 9).
//
// L4 delivery. It reads the store and, for one field, the source line a summary row came from, and hands every
// decision to lib.mjs (L1): planSpans, summaryRowFor, pickHoldingCopy, leafReady, decideLeafId, pickReceipt, the
// block parser and the native gist, forkCounts. It imports ../compact-card.mjs for the card's heading rules and
// token miner and injects them into lib as a toolkit (§6.4), so lib.mjs stays node:crypto-only. sweep.mjs imports
// this module, and this module imports nothing of the sweep back: the sweep helpers it needs (admitFile,
// budgetLeft, isBusy) arrive on the ingest context. It reads no environment. An in-process test may set
// ictx.nodeKit to replace the toolkit (history-test-seams-not-env); the sweep never sets it.
//
// Nodes are DERIVED: a rebuild re-derives every leaf with the same id from entries, memberships and boundaries
// (§6.1, §9.14), so nothing here journals. Each leaf commits in its own NORMAL transaction.
import { closeSync, readSync } from 'node:fs';
import { HEADING_RE, fencedRanges, mineTokens } from '../compact-card.mjs';
import {
  LINE_MAX, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, blockFields, blockStatus, capRefs, classifyRef, decideLeafId, directionOfSummaryRow,
  directiveFlag, eofAfterBoundary, forkCounts, ftsTextOf, gistSha, leafId, leafReady, nativeGist, nativeTopics,
  parseBlocks, pickHoldingCopy, pickReceipt, planSpans, producerOfCopy, redactField, selectBlock, summaryParts,
  summaryRowFor,
} from './lib.mjs';
import { bump, getStep, setStep, unbrotli, withTx } from './store.mjs';

/** derivation_state steps this module keeps (§6.2). None is the 'recover' step status reads. */
const LEAF_STEP = 'leaves';                   // version NODE_PARSER_VERSION; cursor: every boundary at or below it has its leaf or a LEAF_CRASHED_STEP marker
const UNSPANNED_STEP = 'rows-unspanned';      // version = transcript_pk; cursor: '<rows_unspanned folded>:<live bytes read then>'
const FORKED_STEP = 'transcript-forked';      // version = transcript_pk; present once transcript_forked is counted
const LEAF_CRASHED_STEP = 'leaf-crashed';     // version = boundary entry_id; cursor: the NODE_PARSER_VERSION it crashed under (RB5)
/** A summary's source line is read in pieces this size, never past LINE_MAX. */
const LINE_PIECE = 64 * 1024;

const DERIVE_STMTS = new WeakMap();
const NODES_FTS_STMTS = new WeakMap();

/** The prepared statements, one set per connection. Each names its columns. A row's copies are found through
 *  (file_id, entry_id), the memberships primary key: v1 has no index on entry_id alone, on purpose. `todo` and
 *  `firstTodo` take (low, LEAF_CRASHED_STEP, String(NODE_PARSER_VERSION)): a boundary with a crash marker at this parser
 *  version is not to do (RB5). */
function stmts(db) {
  let s = DERIVE_STMTS.get(db);
  if (s !== undefined) return s;
  s = {
    todo: db.prepare(`SELECT b.entry_id AS entry_id, e.uuid AS uuid, e.ts_ms AS ts_ms, b.transcript_pk AS transcript_pk,
        t.cc_session_uuid AS cc_uuid
      FROM boundaries b JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = b.entry_id JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = b.transcript_pk
      WHERE b.entry_id > ? AND t.agent_id = ''
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nodes n WHERE n.boundary_entry_id = b.entry_id)
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM derivation_state d WHERE d.step = ? AND d.version = b.entry_id AND d.cursor = ?)
      ORDER BY b.entry_id`),
    firstTodo: db.prepare(`SELECT min(b.entry_id) AS e FROM boundaries b JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = b.transcript_pk
      WHERE b.entry_id > ? AND t.agent_id = ''
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nodes n WHERE n.boundary_entry_id = b.entry_id)
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM derivation_state d WHERE d.step = ? AND d.version = b.entry_id AND d.cursor = ?)`),
    lastBoundary: db.prepare(`SELECT max(b.entry_id) AS e FROM boundaries b JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = b.transcript_pk
      WHERE t.agent_id = ''`),
    epochOf: db.prepare(`SELECT e.session_pk AS session_pk, e.seq AS seq, s.ccrc_id AS ccrc_id
      FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk
      WHERE e.cc_session_uuid = ? AND e.confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL AND s.merged_into IS NULL
      ORDER BY e.session_pk LIMIT 1`),
    files: db.prepare('SELECT file_id, eof_ms, source_key FROM ingest_files WHERE transcript_pk = ? ORDER BY file_id'),
    liveFiles: db.prepare("SELECT file_id FROM ingest_files WHERE transcript_pk = ? AND source_key = '' ORDER BY file_id"),
    member: db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS hit FROM memberships WHERE file_id = ? AND entry_id = ?'),
    copySize: db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM memberships WHERE file_id = ?'),
    /** Distinct rows over a JSON list of file_ids: the union of some copies, counted in SQLite, never in a JS Set. */
    rowsIn: db.prepare('SELECT count(DISTINCT entry_id) AS n FROM memberships WHERE file_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))'),
    /** Main transcripts with two or more live copies, and the bytes read from them: the ones whose fork counts can
     *  change, and the cheap measure of whether they did. */
    forkCandidates: db.prepare(`SELECT f.transcript_pk AS transcript_pk, sum(f.offset) AS bytes
      FROM ingest_files f JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = f.transcript_pk
      WHERE f.source_key = '' AND t.agent_id = ''
      GROUP BY f.transcript_pk HAVING count(*) > 1`),
    copyRows: db.prepare(`SELECT m.line AS line, e.entry_id AS entry_id, e.uuid AS uuid, e.type AS type,
        e.provenance AS provenance, e.is_compact_summary AS is_compact_summary, e.ts_ms AS ts_ms, e.model AS model,
        e.tool_name AS tool_name, e.blob_id AS blob_id, bl.raw_len AS raw_len,
        CASE WHEN b.entry_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_boundary, b.head_uuid AS head_uuid,
        b.anchor_uuid AS anchor_uuid, b.kept_blob_id AS kept_blob_id
      FROM memberships m JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = m.entry_id JOIN blobs bl ON bl.blob_id = e.blob_id
      LEFT JOIN boundaries b ON b.entry_id = e.entry_id
      WHERE m.file_id = ? ORDER BY m.line`),
    memberLine: db.prepare(`SELECT m.line AS line, e.uuid AS uuid FROM memberships m JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = m.entry_id
      WHERE m.file_id = ? AND m.entry_id = ?`),
    blobZ: db.prepare('SELECT z FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?'),
    paths: db.prepare('SELECT path FROM file_paths WHERE file_id = ? ORDER BY path'),
    receipts: db.prepare('SELECT leaf_id, ts_ms FROM steer_receipts WHERE cc_session_uuid = ? ORDER BY ts_ms, event_key'),
    nodeBound: db.prepare('SELECT boundary_entry_id FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
    priorGists: db.prepare('SELECT node_id, gist FROM nodes WHERE session_pk = ? AND depth = 0 AND gist IS NOT NULL'),
    leafBoundaries: db.prepare('SELECT boundary_entry_id FROM nodes WHERE transcript_pk = ? AND depth = 0 AND boundary_entry_id IS NOT NULL'),
    insNode: db.prepare(`INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, gist, topics,
        summary_blob_id, boundary_entry_id, span_start_uuid, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars,
        directive_flag, capped, parser_version, created_ms)
      VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, ?, ?, ?, ?)`),
    insSource: db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_sources (node_id, entry_id, ord) VALUES (?, ?, ?)'),
    insRef: db.prepare(`INSERT INTO node_refs (node_id, kind, value, origin) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
      ON CONFLICT (node_id, kind, value) DO NOTHING`),
    nodeRowid: db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS r FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
  };
  DERIVE_STMTS.set(db, s);
  return s;
}

/** The card's heading rules and token miner, as lib's native gist and refs take them (§6.4). lib never imports
 *  compact-card.mjs; it receives this. */
export function nodeToolkit() {
  return Object.freeze({ HEADING_RE, fencedRanges, mineTokens });
}

/** The two lookups node derivation and the read verbs make by a column no v1 index covers: a boundary's leaf,
 *  and a child's parent. Created by derivation, as the FTS tables are (§9.1), so no schema migration (which every
 *  real store would escalate to snapshot-needs-op, §6.11) is spent on them. ⟦D:history-node-indexes-by-derivation⟧ */
export function ensureNodeIndexes(db) {
  db.exec('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS nodes_boundary ON nodes(boundary_entry_id)');
  db.exec('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS node_children_child ON node_children(child_id)');
}

/** One line from `offset`, without its '\n'; null when no '\n' falls within LINE_MAX bytes or before EOF. */
function readLineAt(fd, offset, size) {
  const parts = [];
  let got = 0;
  for (let pos = offset; pos < size && got < LINE_MAX;) {
    const want = Math.min(LINE_PIECE, size - pos, LINE_MAX - got);
    const buf = Buffer.allocUnsafe(want);
    const n = readSync(fd, buf, 0, want, pos);
    if (n === 0) break;
    const nl = buf.subarray(0, n).indexOf(0x0a);
    if (nl >= 0) {
      parts.push(buf.subarray(0, nl));
      return Buffer.concat(parts).toString('utf8');
    }
    parts.push(buf.subarray(0, n));
    got += n;
    pos += n;
  }
  return null;
}

/** A summary row's `summarizeMetadata.direction`, read back from its own line in the copy that holds it (§7.4
 *  item 8): the store keeps the row's message only. The file is opened through the sweep's own admission
 *  (O_NOFOLLOW, a regular file, realpath under a rostered projects/ root), the line read at its membership's byte
 *  offset, bounded at LINE_MAX, and believed only when its uuid is the row's. Anything else is null: the pair then
 *  follows the text. ⟦D:history-summary-direction-from-source-line⟧ */
export function summaryDirectionOf(db, ictx, summaryEntryId, fileId) {
  const s = stmts(db);
  const m = s.memberLine.get(fileId, summaryEntryId);
  if (m === undefined) return null;
  for (const { path: p } of s.paths.all(fileId)) {
    const home = ictx.homes.find((h) => p.startsWith(`${h}/`));
    if (home === undefined) continue;
    const a = ictx.admitFile(p, home, ictx.homes, ictx.home);
    if (!a.ok) continue;
    try {
      let text;
      try { text = readLineAt(a.fd, Number(m.line), Number(a.st.size)); } catch { return null; }
      if (text === null) return null;
      let row;
      try { row = JSON.parse(text); } catch { return null; }
      return row !== null && typeof row === 'object' && row.uuid === m.uuid ? directionOfSummaryRow(row) : null;
    } finally {
      closeSync(a.fd);
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/** A stored body, parsed; null for a tombstone (z NULL) or a raw-only blob that is not JSON. Its compressed bytes
 *  count against the run's byte budget, as the FTS backfill's do. */
function bodyOf(s, blobId, budget) {
  const r = s.blobZ.get(blobId);
  if (r === undefined || r.z === null) return null;
  budget.bytes += r.z.length;
  try { return JSON.parse(unbrotli(r.z).toString('utf8')); } catch { return null; }
}

function textOf(s, blobId, budget) {
  const body = bodyOf(s, blobId, budget);
  return body === null ? null : ftsTextOf(body, 'entry');
}

/** A boundary's kept list (preservedMessages.allUuids, stored as its own blob by B1's ingest), as a set. */
function keptOf(s, blobId, budget) {
  if (blobId === null) return new Set();
  const v = bodyOf(s, blobId, budget);
  return new Set(Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((u) => typeof u === 'string') : []);
}

function epochFor(s, pass, ccUuid) {
  if (!pass.epochs.has(ccUuid)) pass.epochs.set(ccUuid, s.epochOf.get(ccUuid) ?? null);
  return pass.epochs.get(ccUuid);
}

/** The copy that holds boundary `b` (§6.1 "The copy"), decided by lib's pickHoldingCopy over what this measures:
 *  each of the transcript's files, whether it is live (source_key '') and whether it has the boundary row as a
 *  member. Answers that file's ingest_files row ({ file_id, eof_ms, source_key }), or null. Task 9's fan-in and
 *  Task 21's reparse call it too: `pass` needs only `{ files: Map }`, `b` only `{ entry_id, transcript_pk }`. */
function holdingCopy(s, pass, b) {
  let files = pass.files.get(b.transcript_pk);
  if (files === undefined) {
    files = s.files.all(b.transcript_pk);
    pass.files.set(b.transcript_pk, files);
  }
  const fileId = pickHoldingCopy(files.map((f) => ({
    fileId: Number(f.file_id), live: f.source_key === '', holds: s.member.get(f.file_id, b.entry_id) !== undefined,
  })));
  return fileId === null ? null : files.find((f) => Number(f.file_id) === fileId);
}

/** The newest stamped row's time at or before `uuid` in the copy's file order: the boundary's own time when it has
 *  one. lib's raw-leaf grace reads it (⟦D:history-raw-leaf-grace⟧); null only when no row up to it has a time. */
function stampAtOrBefore(copy, uuid) {
  for (let i = copy.index.get(uuid); i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    const t = copy.rows[i].ts_ms;
    if (t !== null) return Number(t);
  }
  return null;
}

/** One copy's rows in file order, each of its boundaries' summary pick, and lib's spans over them. Kept for the
 *  next boundary of the same copy, the common case: boundaries come in entry order. */
function copyPlan(s, pass, fileId, budget) {
  if (pass.copy !== null && pass.copy.fileId === fileId) return pass.copy;
  const rows = s.copyRows.all(fileId);
  const index = new Map(rows.map((r, i) => [r.uuid, i]));
  const meta = rows.map((r) => ({ uuid: r.uuid, isCompactSummary: r.is_compact_summary === 1, isEcho: r.type === 'user' && r.provenance === 'harness' }));
  const picks = new Map();
  const boundaries = [];
  for (const r of rows) {
    if (r.is_boundary !== 1) continue;
    const pick = summaryRowFor({ boundaryUuid: r.uuid, anchorUuid: r.anchor_uuid, rows: meta });
    picks.set(r.uuid, pick);
    boundaries.push({ uuid: r.uuid, headUuid: r.head_uuid, kept: keptOf(s, r.kept_blob_id, budget), summaryUuid: pick.uuid });
  }
  const plan = planSpans({
    rows: rows.map((r) => ({ uuid: r.uuid, pos: Number(r.line), isBoundary: r.is_boundary === 1, isSummary: r.is_compact_summary === 1 })),
    boundaries,
  });
  const copy = { fileId, rows, index, picks, boundaries, leafOf: new Map(plan.leaves.map((l) => [l.boundaryUuid, l])) };
  pass.copy = copy;
  return copy;
}

function previousBoundary(copy, uuid) {
  const k = copy.boundaries.findIndex((x) => x.uuid === uuid);
  return k > 0 ? copy.boundaries[k - 1] : null;
}

/** The previous boundary's summary text in the same copy (nativeTopics compares against it), or null. */
function prevSummaryText(s, copy, uuid, budget) {
  const prev = previousBoundary(copy, uuid);
  if (prev === null || prev.summaryUuid === null) return null;
  const i = copy.index.get(prev.summaryUuid);
  return i === undefined ? null : textOf(s, copy.rows[i].blob_id, budget);
}

function receiptsOf(s, ccUuid) {
  return s.receipts.all(ccUuid).map((r) => ({ leafId: r.leaf_id, tsMs: r.ts_ms }));
}

/** The receipt window of boundary `b` (§7.4 item 2): after the previous boundary of the same copy, up to this one. */
function receiptWindow(copy, b, id) {
  const prev = previousBoundary(copy, b.uuid);
  return { id, afterMs: prev === null ? null : copy.rows[copy.index.get(prev.uuid)].ts_ms, uptoMs: b.ts_ms };
}

/** The refs mined from a span's tool_use rows (§7.4 item 7, origin `tool_use`): compact-card's miner over the
 *  rows' tool_use blocks, cut to the inputs it reads, each token redacted (a ref is stored and indexed) and
 *  classified. With no graph the miner reads Edit-shaped and Read paths only (§6.4). */
function minedRefs(s, kit, sources, pairIdx, budget) {
  const lines = [];
  for (const r of sources) {
    if (r.type !== 'assistant' || r.tool_name === null) continue;
    const body = bodyOf(s, r.blob_id, budget);
    const uses = (Array.isArray(body) ? body : []).filter((x) => x !== null && typeof x === 'object' && x.type === 'tool_use')
      .map((x) => ({ type: 'tool_use', name: x.name, input: { file_path: x.input?.file_path, notebook_path: x.input?.notebook_path, command: x.input?.command } }));
    if (uses.length > 0) lines.push(JSON.stringify({ type: 'assistant', message: { content: uses } }));
  }
  const out = [];
  for (const { token } of kit.mineTokens(lines.join('\n'), null)) {
    const value = redactField(token, pairIdx);
    const kind = classifyRef(value);
    if (kind !== null) out.push({ kind, value, origin: 'tool_use' });
  }
  return out;
}

/** A node's nodes_fts row, rowid = nodes.rowid (§6.2): its redacted gist, topics and refs. Deleted first, so a
 *  later backfill or re-derivation of the same node never duplicates it. */
function indexNode(db, s, id, gist, topics, refs) {
  let f = NODES_FTS_STMTS.get(db);
  if (f === undefined) {
    f = {
      del: db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?'),
      ins: db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)'),
    };
    NODES_FTS_STMTS.set(db, f);
  }
  const rowid = s.nodeRowid.get(id).r;
  f.del.run(rowid);
  f.ins.run(rowid, gist ?? '', (topics ?? []).join('\n'), refs.map((r) => r.value).join('\n'));
}

/** One leaf's derived fields from its stored summary (§7.4): kind, status and its reason, gist, topics, refs, the
 *  capped and directive flags, the producer and the counters the derivation folds. deriveOne writes them for a new
 *  leaf; W1-B2 Task 21's refreshLeaf rewrites them for an existing one, never its id, span or sources.
 *  - No summary row, or one stored but unreadable (a tombstone, a body that is not JSON): a raw leaf (§6.1), its
 *    summary blob still recorded when the row exists.
 *  - With no steer receipt the status is not-requested, reason no-receipt (§7.4 item 2): `absent` comes only from
 *    blockStatus, on the receipt path. A raw leaf never looks a receipt up.
 *  - A carried copy is counted by blockStatus' own reason. The prior gists are hashed with gistSha, the hash the
 *    block's gist gets, over the stored form; a prior gist of the leaf itself never counts. */
function leafFields(db, ictx, kit, s, copy, b, pick, id, sessionPk, sources, budget) {
  const summaryAt = pick.uuid === null ? undefined : copy.index.get(pick.uuid);
  const summary = summaryAt === undefined ? null : copy.rows[summaryAt];
  const backend = producerOfCopy(copy.rows, summaryAt ?? copy.index.get(b.uuid));
  const counts = [];
  let kind = 'raw_leaf';
  let status = 'not-requested';
  let reason = 'no-receipt';
  let gist = null;
  let topics = null;
  let modelRefs = [];
  let capped = false;
  const text = summary === null ? null : textOf(s, summary.blob_id, budget);
  if (summary === null) {
    counts.push('summary_missing');
  } else if (text === null) {
    counts.push('summary_unreadable');
  } else {
    kind = 'native_leaf';
    topics = [];
    if (summaryParts(text).unclosed) counts.push(`summary_unclosed:${backend}`);
    const receipt = pickReceipt(receiptsOf(s, b.cc_uuid), receiptWindow(copy, b, id));
    let steered = null;
    if (receipt !== null) {
      const blocks = parseBlocks(redactField(text, ictx.pairIdx));
      const sel = selectBlock({ blocks, kind: 'leaf', computedId: id, generic: receipt.leafId === '' });
      const prior = new Set(s.priorGists.all(sessionPk).filter((r) => r.node_id !== id).map((r) => gistSha(r.gist)));
      const verdict = blockStatus({ receipt: true, block: sel.block, idMismatch: sel.idMismatch, priorGistShas: prior });
      status = verdict.status;
      reason = verdict.reason;
      if (sel.idMismatch) counts.push('id_mismatch');
      if (sel.block === null && blocks.some((x) => x.inAnalysis)) counts.push(`analysis_only:${backend}`);
      if (verdict.reason === 'carried-copy') counts.push('carried_copies');
      if (status === 'ok' || status === 'degraded') steered = blockFields(sel.block);
    }
    if (steered !== null) {
      kind = 'steered_leaf';
      gist = steered.gist;
      topics = steered.topics;
      modelRefs = steered.refs;
      capped = steered.capped;
    } else {
      const direction = summaryDirectionOf(db, ictx, summary.entry_id, copy.fileId);
      const g = nativeGist({ text, direction }, kit, ictx.pairIdx);
      const t = nativeTopics({ text, prevText: prevSummaryText(s, copy, b.uuid, budget) }, kit, ictx.pairIdx);
      gist = g.gist;
      topics = t.topics;
      capped = g.capped || t.capped;
    }
  }
  const refs = capRefs([...modelRefs, ...minedRefs(s, kit, sources, ictx.pairIdx, budget)]);
  const flag = gist !== null && directiveFlag([gist, ...(topics ?? [])].join('\n'));
  return { summary, backend, counts, kind, status, reason, gist, topics, refs, capped, flag, crashed: false };
}

/** A leaf whose parser threw (RB5): written under its own id with its span and sources, kind raw_leaf, status
 *  parse-failed, no gist, topics or refs, and its summary row's blob still recorded, so reparse (Task 21) re-derives
 *  it in place. Counted parser_crash once and no compliance outcome. ⟦D:history-parser-crash-recorded⟧ */
function parseFailedFields(copy, pick) {
  const at = pick.uuid === null ? undefined : copy.index.get(pick.uuid);
  return {
    summary: at === undefined ? null : copy.rows[at], backend: null, counts: ['parser_crash'], kind: 'raw_leaf',
    status: 'parse-failed', reason: null, gist: null, topics: null, refs: { refs: [], capped: false }, capped: false,
    flag: false, crashed: true,
  };
}

/** One boundary's leaf (§6.1, §7.4), or why it waits: no confirmed epoch yet (out of every scope), no holding
 *  copy, or not ready (lib leafReady: a raw leaf is never written while it could still be native). The boundary's
 *  time for the raw-leaf grace is its own, or the newest stamped row before it in the holding copy. */
function deriveOne(db, ictx, kit, s, pass, b, budget) {
  const ep = epochFor(s, pass, b.cc_uuid);
  if (ep === null) return 'waiting';
  const holding = holdingCopy(s, pass, b);
  if (holding === null) return 'waiting';
  const copy = copyPlan(s, pass, holding.file_id, budget);
  const leaf = copy.leafOf.get(b.uuid);
  if (leaf === undefined) return 'waiting';
  const pick = copy.picks.get(b.uuid);
  const ready = leafReady({
    summaryStored: pick.uuid !== null,
    fileAtEofAfterBoundary: eofAfterBoundary({ eofMs: holding.eof_ms, boundaryTsMs: stampAtOrBefore(copy, b.uuid) }),
  });
  if (!ready) return 'waiting';
  const plain = leafId(ep.ccrc_id, b.cc_uuid, leaf.spanStartUuid);
  const bound = s.nodeBound.get(plain);
  const plainBoundOther = bound !== undefined && bound.boundary_entry_id !== b.entry_id;
  const { id, forked } = decideLeafId({ ccrcId: ep.ccrc_id, ccUuid: b.cc_uuid, spanStartUuid: leaf.spanStartUuid, boundaryUuid: b.uuid, plainBoundOther });
  const sources = leaf.sources.map((u) => copy.rows[copy.index.get(u)]);
  let f;
  try {
    f = leafFields(db, ictx, kit, s, copy, b, pick, id, ep.session_pk, sources, budget);
  } catch (e) {
    if (ictx.isBusy(e)) throw e;
    // RB5: the parser threw (a bug). The leaf is written anyway, parse-failed, and only reparse re-derives it.
    f = parseFailedFields(copy, pick);
  }
  const { summary, counts, kind, status, reason, gist, topics, refs, capped, flag, backend, crashed } = f;
  let earliest = null;
  let latest = null;
  let srcChars = 0;
  for (const r of sources) {
    if (r.ts_ms !== null && (earliest === null || r.ts_ms < earliest)) earliest = r.ts_ms;
    if (r.ts_ms !== null && (latest === null || r.ts_ms > latest)) latest = r.ts_ms;
    srcChars += Number(r.raw_len);
  }
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    s.insNode.run(id, ep.session_pk, ep.seq, b.transcript_pk, kind, status, gist,
      topics === null ? null : JSON.stringify(topics), summary === null ? null : summary.blob_id,
      b.entry_id, leaf.spanStartUuid, earliest, latest, srcChars, flag ? 1 : 0, capped || refs.capped ? 1 : 0,
      NODE_PARSER_VERSION, ictx.nowMs);
    sources.forEach((r, ord) => { s.insSource.run(id, r.entry_id, ord); });
    for (const r of refs.refs) s.insRef.run(id, r.kind, r.value, r.origin);
    if (ictx.fts === true) indexNode(db, s, id, gist, topics, refs.refs);
    if (forked) bump(db, 'leaf_id_forked');
    if (leaf.headMissing) bump(db, 'head_missing');
    if (summary !== null && pick.anchorIsBoundary) bump(db, 'anchor_is_boundary');
    for (const c of counts) bump(db, c);
    // §7.4 item 10: compliance by status and by reason, each by producer. A parser crash is no outcome.
    if (!crashed) {
      bump(db, `leaf_status:${status}:${backend}`);
      if (reason !== null) bump(db, `leaf_reason:${reason}:${backend}`);
    }
  });
  return 'derived';
}

/** The rows-unspanned cursor: '<rows_unspanned already folded>:<live bytes read when folded>'. No row, or one this
 *  build cannot read, is "never folded". */
function foldedOf(step) {
  const m = step === null || step.cursor === null ? null : /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*):(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/.exec(step.cursor);
  return m === null ? { unspanned: 0, bytes: null } : { unspanned: Number(m[1]), bytes: Number(m[2]) };
}

/** A main transcript's fork counters (§6.1), from lib's forkCounts over what this measures on its LIVE copies:
 *  - rows_unspanned: rows no holding copy has (they join no leaf), folded as the increase over the count already
 *    recorded;
 *  - transcript_forked: once, when it has two or more live copies and none holds every row.
 *  The holding copy of each leaf's boundary is lib's pickHoldingCopy among the live copies. `bytes` is the live
 *  copies' bytes read now, kept beside the folded count so the next tick knows whether to recount. */
function recountTranscript(db, s, transcriptPk, nowMs, bytes) {
  const live = s.liveFiles.all(transcriptPk).map((f) => Number(f.file_id));
  const holding = new Set();
  for (const { boundary_entry_id: e } of s.leafBoundaries.all(transcriptPk)) {
    const f = pickHoldingCopy(live.map((id) => ({ fileId: id, live: true, holds: s.member.get(id, e) !== undefined })));
    if (f !== null) holding.add(f);
  }
  const { unspanned, forked } = forkCounts({
    liveSizes: live.map((f) => Number(s.copySize.get(f).n)),
    unionSize: Number(s.rowsIn.get(JSON.stringify(live)).n),
    coveredSize: Number(s.rowsIn.get(JSON.stringify([...holding])).n),
    holdingCopies: holding.size,
  });
  const prev = foldedOf(getStep(db, UNSPANNED_STEP, transcriptPk));
  const marked = getStep(db, FORKED_STEP, transcriptPk) !== null;
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    if (unspanned > prev.unspanned) bump(db, 'rows_unspanned', unspanned - prev.unspanned);
    setStep(db, UNSPANNED_STEP, transcriptPk, `${unspanned}:${bytes}`);
    if (forked && !marked) { bump(db, 'transcript_forked'); setStep(db, FORKED_STEP, transcriptPk, '1', nowMs); }
  });
}

/** Every boundary without its leaf, in entry order, within the run's budget (§9.2 step 6); then the fork counts
 *  of every main transcript with two or more live copies whose bytes read changed, or which gained a leaf.
 *  - A throw inside the parser is deriveOne's: the leaf is written parse-failed (RB5).
 *  - A throw before a leaf can be written (span planning, an insert refused) counts parser_crash once and leaves a
 *    ('leaf-crashed', entry_id) marker at this NODE_PARSER_VERSION, in one transaction: the todo queries skip the
 *    boundary, so the cursor moves past it and no tick parses it again. Reparse clears the markers (Task 21); a new
 *    NODE_PARSER_VERSION retries them. ⟦D:history-parser-crash-recorded⟧
 *  - A busy store ends the tick, as ingest's does.
 *  The cursor ('leaves', NODE_PARSER_VERSION) is the low-water mark: every boundary at or below it has its leaf or a
 *  crash marker, and a boundary that waits holds it. */
export function deriveLeaves(db, ictx, budget) {
  ensureNodeIndexes(db);
  const s = stmts(db);
  const kit = ictx.nodeKit ?? nodeToolkit();
  const crashedAt = String(NODE_PARSER_VERSION);
  const low = Number(getStep(db, LEAF_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION)?.cursor ?? 0);
  const pass = { copy: null, epochs: new Map(), files: new Map() };
  const touched = new Set();
  let derived = 0;
  let waiting = 0;
  let failed = 0;
  for (const b of s.todo.all(low, LEAF_CRASHED_STEP, crashedAt)) {
    if (!ictx.budgetLeft(budget)) break;
    let r;
    try {
      r = deriveOne(db, ictx, kit, s, pass, b, budget);
    } catch (e) {
      if (ictx.isBusy(e)) throw e;
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
        bump(db, 'parser_crash');
        setStep(db, LEAF_CRASHED_STEP, Number(b.entry_id), crashedAt, ictx.nowMs);
      });
      r = 'failed';
    }
    if (r === 'derived') {
      derived += 1;
      touched.add(Number(b.transcript_pk));
    } else if (r === 'failed') {
      failed += 1;
    } else {
      waiting += 1;
    }
  }
  for (const c of s.forkCandidates.all()) {
    if (!ictx.budgetLeft(budget)) break;
    const pk = Number(c.transcript_pk);
    const bytes = Number(c.bytes);
    if (touched.has(pk) || foldedOf(getStep(db, UNSPANNED_STEP, pk)).bytes !== bytes) recountTranscript(db, s, pk, ictx.nowMs, bytes);
  }
  const first = s.firstTodo.get(low, LEAF_CRASHED_STEP, crashedAt).e;
  const top = first === null ? Number(s.lastBoundary.get().e ?? low) : Number(first) - 1;
  if (top > low) withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setStep(db, LEAF_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, String(top)); });
  return { derived, waiting, failed };
}

/** Derive, nodes (§9.2 step 6, §6.3). Task 9 adds the parents and the nodes_fts backfill after the leaves. */
export function deriveNodes(db, ictx, budget) {
  deriveLeaves(db, ictx, budget);
}
```

  - The `\n` in comments are two-character escapes in source, never raw control bytes. `derive.mjs` spells no dedupe key of its own: `capRefs` is the one (kind, value) rule.
  - `derive.mjs` reads no `process.env` and declares none of the O14 vocabularies, so B1's single-definition scans over `ccd/history/*.mjs` hold. Its status words (`not-requested`, `parse-failed`) are `PARSE_STATUS` words used, never a list declared.
  - `json_each` is SQLite's built-in JSON table function. `rowsIn`, `forkCandidates` and the todo queries' marker clause were run on `node:sqlite` under Node 24 at plan time; `history-derive.test.ts` is on the node-floor leg (Step 6), so CI re-measures them on 22.16.0 (RB9). `rowsIn` counts a union of copies in SQLite rather than in a JavaScript Set, so a recount of a large forked transcript costs one indexed scan per copy list.

- [ ] **Step 12: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's, byte for byte, written again here so this task stands alone. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8' });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the mutant applier (scratch, never committed).**

Every mutation step in Tasks 9–11 uses this script. It saves the clean file aside, applies one mutant, and refuses to run while an earlier mutant is still unrestored. Create it from the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <<'EOF'
// mut-after.mjs: apply ONE mutant for a mutation pin (W1-B2 plan, Tasks 9-11), in place.
// usage: node .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]
// For each pair, replace the FIRST occurrence of <needle> that follows the first occurrence of <anchor>.
// - The clean file is saved first to .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig.
// - The script exits 1 and writes nothing when the anchor or any needle is missing, so a mutant never applies half.
// - It also exits 1 while an earlier .orig is still there (an unrestored mutant).
// Restore: mv .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig <file>
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
const [file, anchor, ...pairs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (file === undefined || anchor === undefined || pairs.length === 0 || pairs.length % 2 !== 0) {
  console.error('usage: node mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]');
  process.exit(2);
}
const scratch = join('.superpowers', 'sdd', 'history-w1-b2', 'scratch');
mkdirSync(scratch, { recursive: true });
const orig = join(scratch, `${basename(file)}.orig`);
if (existsSync(orig)) {
  console.error(`mut-after: ${orig} exists: restore the earlier mutant first (mv ${orig} ${file})`);
  process.exit(1);
}
let text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const at = text.indexOf(anchor);
if (at < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: anchor not found in ${file}: ${anchor}`); process.exit(1); }
for (let i = 0; i < pairs.length; i += 2) {
  const k = text.indexOf(pairs[i], at);
  if (k < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: needle not found after the anchor: ${pairs[i]}`); process.exit(1); }
  text = text.slice(0, k) + pairs[i + 1] + text.slice(k + pairs[i].length);
}
copyFileSync(file, orig);
writeFileSync(file, text);
console.log(`mut-after: mutated ${file}; restore with: mv ${orig} ${file}`);
EOF
git check-ignore -q .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs && echo ignored
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the lineage in store.mjs.** Append this section to the END of `ccd/history/store.mjs`, after B1's `createFtsTables`:

```js
// ── Lineage: the range CTE and the two edge lookups (spec §6.3; W1-B2 Task 9) ────────────────────────────
// The edge names are directional (§6.3):
//   - node_sources is leaf → its entries, ordered;
//   - node_children is parent → the nodes it condenses, ordered.
// The lineage walks DOWN, from a node to what it condenses and then to those nodes' source entries. The
// upstream subtree CTE walks toward a summary's CONSUMERS with UNION ALL (summary-store.ts:780-822); it is not
// ported (§11, refuted candidate 4). UNION, not UNION ALL, so a cycle in node_children ends the walk.
// derived from lossless-claw src/store/summary-store.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
// From getSummaryMessageSeqRange, upstream lines 595-621. SQLite keeps a CROSS JOIN's order, so this visits
// the lineage before it looks up any link. A reordered join could scan every family's links once per node.
const LINEAGE_SQL = `WITH RECURSIVE source_nodes(node_id) AS (
  SELECT ?
  UNION
  SELECT nc.child_id
  FROM node_children nc
  JOIN source_nodes s ON s.node_id = nc.node_id
)
SELECT ns.node_id AS node_id, ns.entry_id AS entry_id, ns.ord AS ord, e.ts_ms AS ts_ms
FROM source_nodes s
CROSS JOIN node_sources ns ON ns.node_id = s.node_id
CROSS JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = ns.entry_id
ORDER BY ns.node_id, ns.ord`;

/** Every source entry under `nodeId`: a leaf's own, or every leaf's below a parent. Rows come grouped by leaf id
 *  and in each leaf's `ord`. Ordering the leaves themselves (by `boundaries.ord`) is the caller's job. */
export function lineageEntries(db, nodeId) {
  return db.prepare(LINEAGE_SQL).all(nodeId).map((r) => ({
    nodeId: r.node_id, entryId: Number(r.entry_id), ord: Number(r.ord), tsMs: r.ts_ms === null ? null : Number(r.ts_ms),
  }));
}

/** What `nodeId` condenses, in order (empty for a leaf). */
export function childrenOf(db, nodeId) {
  return db.prepare('SELECT child_id, ord FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord').all(nodeId)
    .map((r) => ({ childId: r.child_id, ord: Number(r.ord) }));
}

/** The node that condenses `nodeId`, or null. Fan-in gives a node one parent; ORDER BY keeps the answer
 *  deterministic over a hand-damaged table. */
export function parentOf(db, nodeId) {
  const r = db.prepare('SELECT node_id FROM node_children WHERE child_id = ? ORDER BY node_id LIMIT 1').get(nodeId);
  return r === undefined ? null : r.node_id;
}
```

```ts
 *  which groups per holding copy, finds each boundary's copy the way Task 8's holdingCopy does. By default one
 *  copy holds every boundary. */
function epochFixture9(prefix: string, n: number, missing: ReadonlySet<number>,
  copies = 1, holders: (k: number) => readonly number[] = () => [1]): { db: Db9; leafIds: string[] } {
  const home = tmp9.mkTmp(prefix);
  store9.createStore(home);
  const db = store9.openWriter(lib9.historyPaths(home).dbFile);
  const leafIds: string[] = [];
  db.exec('BEGIN');
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (1, ?, '', 'demo', 1)").run(ID9);
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO epochs (session_pk, seq, cc_session_uuid, cause, declared_by, confirmed_ms) VALUES (1, 1, ?, 'startup', 'hook', 1)").run(E9);
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO transcripts (transcript_pk, cc_session_uuid) VALUES (1, ?)').run(E9);
  const file = db.prepare("INSERT INTO ingest_files (file_id, dev, ino, transcript_pk, status, parser_version) VALUES (?, 1, ?, 1, 'live', 1)");
  for (let f = 1; f <= copies; f += 1) file.run(f, 9000 + f);
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO blobs (blob_id, sha256, codec, z, raw_len) VALUES (1, ?, 'br5', ?, 1)").run(Buffer.alloc(32, 9), Buffer.from([0]));
  const ent = db.prepare("INSERT INTO entries (entry_id, uuid, transcript_pk, type, subtype, provenance, prov_version, struct_rank_ns, struct_file_id, blob_id, ts_ms) VALUES (?, ?, 1, 'system', 'compact_boundary', 'harness', 1, 0, 0, 1, ?)");
  const bnd = db.prepare('INSERT INTO boundaries (entry_id, transcript_pk, ord) VALUES (?, 1, ?)');
  const member = db.prepare('INSERT INTO memberships (file_id, entry_id, line) VALUES (?, ?, ?)');
  for (let k = 1; k <= n; k += 1) {
    ent.run(k, uid9('d9e00000', k), 1000 * k);
    bnd.run(k, k);
    for (const f of holders(k)) member.run(f, k, k);
    const id = lib9.leafId(ID9, E9, `span-${k}`);
    leafIds.push(id);
    if (!missing.has(k)) addLeaf9(db, k, id);
  }
  db.exec('COMMIT');
  return { db, leafIds };
}
function addLeaf9(db: Db9, k: number, id: string): void {
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, gist, topics, boundary_entry_id, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, 1, 1, 1, 'native_leaf', 0, 'not-requested', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 100, 0, 0, 1, 1)")
    .run(id, `Leaf ${k} did part ${k}. It also did more.`, JSON.stringify([`topic ${k}`]), k, 1000 * k, 1000 * k + 500);
}
interface Parent9 { node_id: string; kind: string; status: string; gist: string | null; topics: string | null; earliest_ms: number; latest_ms: number; desc_count: number }
const parents9 = (db: Db9, depth: number): Parent9[] =>
  (db.prepare('SELECT node_id, kind, status, gist, topics, earliest_ms, latest_ms, desc_count FROM nodes WHERE depth = ? ORDER BY earliest_ms').all(depth) as unknown as Parent9[]).map((r) => ({ ...r }));
const children9 = (db: Db9, id: string): string[] =>
  (db.prepare('SELECT child_id FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord').all(id) as { child_id: string }[]).map((r) => r.child_id);

/** `n` manual compactions in one transcript. Each cycle is a user turn, an answer, a kept follow-up, the
 *  boundary (head = the follow-up, kept = [the follow-up]) and the summary row right after it (§6.1's manual
 *  shape: the anchor is the summary, one row past the boundary). Row uuids carry the 8-hex prefix `p`, so two
 *  transcripts never share one. */
function cycles9(p: string, sid: string, n: number, t0: number): fx9.Row[] {
  const rows: fx9.Row[] = [];
  let k = 0;
  let t = t0;
  const ts = (): string => new Date((t += 1000)).toISOString();
  for (let c = 1; c <= n; c += 1) {
    const u = uid9(p, ++k); const a = uid9(p, ++k); const x = uid9(p, ++k); const b = uid9(p, ++k); const s = uid9(p, ++k);
    rows.push(fx9.userRow({ uuid: u, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `fixture request ${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.assistantRow({ uuid: a, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `Fixture answer ${c}. More detail follows.`, requestId: `req_${p}_${c}`, msgId: `msg_${p}_${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.userRow({ uuid: x, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `fixture follow-up ${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.boundaryRow({ uuid: b, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, trigger: 'manual', headUuid: x, anchorUuid: s, tailUuid: x, allUuids: [x] }));
    rows.push(fx9.summaryRow({ uuid: s, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: [
      'This session is being continued from a previous conversation. The summary below covers the earlier portion.',
      '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', `   Fixture request ${c}.`,
      '8. Current Work:', `   Wrote part ${c} of the fixture.`,
      '9. Optional Next Step:', `   Continue with part ${c + 1}.`, '</summary>',
    ].join('\n') }));
  }
  return rows;
}

v9.describe('DM26: parents by fan-in, never across an epoch, only over final leaves (W1-B2 Task 9)', () => {
  v9.it('a boundary whose leaf is not derived yet stops the group: 9 boundaries, leaf 4 missing, no parent; leaf 4 derived, one parent over leaves 1-8', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-dm26-nf-', 9, new Set([4]));
    const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 };
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1), 'slot 4 is not final: slots 1-3 and 5-9 are never one group').toEqual([]);
      addLeaf9(fx.db, 4, fx.leafIds[3]!);
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      const p = parents9(fx.db, 1);
      v9.expect(p).toHaveLength(1);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.node_id, 'parentId over the children in boundary order').toBe(lib9.parentId(fx.leafIds.slice(0, 8)));
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, p[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(fx.leafIds.slice(0, 8));
      v9.expect([p[0]!.kind, p[0]!.status]).toEqual(['condensed', 'ok']);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.gist).toContain('Leaf 1 did part 1');
      v9.expect(p[0]!.gist).toContain('Leaf 8 did part 8');
      v9.expect([p[0]!.earliest_ms, p[0]!.latest_ms]).toEqual([1000, 8500]);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.desc_count).toBe(8);
      v9.expect(JSON.parse(p[0]!.topics ?? '[]')).toEqual(v9.expect.arrayContaining(['topic 1', 'topic 8']));
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1), 'a rerun mints nothing again').toHaveLength(1);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }
  });

  v9.it('fan-in is 4 per level above the leaves: 32 leaves give four depth-1 parents and one depth-2 parent over them, in order', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-dm26-d2-', 32, new Set());
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 }, s.newBudget());
      const level1 = [0, 8, 16, 24].map((i) => lib9.parentId(fx.leafIds.slice(i, i + 8)));
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1).map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual(level1);
      const top = parents9(fx.db, 2);
      v9.expect(top.map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual([lib9.parentId(level1)]);
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, top[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(level1);
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 3)).toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }
  });

  v9.it('a parent never mixes forks: two copies share a head, fork, and interleave in ord; each copy gets its own parent, and a leaf not derived in one stops only that copy (RB4)', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    // Boundaries 1-2: the shared head, in both copies, so held by file 1 (both are live: the smaller file_id).
    // Then the forks arrive interleaved: odd k from 3 to 17 is copy A's (file 1 only), even k from 4 to 18 copy
    // B's (file 2 only). boundaries.ord is per transcript, so the two forks' ords interleave as they do on a box.
    const holders = (k: number): number[] => (k <= 2 ? [1, 2] : k % 2 === 1 ? [1] : [2]);
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-dm26-fork-', 18, new Set([7]), 2, holders);
    const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 };
    const leaf = (k: number): string => fx.leafIds[k - 1]!;
    const copyA = [1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13].map(leaf);
    const copyB = [4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18].map(leaf);
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1).map((p) => p.node_id), 'leaf 7 (copy A) is not derived yet: copy B still gets its parent')
        .toEqual([lib9.parentId(copyB)]);
      addLeaf9(fx.db, 7, leaf(7));
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      const made = parents9(fx.db, 1).map((p) => p.node_id).sort();
      v9.expect(made).toEqual([lib9.parentId(copyA), lib9.parentId(copyB)].sort());
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, lib9.parentId(copyA)), 'the head and copy A\'s first six, in ord').toEqual(copyA);
      // Every parent's children sit in one holding copy: the smallest live file_id with the boundary as a member.
      const holderOf = (id: string): number => {
        const b = (fx.db.prepare('SELECT boundary_entry_id AS e FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?').get(id) as { e: number }).e;
        return Number((fx.db.prepare('SELECT min(file_id) AS f FROM memberships WHERE entry_id = ?').get(b) as { f: number }).f);
      };
      for (const p of made) v9.expect(new Set(children9(fx.db, p).map(holderOf)).size, `${p}: one holding copy`).toBe(1);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }
  });

  v9.it('rerollParents re-rolls every parent above a changed leaf from its children as stored now, ids kept (Tasks 21 and 29 call it)', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();

    try {

      const ids = (): string[] => [...parents9(fx.db, 1), ...parents9(fx.db, 2)].map((p) => p.node_id);
      const before = ids();
      fx.db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run('Leaf 3 was re-derived. Its tail is dropped.', fx.leafIds[2]!);
      v9.expect(d.rerollParents(fx.db, ictx, [fx.leafIds[2]!]), 'its depth-1 parent, then the depth-2 parent above that').toBe(2);
      const p1 = parents9(fx.db, 1);

      v9.expect(p1[1]!.gist, 'a parent above no changed leaf is untouched').toContain('Leaf 9 did part 9.');
      v9.expect(ids(), 'no parent id changes').toEqual(before);
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, p1[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(fx.leafIds.slice(0, 8));
    } finally {

    }

  v9.it('through real ticks: 8 leaves in one epoch make one parent; 8 leaves spanning a /clear make none, and the late-confirmed /clear epoch has no node before it is confirmed', () => {
    const one = h9.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm26-one-');
    const acct = Object.keys(one.accountHome)[0]!;
    const T = 'd26a0000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
    h9.plantSession(one, ID9, { uuid: T, project: 'demo' });
    h9.plantTranscript(one, acct, '-home-u-tree-demo', T, cycles9('d26a1a00', T, 8, T0_9));
    h9.spoolLine(one, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T, src: 'startup', reg: T });
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(one).code).toBe(0);
    const db1 = h9.openStoreRO(one);
    try {
      const leaves = (db1.prepare('SELECT n.node_id AS id FROM nodes n JOIN boundaries b ON b.entry_id = n.boundary_entry_id WHERE n.depth = 0 ORDER BY b.ord').all() as { id: string }[]).map((r) => r.id);
      v9.expect(leaves).toHaveLength(8);
      v9.expect(parents9(db1, 1).map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual([lib9.parentId(leaves)]);
    } finally {
      db1.close();
    }

    const two = h9.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm26-clear-');
    const acct2 = Object.keys(two.accountHome)[0]!;
    const T1 = 'd26c1000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
    const T2 = 'd26c2000-2222-4222-8222-222222222222';
    // B1 renames a spool line at the END of a tick and drains it at the NEXT (sweep.mjs's listDraining loop, then
    // renameAndObserve), and the first tick also runs the registry scan, which books a planted .uuid as an 'import'
    // epoch. So the box is primed first: that tick spends the scan, and epoch 1 is the hook's 'startup'.
    v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);   // prime: spends the first tick's registry scan, so epoch 1 is the hook's 'startup'
    h9.plantSession(two, ID9, { uuid: T1, project: 'demo' });
    h9.plantTranscript(two, acct2, '-home-u-tree-demo', T1, cycles9('d26c1a00', T1, 4, T0_9));
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T1, src: 'startup', reg: T1 });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);
    // The /clear line drains while .uuid still names T1 and no .workdir is set: B1 chains its epoch UNCONFIRMED
    // (SE5; decideEpochLine, then confirmClear waits), out of every scope. .uuid names T2 only after that tick, so
    // a LATER tick confirms it ('later-tick'), and only then do its leaves appear, in that epoch (review focus 4).
    h9.plantTranscript(two, acct2, '-home-u-tree-demo', T2, cycles9('d26c2a00', T2, 4, T0_9 + 3_600_000));
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T2, src: 'clear' });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);   // tick N renames the /clear line, tick N+1 drains it and chains the unconfirmed epoch
    const early = h9.openStoreRO(two);
    try {
      const ep = early.prepare('SELECT seq, confirmed_ms FROM epochs ORDER BY seq').all() as { seq: number; confirmed_ms: number | null }[];
      v9.expect(ep.map((e) => [e.seq, e.confirmed_ms !== null]), 'the /clear epoch waits unconfirmed').toEqual([[1, true], [2, false]]);
      v9.expect((early.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE epoch_seq = 2').get() as { n: number }).n, 'no node in an unconfirmed epoch').toBe(0);
    } finally {
      early.close();
    }
    h9.plantSession(two, ID9, { uuid: T2 });
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: ID9 });   // a renamed line for the id hints its confirmed epochs and .uuid at ingest; without one, T2 waits for the 30-minute scan
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);
    const db2 = h9.openStoreRO(two);
    try {
      const epochs = (db2.prepare('SELECT seq, cause, confirmed_ms FROM epochs ORDER BY seq').all() as { seq: number; cause: string; confirmed_ms: number | null }[]);
      v9.expect(epochs.map((e) => [e.seq, e.cause, e.confirmed_ms !== null])).toEqual([[1, 'startup', true], [2, 'clear', true]]);
      v9.expect((db2.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE depth = 0').get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(8);
      v9.expect((db2.prepare('SELECT epoch_seq AS e, count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE depth = 0 GROUP BY epoch_seq ORDER BY epoch_seq').all() as { e: number; n: number }[])
        .map((r) => [r.e, r.n]), 'the late-confirmed epoch\'s leaves sit in it').toEqual([[1, 4], [2, 4]]);
      v9.expect(parents9(db2, 1), 'four leaves in each epoch: never one group across the /clear').toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      db2.close();
    }
  }, 120_000);
});

      v9.expect(d.indexNodesFts(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget())).toBe(2);

    const s = await sweep9();

    store9.createStore(home);
    const db = store9.openWriter(lib9.historyPaths(home).dbFile);
    const U = ['e1000000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111', 'e2000000-2222-4222-8222-222222222222',
      'e3000000-3333-4333-8333-333333333333', 'e4000000-4444-4444-8444-444444444444'];
    const G = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0123456789ab';
    try {
      db.exec('BEGIN');
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (1, ?, '', 'demo', 1)").run(ID9);
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (2, ?, ?, 'demo', 2)").run(ID9, G);
      U.forEach((u, i) => { db.prepare('INSERT INTO transcripts (transcript_pk, cc_session_uuid) VALUES (?, ?)').run(i + 1, u); });
      const ep = db.prepare("INSERT INTO epochs (session_pk, seq, cc_session_uuid, cause, declared_by, confirmed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'startup', 'hook', 1)");
      ep.run(1, 1, U[0]!); ep.run(1, 2, U[1]!); ep.run(2, 1, U[2]!);
      const node = db.prepare("INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'ok', 1, 1)");
      node.run('L1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 1, 'native_leaf', 0);
      node.run('N1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 1, 'condensed', 1);
      node.run('L2aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 2, 2, 'native_leaf', 0);

      node.run('L4aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 4, 'native_leaf', 0);
      db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_children (node_id, child_id, ord) VALUES (?, ?, 0)').run('N1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 'L1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa');
      s.mergeFamily(db, 1, 2);
      db.exec('COMMIT');
      const where = (id: string): number[] => {
        const r = db.prepare('SELECT session_pk, epoch_seq FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?').get(id) as { session_pk: number; epoch_seq: number };
        return [r.session_pk, r.epoch_seq];
      };
      v9.expect((db.prepare('SELECT seq, cc_session_uuid FROM epochs WHERE session_pk = 2 ORDER BY seq').all() as { seq: number; cc_session_uuid: string }[])
        .map((e) => [e.seq, e.cc_session_uuid])).toEqual([[1, U[0]], [2, U[1]], [3, U[2]]]);
      v9.expect(where('L1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa'), 'a leaf moves with its epoch').toEqual([2, 1]);

      v9.expect(where('L4aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa'), 'no epoch holds its transcript: it stays').toEqual([1, 1]);
      v9.expect((db.prepare("SELECT n FROM counters WHERE name = 'nodes_unrepointed'").get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
    } finally {
      db.close();
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Implement parents and the backfill in derive.mjs.**

Merge these names into derive.mjs's existing import clauses, adding only those absent (Task 8 already imports some):
- from `'./lib.mjs'`: `parentId, planFanIn, parentRollup, FAN_IN, directiveFlag, redactField, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, withinBudget`;
- from `'./store.mjs'`: `withTx, getStep, setStep, parentOf`.

Then append this section to the END of `ccd/history/derive.mjs`:

```js
// ── Parents: fan-in per epoch, deterministic rollups (spec §6.3; W1-B2 Task 9) ───────────────────────────
//
// Which leaves group:
//   - 8 leaves make a depth-1 parent, and 4 nodes per level above (FAN_IN; lib's planFanIn decides each group);
//   - never across a /clear epoch: an epoch's slots are its own main transcript's boundaries, in `ord`;
//   - never across two forks: those slots are split per HOLDING COPY, the transcript file Task 8's holdingCopy
//     picks for each boundary, and fan-in runs per copy, so a parent's children share one copy (the
//     coordinator's ruling RB4; slug history-span-per-boundary-copy, extended to fan-in);
//   - only over FINAL leaves: a boundary whose leaf is not derived yet is a null slot, and a null slot stops the
//     group of its own copy, so a parent never skips a span to fill itself.
// What a parent is:
//   - its id is parentId(child ids, in order), so a retry, a reparse or a rebuild re-derives the same id (§6.1);
//   - its gist, topics, refs, time range and counts come from lib's parentRollup over the children's stored
//     fields. No model summarises anything (§6.3: "always deterministic and rebuildable").
// Writes: each parent, its node_children and node_refs rows, and (when the FTS tables exist) its nodes_fts row
// commit in ONE NORMAL transaction. A node is derived and rebuildable, never journaled (§9.14).
// Cursor (slug history-parents-cursor-by-rowid, NEW): ('parents', NODE_PARSER_VERSION) holds the highest
// nodes.rowid already considered. Only an epoch that gained a node since then is walked again; a budget that
// ends mid-walk leaves the cursor where it was, so the next tick walks those epochs again.

const PARENTS_STEP = 'parents';
/** The nodes_fts backfill's derivation step. Exported: doctor --repair (W1-B2 Task 23) resets its cursor when it
 *  recreates nodes_fts. */
export const NODES_FTS_STEP = 'nodes-fts';
const NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION = 1;
/** The nodes_fts backfill's page: one NORMAL transaction each. */
const NODES_FTS_BATCH = 256;
/** A walk never climbs past this depth. 4^31 leaves is no store this code will meet; the bound only keeps a
 *  hand-damaged node_children table from looping. */
const MAX_FAN_DEPTH = 32;

function parentsBudgetLeft(budget) {
  return withinBudget({ elapsedMs: budget.now() - budget.startMs, bytes: budget.bytes, maxMs: budget.maxMs, maxBytes: budget.maxBytes });
}

/** A node's `topics` column as a list. A parent writes a JSON array; a column that is not one reads as one
 *  topic per line. */
function topicsOfColumn(text) {
  if (text === null || text === undefined || text === '') return [];
  try {
    const v = JSON.parse(text);
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.filter((x) => typeof x === 'string');
  } catch {
    // not JSON: one topic per line, below
  }
  return String(text).split('\n').map((t) => t.trim()).filter((t) => t !== '');
}

const PARENT_STMTS = new WeakMap();
function parentStmts(db) {
  let s = PARENT_STMTS.get(db);
  if (s === undefined) {
    s = {
      maxRow: db.prepare('SELECT max(rowid) AS r FROM nodes'),
      touched: db.prepare('SELECT DISTINCT session_pk, epoch_seq FROM nodes WHERE rowid > ?'),
      epochTranscripts: db.prepare('SELECT t.transcript_pk AS transcript_pk FROM epochs e JOIN transcripts t ON t.cc_session_uuid = e.cc_session_uuid '
        + "WHERE e.session_pk = ? AND e.seq = ? AND t.agent_id = '' ORDER BY t.transcript_pk"),
      bounds: db.prepare('SELECT entry_id, transcript_pk FROM boundaries WHERE transcript_pk = ? ORDER BY ord'),
      leafAt: db.prepare('SELECT node_id FROM nodes WHERE boundary_entry_id = ? AND depth = 0'),
      exists: db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      node: db.prepare('SELECT node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, gist, topics, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      refs: db.prepare('SELECT kind, value, origin FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY rowid'),
      rowidOf: db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS r FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      insNode: db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, gist, topics, '
        + 'summary_blob_id, boundary_entry_id, span_start_uuid, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars, '
        + 'directive_flag, capped, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)'),
      insChild: db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_children (node_id, child_id, ord) VALUES (?, ?, ?)'),
      insRef: db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_refs (node_id, kind, value, origin) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (node_id, kind, value) DO NOTHING'),
    };
    PARENT_STMTS.set(db, s);
  }
  return s;
}

/** A node's stored fields, as parentRollup and the nodes_fts row read them. */
function storedNode(db, id) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const r = s.node.get(id);
  return {
    row: r,
    rollup: {
      gist: typeof r.gist === 'string' ? r.gist : null,
      topics: topicsOfColumn(r.topics),
      refs: s.refs.all(id).map((x) => ({ kind: x.kind, value: x.value, origin: x.origin })),
      earliestMs: r.earliest_ms === null ? null : Number(r.earliest_ms),
      latestMs: r.latest_ms === null ? null : Number(r.latest_ms),
      srcChars: Number(r.src_chars ?? 0),
      descCount: Number(r.desc_count ?? 0),
      descChars: Number(r.desc_chars ?? 0),
    },
  };
}

/** One nodes_fts row: the gist, the topics one per line and the ref values one per line, each run through
 *  redactField with this tick's pairs. The parts are taken from redacted text already (§6.2); this pass also
 *  catches a pair learned since. */
function insertNodeFts(db, ictx, rowid, gist, topics, refs) {
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)').run(
    rowid,
    redactField(gist ?? '', ictx.pairIdx),
    redactField(topics.join('\n'), ictx.pairIdx),
    redactField(refs.map((r) => r.value).join('\n'), ictx.pairIdx),
  );
}

/** The parent of `childIds` at `depth`, unless it exists. Returns its id, or null when it was there. */
function createParent(db, ictx, childIds, depth) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const id = parentId(childIds);
  if (s.exists.get(id) !== undefined) return null;
  const kids = childIds.map((c) => storedNode(db, c));
  const first = kids[0].row;
  const r = parentRollup(kids.map((k) => k.rollup));
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    s.insNode.run(id, first.session_pk, first.epoch_seq, first.transcript_pk, 'condensed', depth, 'ok', r.gist, JSON.stringify(r.topics),
      r.earliestMs, r.latestMs, r.srcChars, r.descCount, r.descChars, directiveFlag(r.gist ?? '') ? 1 : 0, r.capped ? 1 : 0,
      NODE_PARSER_VERSION, ictx.nowMs);
    childIds.forEach((c, i) => { s.insChild.run(id, c, i); });
    for (const ref of r.refs) s.insRef.run(id, ref.kind, ref.value, ref.origin);
    if (ictx.fts === true) insertNodeFts(db, ictx, s.rowidOf.get(id).r, r.gist, r.topics, r.refs);
  });
  return id;
}

/** Fan-in over ONE holding copy's level-0 slots, level by level (§6.3). Each slot holds its leaf or null; each
 *  level above holds the parents of the level below, in their children's order. Returns the parents made. */
function fanInLevels(db, ictx, level0) {
  let made = 0;
  let level = level0;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < MAX_FAN_DEPTH && level.length > 0; depth += 1) {
    const width = depth === 0 ? FAN_IN.leaf : FAN_IN.condensed;
    const slots = level.map((id) => ({ nodeId: id, final: id !== null, parented: id !== null && parentOf(db, id) !== null }));
    for (const group of planFanIn({ slots, width })) {
      if (createParent(db, ictx, group, depth + 1) !== null) made += 1;
    }
    const next = [];
    for (const id of level) {
      if (id === null) continue;
      const p = parentOf(db, id);
      if (p !== null && !next.includes(p)) next.push(p);
    }
    level = next;
  }
  return made;
}

/** Every parent one epoch can have now (§6.3; the coordinator's ruling RB4). Level 0 is split PER HOLDING COPY:
 *  each boundary of the epoch's main transcript, in `ord`, joins the slot list of the file Task 8's holdingCopy
 *  picks for it (a live file first, then the smallest file_id, among the files that have it as a member).
 *  - Why: `boundaries.ord` is numbered per transcript in arrival order, so two forks of one transcript
 *    interleave in it. One list for the whole transcript would let a parent take leaves of both forks, and a
 *    leaf not derived yet in one fork would stop the other's grouping. Per copy, a null slot stops only its own
 *    copy, and a parent's children share one copy.
 *  - A shared head falls to the copy that holds it (the smaller file_id when both are live), so the other fork's
 *    list starts after the fork.
 *  - A boundary no file holds has no leaf (Task 8 waits on it) and joins no list.
 *  - The split is read when a parent is minted. A parent minted earlier keeps its children: they read parented
 *    (parentOf), and planFanIn never regroups a parented slot.
 *  The lists run in ascending file_id. Returns the parents made. */
function deriveEpochParents(db, ictx, sessionPk, epochSeq) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const ds = stmts(db);
  const pass = { files: new Map() };
  const copies = new Map();   // holding file_id → its level-0 slots, in ord
  for (const t of s.epochTranscripts.all(sessionPk, epochSeq)) {
    for (const b of s.bounds.all(t.transcript_pk)) {
      const holding = holdingCopy(ds, pass, b);
      if (holding === null) continue;
      const copyKey = holding.file_id;
      if (!copies.has(copyKey)) copies.set(copyKey, []);
      const leaf = s.leafAt.get(b.entry_id);
      copies.get(copyKey).push(leaf === undefined ? null : leaf.node_id);
    }
  }
  let made = 0;
  for (const key of [...copies.keys()].sort((x, y) => Number(x) - Number(y))) made += fanInLevels(db, ictx, copies.get(key));
  return made;
}

/** Fan-in for every epoch that gained a node since the cursor (§6.3). Returns how many parents it made. */
export function deriveParents(db, ictx, budget) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const step = getStep(db, PARENTS_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION);
  const from = step === null || step.cursor === null ? 0 : Number(step.cursor);
  const top = s.maxRow.get().r;
  if (top === null || Number(top) <= from) return 0;
  let made = 0;
  for (const e of s.touched.all(from)) {
    if (!parentsBudgetLeft(budget)) return made;
    made += deriveEpochParents(db, ictx, e.session_pk, e.epoch_seq);
  }
  setStep(db, PARENTS_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, String(top), null);
  return made;
}

/** The nodes_fts backfill (§6.2): every node past the ('nodes-fts', 1) cursor with no nodes_fts row gets one.
 *  This covers a node derived while the FTS tables did not exist, or after doctor --repair recreated them.
 *  A node indexed at derivation is skipped, never inserted twice: a second insert of one rowid throws.
 *  Returns the rows added. */
export function indexNodesFts(db, ictx, budget) {
  if (ictx.fts !== true) return 0;
  const step = getStep(db, NODES_FTS_STEP, NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION);
  let cursor = step === null || step.cursor === null ? 0 : Number(step.cursor);
  const page = db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS rid, node_id FROM nodes WHERE rowid > ? ORDER BY rowid LIMIT ?');
  const has = db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?');
  let added = 0;
  while (parentsBudgetLeft(budget)) {
    const rows = page.all(cursor, NODES_FTS_BATCH);
    if (rows.length === 0) break;
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
      for (const r of rows) {
        if (has.get(r.rid) !== undefined) continue;
        const n = storedNode(db, r.node_id).rollup;
        insertNodeFts(db, ictx, r.rid, n.gist, n.topics, n.refs);
        added += 1;
      }
      cursor = Number(rows[rows.length - 1].rid);
      setStep(db, NODES_FTS_STEP, NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION, String(cursor), null);
    });
  }
  return added;
}

/** Every condensed node above `nodeIds`, re-rolled from its children as they are stored now (§6.3), for a reparse
 *  (W1-B2 Task 21) or a pair learned late (Task 29). Ids and node_children never change; a parent's rollup fields,
 *  node_refs and nodes_fts row do. Lower levels go first, so each level reads children already re-rolled. Returns
 *  how many parents it rewrote. */
export function rerollParents(db, ictx, nodeIds) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const depthOf = db.prepare('SELECT depth FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?');
  const kidsOf = db.prepare('SELECT child_id FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord');
  const setParent = db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ?, topics = ?, earliest_ms = ?, latest_ms = ?, src_chars = ?, '
    + 'desc_count = ?, desc_chars = ?, directive_flag = ?, capped = ?, parser_version = ? WHERE node_id = ?');
  const dropRefs = db.prepare('DELETE FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?');
  const above = new Map();
  for (const id of nodeIds) {
    let p = parentOf(db, id);
    for (let k = 0; p !== null && k < MAX_FAN_DEPTH && !above.has(p); k += 1) {
      const d = depthOf.get(p);
      if (d === undefined) break;
      above.set(p, Number(d.depth));
      p = parentOf(db, p);
    }
  }
  const order = [...above.entries()].sort((x, y) => x[1] - y[1] || (x[0] < y[0] ? -1 : x[0] > y[0] ? 1 : 0)).map(([id]) => id);
  let n = 0;
  for (const id of order) {
    const kids = kidsOf.all(id).map((r) => storedNode(db, r.child_id));
    if (kids.length === 0) continue;
    const r = parentRollup(kids.map((k) => k.rollup));
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
      setParent.run(r.gist, JSON.stringify(r.topics), r.earliestMs, r.latestMs, r.srcChars, r.descCount, r.descChars,
        directiveFlag(r.gist ?? '') ? 1 : 0, r.capped ? 1 : 0, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, id);
      dropRefs.run(id);
      for (const ref of r.refs) s.insRef.run(id, ref.kind, ref.value, ref.origin);
      if (ictx.fts === true) {
        const rowid = s.rowidOf.get(id).r;
        db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?').run(rowid);
        insertNodeFts(db, ictx, rowid, r.gist, r.topics, r.refs);
      }
    });
    n += 1;
  }
  return n;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: (Re)create the mutant applier (scratch, gitignored, never committed).** It is the same script Task 9 Step 1 wrote; writing it again is harmless and makes this task self-contained. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <<'EOF'
// mut-after.mjs: apply ONE mutant for a mutation pin (W1-B2 plan, Tasks 9-11), in place.
// usage: node .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]
// For each pair, replace the FIRST occurrence of <needle> that follows the first occurrence of <anchor>.
// - The clean file is saved first to .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig.
// - The script exits 1 and writes nothing when the anchor or any needle is missing, so a mutant never applies half.
// - It also exits 1 while an earlier .orig is still there (an unrestored mutant).
// Restore: mv .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig <file>
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
const [file, anchor, ...pairs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (file === undefined || anchor === undefined || pairs.length === 0 || pairs.length % 2 !== 0) {
  console.error('usage: node mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]');
  process.exit(2);
}
const scratch = join('.superpowers', 'sdd', 'history-w1-b2', 'scratch');
mkdirSync(scratch, { recursive: true });
const orig = join(scratch, `${basename(file)}.orig`);
if (existsSync(orig)) {
  console.error(`mut-after: ${orig} exists: restore the earlier mutant first (mv ${orig} ${file})`);
  process.exit(1);
}
let text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const at = text.indexOf(anchor);
if (at < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: anchor not found in ${file}: ${anchor}`); process.exit(1); }
for (let i = 0; i < pairs.length; i += 2) {
  const k = text.indexOf(pairs[i], at);
  if (k < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: needle not found after the anchor: ${pairs[i]}`); process.exit(1); }
  text = text.slice(0, k) + pairs[i + 1] + text.slice(k + pairs[i].length);
}
copyFileSync(file, orig);
writeFileSync(file, text);
console.log(`mut-after: mutated ${file}; restore with: mv ${orig} ${file}`);
EOF
git check-ignore -q .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs && echo ignored
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 10: the CLI runner, the pane fixtures, and a captured family ─────────────────────────────
/** The pane every read-verb case runs in. */
export const PANE = '%1';

/** A working tmux in <home>/.local/bin, over the poison: it records its argv in $HOME/tmux-calls and answers
 *  `cc-<id>` (or `opts.name` verbatim) as the pane's session name. Returns the env a CLI child needs. */
export function withPane(box: HistoryBox, id: string, opts: { name?: string } = {}): Record<string, string> {
  const name = opts.name ?? `cc-${id}`;
  const bin = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'tmux');
  fs.writeFileSync(bin, `#!/bin/sh\nprintf '%s\\n' "$*" >> "$HOME/tmux-calls"\nprintf '%s\\n' '${name}'\n`);
  fs.chmodSync(bin, 0o755);
  return { TMUX_PANE: PANE };
}

/** A tmux that never answers: `exec sleep` keeps one pid, so the CLI's SIGKILL at its deadline ends it (a child
 *  `sleep` would keep the pipe open past the kill). */
export function sleepyTmux(box: HistoryBox, seconds: number): Record<string, string> {
  const bin = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'tmux');
  fs.writeFileSync(bin, `#!/bin/sh\nexec sleep ${String(seconds)}\n`);
  fs.chmodSync(bin, 0o755);
  return { TMUX_PANE: PANE };
}

/** `node --no-warnings cli.mjs <args>` in the box, on the statfs preload, capped like every spawn here. `json` is
 *  the last stdout line parsed, or null when it is not a JSON object. */
export function runCli(box: HistoryBox, args: string[], opts: SpawnOpts = {}): SpawnResult & { json: Record<string, unknown> | null } {
  const r = timed(() => spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', CLI, ...args],
    { env: childEnv(box, opts), cwd: box.home, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: opts.timeoutMs ?? SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, killSignal: 'SIGTERM' }));
  let json: Record<string, unknown> | null = null;
  try {
    const v: unknown = JSON.parse(r.stdout.trim().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '');
    if (v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v)) json = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  } catch {
    // a human-format answer
  }
  return { ...r, json };
}

/** The project slug a seeded transcript sits under. */
export const SEED_SLUG = '-home-u-tree-demo';
export interface SeedSpec {
  id: string; project: string; uuid: string; rows: object[];
  workdir?: string; generation?: string | null; accountId?: string;
}

/** One family, captured as the box captures one:
 *  - one priming sweep first, which spends the first tick's registry scan so the epoch is the hook's 'startup' and
 *    not the scan's 'import' (B1's scanDue is true while meta scan_ms is null; registryBackfill books a planted .uuid);
 *  - its registry fields;
 *  - its transcript, under the roster's first account unless `accountId` names another;
 *  - a SessionStart(startup) line whose `reg` is the uuid; B1 drains it one tick after renaming it, so the epoch
 *    appears on the second sweep (§6.1);
 *  - sweep ticks until one leaves the transcript at end-of-file AND its epoch confirmed.
 *  A string `generation` is written to the registry and carried on the line; null writes none (a gen-less line).
 *  Throws when four ticks do not get there: a seed that stops short would make every case built on it vacuous. */
export function seedFamily(box: HistoryBox, f: SeedSpec): { uuid: string; transcript: string } {
  const prime = runSweep(box);
  if (prime.code !== 0) throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): the priming sweep exited ${String(prime.code)}: ${prime.stderr}${prime.stdout}`);
  plantSession(box, f.id, {
    uuid: f.uuid, project: f.project,
    ...(f.generation === undefined ? {} : { generation: f.generation }),
    ...(f.workdir === undefined ? {} : { workdir: f.workdir }),
  });
  const transcript = plantTranscript(box, f.accountId ?? Object.keys(box.accountHome)[0]!, SEED_SLUG, f.uuid, f.rows);
  spoolLine(box, f.id, {
    v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: f.id, sid: f.uuid, src: 'startup', reg: f.uuid,
    ...(typeof f.generation === 'string' ? { gen: f.generation } : {}),
  });
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i += 1) {
    const r = runSweep(box);
    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): the sweep exited ${String(r.code)}: ${r.stderr}${r.stdout}`);
    if (atEndOfFile(box, f.uuid)) return { uuid: f.uuid, transcript };
  }
  throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): four ticks left ${f.uuid} short of end-of-file`);
}

function atEndOfFile(box: HistoryBox, uuid: string): boolean {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    const row = db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ingest_files f JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = f.transcript_pk WHERE t.cc_session_uuid = ? AND f.source_key = '' AND f.eof_ms IS NOT NULL")
      .get(uuid) as { n: number };
    // B1 reaches the transcript's EOF through hintedUuids in the tick that RENAMES the line, but drains the line (and so
    // books the family and its epoch) only in the next: EOF alone would return before the family exists.
    const ep = db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM epochs WHERE cc_session_uuid = ? AND confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL').get(uuid) as { n: number };
    return Number(row.n) > 0 && Number(ep.n) > 0;
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}
```
