```js
// ── grep: arguments and the index gate (W1-B2 Task 12; spec §8.4, §9.1) ──────────────────────────────

/** What the sweep indexes and grep may search: the searchable provenances plus recall-echo. Default grep
 *  filters to SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE at query time; `--include-recall` widens it to this list (§8.4
 *  "Recall echoes … are stored, excluded from default search, and found with --include-recall").
 *  ⟦D:history-recall-echo-indexed⟧ */
export const INDEXED_PROVENANCE = Object.freeze([...SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE, 'recall-echo']);

/** derivation_state's FTS step (§9.1): the sweep creates and backfills the FTS tables under ('fts', 1), and
 *  grep's index gate reads the same row. Spelled once, here. */
export const FTS_STEP = 'fts';

/** grep's index gate (§9.1, §8.3 exit 7), over what the reader measured:
 *  - a probe that THREW is 5 probe-failed, never folded into absent;
 *  - an absent module is 7 fts5-absent;
 *  - no blobs_fts yet, or a backfill ('fts', 1) that has not completed, is 7 fts-pending, so a partial index
 *    never answers 3 for text the store holds but has not indexed yet.
 *  ⟦D:history-grep-pending-until-backfilled⟧ */
export function decideGrepIndex({ probe, table, completed }) {
  if (probe === 'threw') return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.DB, reason: 'probe-failed' };
  if (probe !== 'present') return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.FTS_UNAVAILABLE, reason: 'fts5-absent' };
  if (!table || !completed) return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.FTS_UNAVAILABLE, reason: 'fts-pending' };
  return { ok: true };
}

/** grep's option grammar (§8.4), over the argv after the verb word. Every value is checked here, before any
 *  identity or store read. The scope flags (--project, --workspace, --session <id>) are consumed and passed
 *  over: readContext decides them (Task 10). `--` ends the options, so a word that begins with `--` can be
 *  searched. With --regex there are no positional words and no rank to sort by (Task 14). */
export function parseGrepArgs(argv, nowMs) {
  const a = {
    words: [], regex: null, role: null, tool: null, sinceMs: null, beforeMs: null, node: null,
    sort: 'recency', limit: GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT, cursor: null, includeRecall: false, json: false,
  };
  const bad = { ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' };
  const seen = new Set();
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const t = argv[i];
    if (t === '--') { a.words.push(...argv.slice(i + 1)); break; }
    if (!t.startsWith('--')) { a.words.push(t); continue; }
    if (seen.has(t)) return bad;
    seen.add(t);
    if (t === '--json') { a.json = true; continue; }
    if (t === '--include-recall') { a.includeRecall = true; continue; }
    if (t === '--project' || t === '--workspace') continue;
    if (i + 1 >= argv.length) return bad;
    i += 1;
    const v = argv[i];
    switch (t) {
      case '--session': break;
      case '--regex': a.regex = v; break;
      case '--role': if (!/^[a-z]{1,16}$/.test(v)) return bad; a.role = v; break;
      case '--tool': if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$/.test(v)) return bad; a.tool = v; break;
      case '--since': a.sinceMs = parseTimeBound(v, nowMs); if (a.sinceMs === null) return bad; break;
      case '--before': a.beforeMs = parseTimeBound(v, nowMs); if (a.beforeMs === null) return bad; break;
      case '--node': a.node = v; break;
      case '--sort': if (!GREP_SORTS.includes(v)) return bad; a.sort = v; break;
      case '--limit': {
        if (!/^[1-9][0-9]{0,5}$/.test(v) || Number(v) > GREP_LIMIT_MAX) return bad;
        a.limit = Number(v);
        break;
      }
      case '--cursor': a.cursor = v; break;
      default: return bad;
    }
  }
  if (a.regex === null ? a.words.length === 0 : a.words.length > 0 || a.sort !== 'recency') return bad;
  return { ok: true, args: a };
}
```

export const INDEXED_PROVENANCE: readonly Provenance[];
export const FTS_STEP: 'fts';
export type GrepIndexVerdict =
  | { ok: true }
  | { ok: false; exit: 5 | 7; reason: 'probe-failed' | 'fts5-absent' | 'fts-pending' };
export function decideGrepIndex(i: { probe: 'present' | 'absent' | 'threw'; table: boolean; completed: boolean }): GrepIndexVerdict;
export interface GrepArgs {
  words: string[]; regex: string | null; role: string | null; tool: string | null; sinceMs: number | null; beforeMs: number | null;
  node: string | null; sort: 'recency' | 'relevance' | 'hybrid'; limit: number; cursor: string | null; includeRecall: boolean; json: boolean;
}
export function parseGrepArgs(argv: readonly string[], nowMs: number): { ok: true; args: GrepArgs } | { ok: false; reason: 'bad-args' };

/** The ReadContext Task 10's readContext builds, as these tests build it in-process (cli.mjs is never imported
 *  here: it sets this worker's umask). */
interface GrepRc {
  db: RDatabaseSync; version: number; schema: unknown; storeId: string | null; nowMs: number; home: string; id: string;
  scope: {
    kind: 'family' | 'project' | 'workspace'; id: string; generation: string | null; project: string | null; workdir: string | null;
    sessionPks: number[]; transcriptPks: number[];
    families: Array<{ sessionPk: number; ccrcId: string; generation: string; firstSeenMs: number }>;
  };
  pairIdx: unknown;
}
interface GrepVerbResult {
  exit: number; reason?: string; header: string | null; blocks: string[]; items: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  shown: number; total: number; next: string[] | null; hint?: string;
}
interface GrepDeps { cap?: number; budgetMs?: number; spawn?: (...args: unknown[]) => unknown }
interface GrepMod {
  runGrep(rc: GrepRc, a: RGrepArgs, deps?: GrepDeps): GrepVerbResult;
  runDescribe?(rc: GrepRc, a: unknown, deps?: GrepDeps): GrepVerbResult;
}
type CliRun = rH.SpawnResult & { json: Record<string, unknown> | null };

const GRX = {
  idA: 'claude-a-demo',
  idB: 'claude-b-demo',
  idO: 'claude-b-other',
  /** The fixtures' default cwd (historyFixtures' envelope), used as the workdir of every family here. */
  W: '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin',
  t0: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 5, 10, 0, 0),
  ts(s: number): string { return new Date(GRX.t0 + s * 1000).toISOString(); },
  /** A row uuid: tag and ordinal in hex, the UUID grammar (lowercase). */
  uuid(tag: number, i: number): string {
    return `0189abcd-${tag.toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}-4000-8000-${i.toString(16).padStart(12, '0')}`;
  },
  /** A transcript's (cc session's) uuid for a tag. */
  file(tag: number): string { return `0189abcd-${tag.toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}-4fff-8fff-ffffffffffff`; },
  user(tag: number, i: number, text: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}): rFx.Row {
    return { ...rFx.userRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), text }), ...extra };
  },
  assistant(tag: number, i: number, text: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.assistantRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), text,
      requestId: `req_g${tag}_${i}`, msgId: `msg_g${tag}_${i}` });
  },
  toolUse(tag: number, i: number, toolUseId: string, command: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.toolUseRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), toolUseId, name: 'Bash',
      input: { command }, requestId: `req_g${tag}_${i}`, msgId: `msg_g${tag}_${i}` });
  },
  toolResult(tag: number, i: number, toolUseId: string, content: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.toolResultRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), toolUseId, content });
  },
  /** A family: registry rows, the transcript, its startup line, swept to end of file (Task 10's seedFamily). */
  seed(box: rH.HistoryBox, tag: number, id: string, project: string, rows: rFx.Row[], accountId = 'claude-a'): string {
    return rH.seedFamily(box, { id, project, workdir: GRX.W, uuid: GRX.file(tag), rows, accountId }).transcript;
  },
  /** `ccrc history <args>` from `id`'s pane. */
  cli(box: rH.HistoryBox, id: string, args: string[], opts: rH.SpawnOpts = {}): CliRun {
    return rH.runCli(box, args, { ...opts, env: { ...rH.withPane(box, id), ...(opts.env ?? {}) } }) as CliRun;
  },
  items(r: CliRun): Array<Record<string, unknown>> {
    return ((r.json?.items ?? []) as Array<Record<string, unknown>>);
  },
  uuids(r: CliRun): unknown[] { return GRX.items(r).map((x) => x.entry_uuid); },
  async grepArgs(argv: string[]): Promise<RGrepArgs> {
    const lib = await import('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs');
    const p = lib.parseGrepArgs(argv, Date.now());
    if (!p.ok) throw new Error(`fixture argv refused: ${argv.join(' ')}`);
    return p.args;
  },
  async recall(): Promise<GrepMod> {
    return (await import('../../ccd/history/recall.mjs')) as unknown as GrepMod;
  },
  /** A family-scope ReadContext for `id`'s newest family, read off the fixture store the way Task 10 reads it: the
   *  family's confirmed epochs give its transcripts. The caller closes `db`. */
  async rc(box: rH.HistoryBox, id: string): Promise<GrepRc> {
    const store = await import('../../ccd/history/store.mjs');
    const lib = await import('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs');
    const db: RDatabaseSync = store.openReader(lib.historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    const fam = (db.prepare(`SELECT session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms FROM sessions
      WHERE ccrc_id = ? AND merged_into IS NULL ORDER BY first_seen_ms DESC LIMIT 1`).all(id) as unknown as
      Array<{ session_pk: number; ccrc_id: string; generation: string; project: string; first_seen_ms: number }>);
    const sessionPks = fam.map((f) => f.session_pk);
    const transcriptPks = (db.prepare(`SELECT DISTINCT t.transcript_pk AS pk FROM epochs e
      JOIN transcripts t ON t.cc_session_uuid = e.cc_session_uuid
      WHERE e.confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL AND e.session_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`).all(JSON.stringify(sessionPks)) as unknown as
      Array<{ pk: number }>).map((r) => r.pk);
    const storeId = (db.prepare("SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'store_id'").get() as { v: string } | undefined)?.v ?? null;
    return {
      db, version: store.userVersion(db), schema: lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, storeId, nowMs: Date.now(), home: box.home, id,
      scope: {
        kind: 'family', id, generation: fam[0]?.generation ?? null, project: fam[0]?.project ?? null, workdir: GRX.W,
        sessionPks, transcriptPks,
        families: fam.map((f) => ({ sessionPk: f.session_pk, ccrcId: f.ccrc_id, generation: f.generation, firstSeenMs: f.first_seen_ms })),
      },
      pairIdx: lib.makePairIndex([]),
    };
  },
  /** `db` with every prepare() recorded: the spy C7 reads. */
  spyDb(db: RDatabaseSync, calls: string[]): RDatabaseSync {
    return new Proxy(db, {
      get(t, k) {
        if (k === 'prepare') return (sql: string) => { calls.push(sql); return t.prepare(sql); };
        const v = Reflect.get(t, k, t) as unknown;
        return typeof v === 'function' ? (v as (...x: unknown[]) => unknown).bind(t) : v;
      },
    }) as RDatabaseSync;
  },
};

describe('grep, the FTS path: index gate, provenance, filters and everyday words (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  const T = 0x21;
  /** A deviation-number-shaped word, built in two pieces so this test's source holds no D-number token for the ledger's
   *  scanners to count (CLAUDE.md "Deviation ledger"). */
  const DNUM = ['D', '1234'].join('-');
  let box: rH.HistoryBox;
  beforeAll(() => {
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') return;
    box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-');
    GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [
      GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqoperatorword plain operator words'),
      GRX.assistant(T, 2, 'zqmodelword the answer'),
      rFx.systemRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(T, 3), ts: GRX.ts(3), sessionId: GRX.file(T), subtype: 'informational', content: 'zqharnessword' }),
      GRX.user(T, 4, 'zqmetaword injected', { isMeta: true }),
      rFx.summaryRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(T, 5), ts: GRX.ts(5), sessionId: GRX.file(T), text: 'zqsummaryword summary' }),
      GRX.toolUse(T, 6, 'toolu_g21echo', '"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history grep zqasked'),
      GRX.toolResult(T, 7, 'toolu_g21echo', 'zqechoword earlier recall output'),
      GRX.toolUse(T, 8, 'toolu_g21cat', 'cat notes.md'),
      GRX.toolResult(T, 9, 'toolu_g21cat', 'zqcatword <ccrc-recall id="L0123456789abcdef0123"> page body'),
      GRX.user(T, 10, 'zqfirstline\nzqsecondword'),
      GRX.user(T, 11, 'edit server/src/coord/store.ts now'),
      GRX.user(T, 12, 'run it with --force please'),
      GRX.user(T, 13, `set history-off before ${DNUM} lands`),
      GRX.user(T, 14, 'fixes #123 finally'),
      GRX.user(T, 15, 'look at arr[0] closely'),
      GRX.user(T, 16, 'commit a0860d1f2e3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f70819 landed'),
      GRX.user(T, 17, 'a naïve café visit'),
      GRX.user(T, 18, 'please say zqinner words now'),
    ]);
  }, 120_000);
  const grep = (args: string[], opts: rH.SpawnOpts = {}): CliRun => GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', ...args], opts);

  it('C26: the CLI handle on an FTS-ready store answers 0 or 3, never 7, and every --json reason maps to its exit', () => {
    const hit = grep(['zqoperatorword', '--json']);
    expect(hit.code, hit.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(hit)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 1)]);
    expect(hit.json?.total).toBe(1);
    const none = grep(['zqnowhereword', '--json']);
    expect(none.code, none.stderr).toBe(3);
    expect(none.json?.exit).toBe(3);
    expect(none.json).not.toHaveProperty('reason');
    expect(none.json?.coverage).toBe('this-box');
  }, 60_000);

  it('C26: a probe that throws is 5 probe-failed; one answering absent is 7 fts5-absent (the reader\'s own probe, never meta)', () => {
    const seam = (mode: string): CliRun => grep(['zqoperatorword', '--json'], { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: mode } });
    const threw = seam('throw');
    expect([threw.code, threw.json?.reason]).toEqual([5, 'probe-failed']);
    const absent = seam('absent');
    expect([absent.code, absent.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts5-absent']);
  }, 60_000);

  it('C7: regex syntax in plain search is exit 2 regex-syntax with a hint line, and no statement is ever prepared', async () => {
    const r = grep(['a|b', '--json']);
    expect([r.code, r.json?.reason]).toEqual([2, 'regex-syntax']);
    const human = grep(['zq.*word']);
    expect(human.code).toBe(2);
    expect(`${human.stdout}\n${human.stderr}`).toMatch(/^hint: .*--regex/m);
    const recall = await GRX.recall();
    const rc = await GRX.rc(box, GRX.idA);
    try {
      const calls: string[] = [];
      const spied = { ...rc, db: GRX.spyDb(rc.db, calls) };
      const refused = recall.runGrep(spied, await GRX.grepArgs(['a|b']));
      expect([refused.exit, refused.reason]).toEqual([2, 'regex-syntax']);
      expect(calls).toEqual([]);
      const answered = recall.runGrep(spied, await GRX.grepArgs(['zqoperatorword']));   // CONTROL: the spy sees a real query
      expect(answered.exit).toBe(0);
      expect(calls.some((s) => /blobs_fts MATCH/.test(s))).toBe(true);
    } finally { rc.db.close(); }
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM28 (CLI half): summary, harness and recall-echo text is not found by default grep; operator and model text is', () => {
    for (const w of ['zqharnessword', 'zqmetaword', 'zqsummaryword', 'zqechoword']) {
      const r = grep([w, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, w).toBe(3);
    }
    for (const w of ['zqoperatorword', 'zqmodelword']) expect(grep([w]).code, w).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('C9: an earlier `ccrc history grep` tool_result is not matched by default, and is matched with --include-recall', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqechoword']).code).toBe(3);
    const r = grep(['zqechoword', '--include-recall', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 7)]);
    expect(GRX.items(r)[0]?.provenance).toBe('recall-echo');
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM32 (CLI half): a cat result holding <ccrc-recall stays in default search (provenance by structure)', () => {
    const r = grep(['zqcatword', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 9)]);
    expect(GRX.items(r)[0]?.provenance).toBe('tool');
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM30 (CLI half): a word after a newline in a text block is found; the JSON keys type and text are not', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqsecondword']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['type']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['text']).code).toBe(3);
  }, 60_000);

  it('filters: --role, --tool, --since and --before narrow inside the scope', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqmodelword', '--role', 'assistant']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['zqmodelword', '--role', 'user']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqasked', '--tool', 'Bash']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['zqasked', '--tool', 'Read']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqoperatorword', '--since', '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqoperatorword', '--before', '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('everyday words that are not plain words are quoted FTS terms, never an FTS syntax error or exit 1 (review focus 2)', () => {
    const found: Array<[string[], number]> = [
      [['server/src/coord/store.ts'], 11], [['--', '--force'], 12], [['history-off'], 13], [[DNUM], 13], [['#123'], 14],
      [['"arr[0]"'], 15], [['"a0860d1f"*'], 16], [['a0860d1f*'], 16], [['café'], 17], [['cafe'], 17],
      // A quoted phrase with an inner quote splits at the quotes into three quoted terms (AND); an unbalanced quote
      // is dropped from its word. Neither is an FTS syntax error.
      [['"say "zqinner" words"'], 18], [['"zqinner'], 18],
    ];
    for (const [words, row] of found) {
      const r = grep(['--json', ...words]);
      expect(r.code, `${words.join(' ')}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(GRX.uuids(r), words.join(' ')).toContain(GRX.uuid(T, row));
    }
    for (const words of [['arr[0]'], ['a|b']]) {
      const r = grep(words);
      expect(r.code, words.join(' ')).toBe(2);
      expect(`${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`, words.join(' ')).toMatch(/^hint: /m);
    }
  }, 120_000);

  it('a statement that finds no blobs_fts (a repair racing the read) is 7 fts-pending, never exit 1 (review focus 5)', async () => {
    const recall = await GRX.recall();
    const rc = await GRX.rc(box, GRX.idA);
    try {
      const racing = new Proxy(rc.db, {
        get(t, k) {
          if (k === 'prepare') {
            return (sql: string) => {
              if (/blobs_fts MATCH/.test(sql)) throw new Error('no such table: blobs_fts');
              return t.prepare(sql);
            };
          }
          const v = Reflect.get(t, k, t) as unknown;
          return typeof v === 'function' ? (v as (...x: unknown[]) => unknown).bind(t) : v;
        },
      }) as RDatabaseSync;
      const r = recall.runGrep({ ...rc, db: racing }, await GRX.grepArgs(['zqoperatorword']));
      expect([r.exit, r.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    } finally { rc.db.close(); }
  });
});

describe('grep\'s index gate: no blobs_fts, or a backfill still running, is 7 fts-pending (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });

  it('a store whose sweep only ever saw FTS5 absent has no blobs_fts: grep is 7 fts-pending until a sweep with FTS makes it', () => {
    const T = 0x22;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-pend-');
    rH.plantSession(box, GRX.idA, { uuid: GRX.file(T), project: 'demo', workdir: GRX.W });
    rH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', '-home-u-worktrees-p-quiet-basin', GRX.file(T), [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqpendingword here')]);
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: GRX.idA, sid: GRX.file(T), src: 'startup', reg: GRX.file(T) });
    const absent = { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: 'absent' } };
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box, [], absent); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the row is captured, and no FTS table exists
      expect((db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'blobs_fts'").get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(0);
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?').get(GRX.uuid(T, 1)) as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqpendingword', '--json']);
    expect([r.code, r.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqpendingword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 120_000);

  it('a completed backfill re-opened by a tick that could not index answers 7 until a tick with FTS completes it', () => {
    const T = 0x23;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-reopen-');
    const file = GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqfirstword indexed at once')]);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqfirstword']).code).toBe(0);
    rFs.appendFileSync(file, rFx.jsonl([GRX.user(T, 2, 'zqlateword while the probe fails')]));
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: GRX.idA });
    const s = rH.runSweep(box, [], { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: 'throw' } });
    expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0);
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the table exists, the first word IS indexed, and the backfill row is open
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?').get('zqfirstword') as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
      expect((db.prepare("SELECT completed_ms AS c FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'fts' AND version = 1").get() as { c: number | null }).c).toBeNull();
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const pending = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqfirstword', '--json']);
    expect([pending.code, pending.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    expect(rH.runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('recall echoes are indexed by both paths, each pinned alone: inline at ingest, and by the backfill (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  /** An earlier recall and its output, appended in ONE write, so the tool_result meets its tool_use in one tick and is
   *  classed recall-echo by structure. */
  const echoPair = (tag: number, i: number): rFx.Row[] => [
    GRX.toolUse(tag, i, `toolu_g${tag.toString(16)}late`, '"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history grep zq'),
    GRX.toolResult(tag, i + 1, `toolu_g${tag.toString(16)}late`, 'zqlateecho earlier recall output'),
  ];
  /** derivation ('fts', 1)'s completed_ms: null while the backfill is open. */
  const fts1 = (box: rH.HistoryBox): number | null => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      return (db.prepare("SELECT completed_ms AS c FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'fts' AND version = 1").get() as { c: number | null }).c;
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };
  /** A row's provenance and its first body's fts_indexed mark. */
  const echoRow = (box: rH.HistoryBox, uuid: string): { provenance: string; fts_indexed: number } | undefined => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      return db.prepare(`SELECT e.provenance AS provenance, b.fts_indexed AS fts_indexed FROM entries e
        JOIN blobs b ON b.blob_id = e.blob_id WHERE e.uuid = ?`).get(uuid) as { provenance: string; fts_indexed: number } | undefined;
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };

  it('inline: an echo appended after the backfill completed is indexed by the tick that ingests it', () => {
    const T = 0x24;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-echo-inline-');
    const file = GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqplainword before the echo')]);
    expect(fts1(box), 'CONTROL: the seed completed the backfill').not.toBeNull();

describe('C27 and DM46: the scope join runs before the LIMIT; another project\'s transcript is never in scope (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  const TA = 0x27; const TB = 0x28; const TO = 0x29;
  let box: rH.HistoryBox;
  beforeAll(() => {
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') return;
    box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-scope-');
    // A: one old hit in a long sentence. B (same project, another family): 3,000 newer short rows that each say the
    // word three times, so every one of them outranks A's hit on BM25 and on recency.
    GRX.seed(box, TA, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(TA, 1, 'an older note with a single zqneedle among many other plain words here')]);
    GRX.seed(box, TB, GRX.idB, 'demo',
      Array.from({ length: 3000 }, (_, i) => GRX.user(TB, 100 + i, `zqneedle zqneedle zqneedle n${i}`)), 'claude-b');
    // O: another project's family, its own words.
    GRX.seed(box, TO, GRX.idO, 'other',
      [GRX.user(TO, 1, 'zqforeignword lives in the other project', { cwd: '/home/u/worktrees/other/x' })], 'claude-b');
    // A planted clear line in A's spool naming O's transcript (DM46): the first claim (O's, confirmed) stands.
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: GRX.idA, sid: GRX.file(TO), src: 'clear' });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
  }, 240_000);

  it('C27: 3,000 other-family blobs outrank one family hit, and the hit is still returned (exit 0, true count 1)', () => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: globally, A's blob is outside the top RANK_POOL on rank
      const aBlob = (db.prepare('SELECT blob_id AS b FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?').get(GRX.uuid(TA, 1)) as { b: number }).b;
      const top = (db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS r FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT 2000').all('zqneedle') as unknown as
        Array<{ r: number }>).map((x) => x.r);
      expect(top).toHaveLength(2000);
      expect(top).not.toContain(aBlob);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    for (const sort of ['relevance', 'recency', 'hybrid']) {
      const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqneedle', '--sort', sort, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, `${sort}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(GRX.uuids(r), sort).toEqual([GRX.uuid(TA, 1)]);
      expect(r.json?.total, sort).toBe(1);
    }
  }, 120_000);

  it('DM46 (CLI half): a planted clear line naming another project\'s transcript leaves its text out of the family: default grep is 3', () => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the text is stored and indexed; only the scope keeps it out
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?').get('zqforeignword') as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqforeignword']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idO, ['grep', 'zqforeignword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM46 (node half, review focus 4): the second claim chains no epoch, so none of that transcript\'s nodes can enter the family', () => {
    // A node's family is its epoch's (Tasks 8 and 9 take session_pk and epoch_seq from the epoch that holds the
    // transcript), so a uuid the first family keeps is never a node of the second.
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const count = (sql: string): number => (db.prepare(sql).get(GRX.idA, GRX.file(TO)) as { n: number }).n;
      expect(count(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk
        WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND e.cc_session_uuid = ?`), 'no epoch of A names O\'s transcript').toBe(0);
      expect(count(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk
        JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = n.transcript_pk WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND t.cc_session_uuid = ?`),
      'no node of A sits on O\'s transcript').toBe(0);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqneedle', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect((r.json?.scope as { transcripts: number }).transcripts, 'A\'s scope holds its own transcript only').toBe(1);
  }, 60_000);
});

Then append to the END of the file:

```js
/** A stored blob's plain text for the READ verbs: grep's snippets, the regex child and describe (W1-B2 Task 12). It is
 *  the text the FTS index holds for the blob (§6.2 "FTS indexing"), by lib's two rules:
 *  - a sidecar's is lib's sidecarIndexText over its decoded body with the pair index `idx`: the first
 *    SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES + SIDECAR_REDACT_MARGIN bytes redacted raw, unescaped and redacted again, and only THEN cut to
 *    SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES (B1's ⟦D:history-sidecar-redact-before-cut⟧, history-sidecar-redact-before-cut), so a secret straddling the cut leaves no
 *    prefix. It comes back already redacted;
 *  - a body's is its extracted text (text blocks, tool_use input string leaves, tool_result text; never the JSON),
 *    UNREDACTED: the caller runs redactField on it before any cut (history-redaction-before-cut). One that does not
 *    parse gives '': the index is derived, and the blob stays verbatim.
 *  This call is synchronous, so it decompresses a blob whole; B1's bounded unbrotliPrefix is async. A sidecar whose
 *  recorded `rawLen` (blobs.raw_len, read with z) passes SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX is therefore never decompressed here and
 *  gives '', the bound expand holds too (⟦D:history-read-skips-oversize-sidecar⟧). The sweep's own index keeps B1's
 *  async `ftsTextOfBlob`, which reads any sidecar's window through unbrotliPrefix. */
export function blobPlainText(z, isSidecar, idx, rawLen) {
  if (isSidecar) return rawLen <= SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX ? sidecarIndexText(unbrotli(z), idx) : '';
  const bytes = unbrotli(z);
  try {
    return ftsTextOf(JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8')), 'entry');
  } catch {
    return '';
  }
}
```

Merge these names into recall.mjs's existing import lines, adding a line only for a module it does not import yet:
- from `./lib.mjs`: `EXIT`, `REASONS`, `INDEXED_PROVENANCE`, `SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE`, `FTS_STEP`, `RANK_POOL`, `SNIPPET_MAX`, `decideGrepIndex`, `sanitizeFtsQuery`, `queryTerms`, `regexSyntaxIn`, `regexSyntaxHint`, `ftsOrderBy`, `snippetWindow`, `snippetLine`, `recallEnvelope`, `escapeXmlText`, `redactField`, `extractNodeId`, `resolveScopedId` and `selectColumns`;

Append the block below to the END of `ccd/history/recall.mjs`. Then run `node --check ccd/history/recall.mjs`. If Task 10's recall.mjs already declares a module-level name this block declares (`refusal`, `notFound`, `iso`, `versioned`, `bindFor`, `hintLine`, `scopeArgs` or `FRAME_RESERVE`), node reports `Identifier '…' has already been declared`:
- if the earlier declaration does the same thing, keep it and delete this block's copy;
- otherwise rename this block's helper, and its uses in this block, with a `grep` prefix.

```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// grep, the FTS path (spec §8.4, §8.3, §9.1; W1-B2 Task 12).
//  - A hit is one in-scope REFERRER of a matching blob: an entry (its first body), an entry variant (a
//    later body of the same uuid), or a sidecar. Blobs are shared across families, so a blob's match says
//    nothing about scope until it is joined to a referrer.
//  - The scope join and the provenance filter run INSIDE the ranking statement, before its LIMIT
//    (RANK_POOL), so exit 3 means zero in-scope matches, never zero in a global top-N (C27).
//  - total is a separate count of every in-scope matching referrer: the N of "shown K of N" (§8.3).
//  - Every select names its columns through selectColumns, so a store older than this code answers NULL
//    for a column it lacks (§6.11, DM44); none is SELECT * (C43).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Room kept for what the CLI prints around a verb's blocks: Task 11's header, `shown K of N`, `next:` and a hint
 *  line; with --json, the envelope's fixed fields and its scope, which names at most a handful of families plus
 *  `families_total` (Task 11's scopeJson and lib's SCOPE_FAMILIES_JSON_MAX), so it is bounded whatever the project holds. A verb's own blocks fill
 *  OUTPUT_CAP minus this (Tasks 13 and 15). */
const FRAME_RESERVE = 1200;

/** The entries columns a referrer carries. */
const REFERRER_ENTRY_COLS = Object.freeze(['entry_id', 'uuid', 'transcript_pk', 'ts_ms', 'role', 'provenance', 'tool_name', 'blob_id']);

/** The FTS match: each blob whose redacted plain text holds the sanitised query, with its BM25 rank. */
const FTS_MATCH = 'SELECT rowid, rank FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH :q';

/** The scope join, the provenance filter and grep's filters, over `refs r`. Named parameters: :tpks and :provs
 *  are JSON arrays (json_each), :nodes a JSON array or NULL, the rest a value or NULL. */
const GREP_FILTER = `r.transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:tpks))
      AND r.provenance IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:provs))
      AND (:role IS NULL OR r.role = :role)
      AND (:tool IS NULL OR r.tool_name = :tool)
      AND (:since IS NULL OR r.ts_ms >= :since)
      AND (:before IS NULL OR r.ts_ms < :before)
      AND (:nodes IS NULL OR r.entry_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:nodes)))`;

/** One table as a derived table holding the columns the store's version has (NULL AS <col> for one a later
 *  version adds). SQLite flattens it into the enclosing join, so the table's own indexes still serve it. */
function versioned(rc, table, alias, cols) {
  return `(SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, table, cols, rc.schema)} FROM ${table}) AS ${alias}`;
}

/** The named parameters `sql` uses, taken from `all`. node:sqlite refuses a named parameter the statement does
 *  not hold ("Unknown named parameter", M, 22.16.0), and the ranked and count statements use different sets. */
function bindFor(sql, all) {
  const out = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(all)) if (new RegExp(`:${k}(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`).test(sql)) out[k] = v;
  return out;
}

/** `refs`: every referrer of a blob `matchSql` selects as (blob_id, rank). That is the FTS MATCH here, and the
 *  regex child's blob list in Task 14. A variant whose blob is the entry's first body is that entry's own row
 *  (§6.2: the first body also gets a variant row once a second appears), so it is not counted twice. */
function referrerSql(rc, matchSql) {
  const e = (alias) => versioned(rc, 'entries', alias, REFERRER_ENTRY_COLS);
  return `WITH m(blob_id, rank) AS (${matchSql}),
  refs(via, entry_id, uuid, transcript_pk, ts_ms, role, provenance, tool_name, blob_id, name, rank) AS (
    SELECT 'entry', e.entry_id, e.uuid, e.transcript_pk, e.ts_ms, e.role, e.provenance, e.tool_name, m.blob_id, NULL, m.rank
      FROM m JOIN ${e('e')} ON e.blob_id = m.blob_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'variant', e.entry_id, e.uuid, e.transcript_pk, e.ts_ms, e.role, e.provenance, e.tool_name, m.blob_id, NULL, m.rank
      FROM m JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entry_variants', 'v', ['entry_id', 'blob_id'])} ON v.blob_id = m.blob_id
        JOIN ${e('e')} ON e.entry_id = v.entry_id
      WHERE v.blob_id <> e.blob_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'sidecar', s.entry_id, se.uuid, s.transcript_pk, COALESCE(se.ts_ms, s.first_seen_ms), NULL, 'tool', NULL,
        m.blob_id, s.name, m.rank
      FROM m JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'sidecars', 's', ['transcript_pk', 'name', 'blob_id', 'entry_id', 'first_seen_ms'])} ON s.blob_id = m.blob_id
        LEFT JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entries', 'se', ['entry_id', 'uuid', 'ts_ms'])} ON se.entry_id = s.entry_id
  )`;
}

/** The top RANK_POOL in-scope referrers in `sort` order. The scope sits in this statement's WHERE, before its
 *  LIMIT (C27). The tie-break makes the order total, so a cursor's position means one hit. */
function rankedSql(rc, matchSql, sort) {
  return `${referrerSql(rc, matchSql)}
  SELECT r.via AS via, r.entry_id AS entry_id, r.uuid AS uuid, r.ts_ms AS ts_ms, r.role AS role,
      r.provenance AS provenance, r.blob_id AS blob_id, r.name AS name
    FROM refs r WHERE ${GREP_FILTER}
    ORDER BY ${ftsOrderBy(sort, 'r.ts_ms')}, r.blob_id, r.entry_id LIMIT :pool`;
}

/** The true in-scope count, the same filter with no LIMIT. */
function countSql(rc, matchSql) {
  return `${referrerSql(rc, matchSql)}
  SELECT count(*) AS n FROM refs r WHERE ${GREP_FILTER}`;
}

/** A refusing VerbResult. Its exit is the one REASONS maps the word to (2, 4, 5 or 7). `hint` is the hint's text;
 *  the CLI prints it after `hint: ` (Task 10's emitResult). */
function refusal(reason, hint = null) {
  return { exit: REASONS[reason], reason, header: null, blocks: [], items: [], shown: 0, total: 0, next: null, ...(hint === null ? {} : { hint }) };
}

/** Exit 3: nothing in this scope, on this box (§8.3; coverage=this-box). It carries no reason. */
function notFound() {
  return { exit: EXIT.NOT_FOUND, header: null, blocks: [], items: [], shown: 0, total: 0, next: null };
}

/** A hint's text as VerbResult.hint carries it. The CLI prints the `hint: ` prefix itself (Task 10's emitResult),
 *  so one that arrives prefixed is stripped, never doubled. */
function hintLine(text) {
  return text.startsWith('hint: ') ? text.slice('hint: '.length) : text;
}

/** The flags that reproduce this call's scope in a `next:` line. */
function scopeArgs(rc) {
  if (rc.scope.kind === 'project') return ['--project'];
  if (rc.scope.kind === 'workspace') return ['--workspace'];
  return rc.scope.id === rc.id ? [] : ['--session', rc.scope.id];
}

/** An ISO time, or `?` for none. */
function iso(ms) {
  return ms === null || ms === undefined ? '?' : new Date(ms).toISOString();
}

/** A node id, prefix or pasted line resolved INSIDE the scope (§8.2 "Every verb resolves ids inside the scope";
 *  RV19). A node outside it is exit 2 out-of-scope, never 3; prefix uniqueness is computed among the scope's
 *  nodes. Node ids are hex after the kind letter, so `wanted + 'g'` bounds the prefix range on the primary key. */
export function resolveNodeInScope(rc, wanted) {
  const rows = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'nodes', ['node_id', 'session_pk'], rc.schema)} FROM nodes
    WHERE node_id >= ? AND node_id < ?`).all(wanted, `${wanted}g`);
  const mine = new Set(rc.scope.sessionPks);
  const verdict = resolveScopedId({
    wanted,
    inScope: rows.filter((x) => mine.has(x.session_pk)).map((x) => x.node_id),
    outOfScope: rows.filter((x) => !mine.has(x.session_pk)).map((x) => x.node_id),
  });
  switch (verdict.kind) {
    case 'ok': return { ok: true, id: verdict.id };
    case 'out-of-scope': return { ok: false, result: refusal('out-of-scope') };
    case 'not-found': return { ok: false, result: notFound() };
    case 'ambiguous':
      return { ok: false, result: refusal('bad-args',
        `${wanted} names ${verdict.candidates.length} nodes in this scope (${verdict.candidates.slice(0, 5).join(', ')}); give more of the id`) };
    default: return { ok: false, result: refusal('bad-args') };
  }
}

/** `--node`'s entries: the node resolved in scope, then its lineage (Task 9's range CTE, toward sources). */
function nodeEntries(rc, raw) {
  const ex = extractNodeId(raw);
  if (!ex.ok) return { ok: false, result: refusal('bad-args', hintLine(redactField(ex.error, rc.pairIdx))) };
  const found = resolveNodeInScope(rc, ex.id);
  if (!found.ok) return found;
  return { ok: true, entries: lineageEntries(rc.db, found.id).map((x) => x.entryId) };
}

/** Every named parameter grep's statements may use; bindFor keeps each statement's own. */
function grepParams(rc, a, nodes, extra) {
  return {
    ...extra,
    tpks: JSON.stringify(rc.scope.transcriptPks),
    provs: JSON.stringify(a.includeRecall ? INDEXED_PROVENANCE : SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE),
    role: a.role, tool: a.tool, since: a.sinceMs, before: a.beforeMs,
    nodes: nodes === null ? null : JSON.stringify(nodes),
    pool: RANK_POOL, now_ms: rc.nowMs,
  };
}

/** The ranked pool and the true count. When blobs_fts vanished between the gate and the statement (a
 *  `doctor --repair` drop and recreate), the answer is 7 fts-pending, never exit 1 (review focus 5). */
function rankedAndCounted(rc, matchSql, sort, all) {
  try {
    const rs = rankedSql(rc, matchSql, sort);
    const cs = countSql(rc, matchSql);
    const pool = rc.db.prepare(rs).all(bindFor(rs, all));
    const total = Number(rc.db.prepare(cs).get(bindFor(cs, all)).n);
    return { pool, total };
  } catch (e) {
    if (/no such table: (?:main\.)?blobs_fts\b/.test(String(e && e.message))) return { result: refusal('fts-pending') };
    throw e;
  }
}

/** grep's index gate on the reader (§9.1): the read-only probe, blobs_fts, and the backfill's row. */
function indexGate(rc) {
  let probe;
  try { probe = probeFts5(rc.db); } catch { probe = 'threw'; }
  const table = probe === 'present'
    && rc.db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'blobs_fts'").get() !== undefined;
  // derivation ('fts', 1), the one version the sweep creates (B1 Task 23).
  const row = table
    ? rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'derivation_state', ['completed_ms'], rc.schema)} FROM derivation_state
        WHERE step = ? AND version = 1`).get(FTS_STEP)
    : undefined;
  return decideGrepIndex({ probe, table, completed: row !== undefined && row.completed_ms !== null });
}

/** A blob's z, its recorded size (blobPlainText's sidecar bound) and pruned time. */
function blobOf(rc, blobId) {
  return rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'blobs', ['z', 'raw_len', 'pruned_ms'], rc.schema)} FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?`).get(blobId);
}

/** One hit's snippet (§8.3, P9, P12). The blob's plain text is REDACTED first, then cut to the window around the
 *  earliest term, made one line and cut to SNIPPET_MAX by Task 3's snippetLine (surrogate-safe). Redaction comes
 *  before every cut, so no window edge can leave a secret's prefix (history-redaction-before-cut): a sidecar's text
 *  is redacted inside blobPlainText, before its own 512 KB cut, and the outer redactField covers a body's text (and
 *  re-checks a sidecar's). */
function hitSnippet(rc, hit, terms) {
  const b = blobOf(rc, hit.blob_id);
  if (b === undefined) return '';
  if (b.z === null) return `content pruned on ${b.pruned_ms === null ? '?' : new Date(b.pruned_ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10)}`;
  const text = redactField(blobPlainText(b.z, hit.via === 'sidecar', rc.pairIdx, Number(b.raw_len)), rc.pairIdx);
  return snippetLine(snippetWindow(text, terms).replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
}

/** A hit's human line: its snippet inside the untrusted-content envelope, which escapes it (§8.3, P30). */
function hitLine(hit, snippet) {
  return `  ${recallEnvelope({ src: hit.provenance, id: hit.uuid ?? `sidecar:${hit.name}`, ts: hit.ts_ms, role: hit.role, text: snippet })}`;
}

/** A hit's --json item: JSON escaping only, so exact copies come from here (§8.3). */
function hitItem(hit, snippet, nodeId) {
  return {
    entry_uuid: hit.uuid, node_id: nodeId, ts_ms: hit.ts_ms, role: hit.role, provenance: hit.provenance, snippet,
    sidecar: hit.name, trust: 'untrusted',
  };
}

/** The first page of hits, flat. Task 13 replaces this with the grouped, capped and cursored rendering. */
function renderHits(rc, pool, termsOf, a, total) {
  const page = pool.slice(0, a.limit);
  const snippets = page.map((h) => hitSnippet(rc, h, termsOf(h)));
  return {
    exit: EXIT.OK, header: null, blocks: page.map((h, i) => hitLine(h, snippets[i])),
    items: page.map((h, i) => hitItem(h, snippets[i], null)), shown: page.length, total, next: null,
  };
}

/** `grep <words>` (§8.4). In order:
 *  1. regex syntax in plain search refuses BEFORE any statement is prepared (C7);
 *  2. the index gate;
 *  3. `--node`, resolved in scope;
 *  4. the ranked pool and the true count;
 *  5. the hits. */
export function runGrep(rc, a, deps = {}) {
  if (a.regex !== null) return refusal('bad-args', '--regex is not served by this build');   // Task 14 replaces this line
  const raw = a.words.join(' ');
  const syntax = regexSyntaxIn(raw);
  if (syntax !== null) {
    return refusal('regex-syntax', hintLine(regexSyntaxHint(escapeXmlText(redactField(raw, rc.pairIdx)), syntax)));
  }
  const gate = indexGate(rc);
  if (!gate.ok) return refusal(gate.reason);
  let nodes = null;
  if (a.node !== null) {
    const ne = nodeEntries(rc, a.node);
    if (!ne.ok) return ne.result;
    nodes = ne.entries;
  }
  const found = rankedAndCounted(rc, FTS_MATCH, a.sort, grepParams(rc, a, nodes, { q: sanitizeFtsQuery(raw) }));
  if ('result' in found) return found.result;
  if (found.total === 0) return notFound();
  const terms = queryTerms(raw);
  return renderHits(rc, found.pool, () => terms, a, found.total);   // deps: Task 13 reads deps.cap
}
```

  - Module-private: `LIVE_TAIL`, `STALE_CURSOR`, `grepKey(rc, a): string`, `cursorPos(cursor, key): number | null`, `grepArgv(rc, a, cursor): string[]`, `scopePrefixes(rc): Map<string, string>`, `coveringLeaves(rc, entryIds): Map<number, string>`, `leafHeads(rc, ids)`.
  - `runGrep` now validates `--cursor` before any statement, passes `{ pos, total, key }` and `deps` to `renderHits`, and still answers `--regex` with bad-args until Task 14.
  - The grep `--json` item: `{ entry_uuid: string | null, node_id: string | null, ts_ms: number | null, role: string | null, provenance: string, snippet: string, sidecar: string | null, trust: 'untrusted' }`. `node_id` is the covering leaf's full 20-hex id, or null for the live tail.
  - The grep cursor: `encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'grep', q: <grepKey>, pos: <offset in the ranked pool> })`.
- Produces (history-recall.test.ts): `GRX_C.summary(o)`, `GRX_C.compactions(tag, n, summaryOf)`, `GRX_C.nodes(box, id)` and `GRX_C.fillProject(box, project, n, tag0)`, which Task 15 reuses.

**Spec:**
- Sections:
  - §8.3: the envelope, the cap, "shown K of N" with true in-scope counts, the `next:` line, and `--json` with `trust:"untrusted"`;
  - §8.4: grep's grouping and live tail;
  - §11: P9 (snippet window), P12 (the cap with true counts) and P30 (escaping).
  - PROVENANCE entries for P9, P12 and P30 are Tasks 2 and 3's; this task copies no further upstream code.
- Pins: C12, C15.
- Departures:
  - ⟦D:history-redaction-before-cut⟧ ⟦D:history-coverage-this-box⟧
  - ⟦D:history-grep-pages-end-at-rank-pool⟧ (NEW). §8.4 gives the 2,000 pool to `hybrid` only. Every grep sort ranks and pages the top RANK_POOL in-scope matches, so each call sorts a bounded set. The true N stays in `shown K of N`; past the pool, the last page carries a `hint:` naming `--since` and `--before` instead of a `next:` line.

**Choices** (also in open_issues):
- **The cursor is an offset into the ranked pool.**
  - It is bound to a key over the sanitised query, the scope and every filter, so a cursor used with another query, scope or filter is refused (exit 2 `bad-args`), never applied to the wrong list.
  - Text indexed between two pages can shift positions by the number of new hits. That is accepted, and stated in the code.
- **Pages end at RANK_POOL** (⟦D:history-grep-pages-end-at-rank-pool⟧). When N exceeds RANK_POOL and the pool is exhausted, the last page carries no `next:`. It carries a `hint:` line to narrow the words or the time range instead.
- **The cap is measured on what is printed.** The human output is measured with its group headers; `--json` is measured on its items. FRAME_RESERVE (Task 12) holds the room for the CLI's header, shown, next and hint lines, and for the `--json` envelope, whose scope Task 11 bounds to `SCOPE_FAMILIES_JSON_MAX` (3) named families plus `families_total`.
- **The cap is fitted in rank order, then grouped.** `shown` is always the first K ranked hits of the page, so the next cursor is `pos + K`. At least one hit is always shown.
- **A row in two fork leaves groups under the lower `node_id`.** DM36/DM37 shared prefixes can put one row in two leaves.

const GRX_C = {
  /** A nine-section compaction summary as Claude Code writes it. Section 1 is optionally padded and closed by `tail`;
   *  then come 8. Current Work and 9. Optional Next Step, the pair the native gist reads (§7.4 item 8). */
  summary(o: { current: string; next: string; pad?: number; tail?: string }): string {
    return [
      'This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context.',
      '<summary>',
      '1. Primary Request and Intent:',
      '   Build the fixture feature.',
      ...Array.from({ length: o.pad ?? 0 }, () => '   filler line for the long summary fixture, plain words only.'),
      ...(o.tail === undefined ? [] : [`   ${o.tail}`]),
      '8. Current Work:',
      `   ${o.current}`,
      '9. Optional Next Step:',
      `   ${o.next}`,
      '</summary>',
    ].join('\n');
  },
  /** `n` manual compactions, then a live tail.
   *  - Span i is a user row and an assistant row, each saying `zqcommon` and `zqspan<i>`.
   *  - Boundary i keeps nothing (allUuids []), names span i's first row as its head, and names the summary row right
   *    after it as its anchor (manual: +1). So leaf i's sources are exactly span i (§6.1's span rule).
   *  - The claude assistant row of the next span is the first model reply after each summary: its producer (§6.2). */
  compactions(tag: number, n: number, summaryOf: (i: number) => string): { rows: rFx.Row[]; spans: string[][]; tail: string[] } {
    const rows: rFx.Row[] = [];
    const spans: string[][] = [];
    let s = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i <= n; i += 1) {
      const u = ++s;
      rows.push(GRX.user(tag, u, `zqcommon zqspan${i} question ${i}`));
      const asst = ++s;
      rows.push(GRX.assistant(tag, asst, `zqcommon zqspan${i} answer ${i}`));
      const b = ++s;
      const sm = ++s;
      rows.push(rFx.boundaryRow({
        uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, b), ts: GRX.ts(b), parentUuid: GRX.uuid(tag, asst), sessionId: GRX.file(tag),
        trigger: 'manual', headUuid: GRX.uuid(tag, u), anchorUuid: GRX.uuid(tag, sm), tailUuid: GRX.uuid(tag, asst), allUuids: [],
      }));
      rows.push(rFx.summaryRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, sm), ts: GRX.ts(sm), parentUuid: GRX.uuid(tag, b), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), text: summaryOf(i) }));
      spans.push([GRX.uuid(tag, u), GRX.uuid(tag, asst)]);
    }
    const tu = ++s;
    rows.push(GRX.user(tag, tu, 'zqcommon zqtailrow question'));
    const ta = ++s;
    rows.push(GRX.assistant(tag, ta, 'zqcommon zqtailrow answer'));
    return { rows, spans, tail: [GRX.uuid(tag, tu), GRX.uuid(tag, ta)] };
  },
  /** `id`'s leaf ids in boundary order, and its depth-1 parents. */
  nodes(box: rH.HistoryBox, id: string): { leaves: string[]; parents: string[] } {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const leaves = (db.prepare(`SELECT n.node_id AS id FROM nodes n JOIN boundaries b ON b.entry_id = n.boundary_entry_id
        JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND n.depth = 0 ORDER BY b.ord`).all(id) as unknown as
        Array<{ id: string }>).map((r) => r.id);
      const parents = (db.prepare(`SELECT n.node_id AS id FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk
        WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND n.depth = 1 ORDER BY n.earliest_ms`).all(id) as unknown as Array<{ id: string }>).map((r) => r.id);
      return { leaves, parents };
    } finally { db.close(); }
  },
  /** `n` more families of `project`, planted together and swept twice: the many-family project of the `--json` frame
   *  cases. Ids are `claude-a-zqf<i>`, and transcript tags are tag0 + i. Each family is one row whose cwd is a workdir of
   *  its own, so no existing --workspace scope gains a family. */
  fillProject(box: rH.HistoryBox, project: string, n: number, tag0: number): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {

      rH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', rH.SEED_SLUG, GRX.file(tag), [GRX.user(tag, 1, `filler family ${i}`, { cwd: workdir })]);
      rH.spoolLine(box, id, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id, sid: GRX.file(tag), src: 'startup', reg: GRX.file(tag) });

    try {   // a fill that stopped short would make the frame cases vacuous

        .get(project) as { n: number }).n;
      if (Number(have) !== n) throw new Error(`fillProject: ${String(have)} of ${String(n)} families captured`);

Replace Task 12's whole `renderHits` function (its doc comment included) with:

```js
/** The group key of rows no leaf covers yet: grep's live tail (§8.4). */
const LIVE_TAIL = '';

/** The hint a refused cursor carries. */
const STALE_CURSOR = 'that --cursor belongs to another query, scope or filter; run the query again without it';

/** What a grep cursor is bound to: the query, the scope and every filter. A cursor from another query or scope
 *  is refused, never applied to the wrong list. */
function grepKey(rc, a) {
  return sha256Hex(canonicalJson({
    words: a.regex === null ? sanitizeFtsQuery(a.words.join(' ')) : null, regex: a.regex,
    scope: [rc.scope.kind, rc.scope.id, rc.scope.generation],
    role: a.role, tool: a.tool, since: a.sinceMs, before: a.beforeMs, node: a.node, sort: a.sort, recall: a.includeRecall,
  })).slice(0, 20);
}

/** The ranked-pool offset a --cursor names, 0 with none, or null for a cursor that does not decode or belongs to
 *  another key. An offset is a position in a total order (rankedSql's tie-break). Text indexed between two pages
 *  can shift it by the number of new hits; that is accepted. */
function cursorPos(cursor, key) {
  if (cursor === null) return 0;
  const c = decodeCursor(cursor, 'grep');
  if (c === null || c.q !== key || !Number.isSafeInteger(c.pos) || c.pos < 0) return null;
  return c.pos;
}

/** The next page's argv: this call's query, scope and filters, then the cursor. Each argument is redacted as a raw
 *  field before nextLine serialises it (history-redaction-before-cut). Times are absolute, so a relative --since
 *  does not drift between pages. */
function grepArgv(rc, a, cursor) {
  const out = ['grep'];
  if (a.regex !== null) out.push('--regex', a.regex);
  out.push(...scopeArgs(rc));
  if (a.role !== null) out.push('--role', a.role);
  if (a.tool !== null) out.push('--tool', a.tool);
  if (a.sinceMs !== null) out.push('--since', new Date(a.sinceMs).toISOString());
  if (a.beforeMs !== null) out.push('--before', new Date(a.beforeMs).toISOString());
  if (a.node !== null) out.push('--node', a.node);
  if (a.sort !== 'recency') out.push('--sort', a.sort);
  if (a.limit !== GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT) out.push('--limit', String(a.limit));
  if (a.includeRecall) out.push('--include-recall');
  if (a.json) out.push('--json');
  out.push('--cursor', cursor);
  if (a.regex === null) out.push('--', ...a.words);
  return out.map((x) => redactField(x, rc.pairIdx));
}

/** Display prefixes for every node of the scope (§6.1): unique within the scope, never shorter than
 *  NODE_ID_DISPLAY_MIN. */
function scopePrefixes(rc) {
  const ids = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'nodes', ['node_id'], rc.schema)} FROM nodes
    WHERE session_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`).all(JSON.stringify(rc.scope.sessionPks)).map((r) => r.node_id);
  return displayPrefixes(ids);
}

/** Each entry's covering leaf, through node_sources_entry (§8.4). node_sources holds leaf edges only (§6.3). Two
 *  fork leaves can hold one shared row (DM36, DM37); it groups under the lower node_id, deterministically. */
function coveringLeaves(rc, entryIds) {
  if (entryIds.length === 0) return new Map();
  const rows = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ns.entry_id AS entry_id, min(ns.node_id) AS node_id
      FROM ${versioned(rc, 'node_sources', 'ns', ['node_id', 'entry_id'])}
      WHERE ns.entry_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?)) GROUP BY ns.entry_id`).all(JSON.stringify(entryIds));
  return new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.entry_id, r.node_id]));
}

/** The time range and gist of each group's leaf. */
function leafHeads(rc, ids) {
  if (ids.length === 0) return new Map();
  const rows = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'nodes', ['node_id', 'earliest_ms', 'latest_ms', 'gist'], rc.schema)}
    FROM nodes WHERE node_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`).all(JSON.stringify(ids));
  return new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.node_id, r]));
}

/** One page of hits (§8.3, §8.4), grouped under their covering leaves plus a live tail.
 *  - The page is pool[pos, pos + limit).
 *  - The cap is fitted in RANK order: K is the most leading hits whose grouped rendering (or, with --json, whose
 *    items) fits OUTPUT_CAP minus FRAME_RESERVE. At least one hit is always shown. Those K are then grouped; groups
 *    are ordered by their best hit, and hits keep rank order inside a group.
 *  - The next cursor is pos + K, so the cap never skips a hit.
 *  - A leaf group shows the leaf's display prefix, its time range and its gist, redacted then cut (one line,
 *    SNIPPET_MAX). Every recalled field sits in an escaped envelope.
 *  - `total` is the true in-scope count; past RANK_POOL there is no next page, and a hint says so. */
function renderHits(rc, pool, termsOf, a, page, deps = {}) {
  const budget = (deps.cap ?? OUTPUT_CAP) - FRAME_RESERVE;
  const hits = pool.slice(page.pos, page.pos + a.limit);
  if (hits.length === 0) return notFound();
  const snippets = hits.map((h) => hitSnippet(rc, h, termsOf(h)));
  const leafOf = coveringLeaves(rc, [...new Set(hits.map((h) => h.entry_id).filter((x) => x !== null))]);
  const groupOf = hits.map((h) => (h.entry_id === null ? LIVE_TAIL : leafOf.get(h.entry_id) ?? LIVE_TAIL));
  const heads = leafHeads(rc, [...new Set(groupOf.filter((g) => g !== LIVE_TAIL))]);
  const pre = scopePrefixes(rc);
  const headers = new Map();
  const headerOf = (g) => {
    if (headers.has(g)) return headers.get(g);
    let text;
    if (g === LIVE_TAIL) {
      text = '── live tail (rows no leaf covers yet)';
    } else {
      const n = heads.get(g);
      const shown = pre.get(g) ?? g;
      text = `── leaf ${shown} ${iso(n?.earliest_ms ?? null)} → ${iso(n?.latest_ms ?? null)}`;
      if (n !== undefined && n.gist !== null) {
        const gist = redactField(n.gist, rc.pairIdx).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
        const cut = snippetLine(gist);
        text += `\n  ${recallEnvelope({ src: 'node', id: shown, ts: n.latest_ms, role: null, text: cut })}`;
      }
    }
    headers.set(g, text);
    return text;
  };
  const lines = hits.map((h, i) => hitLine(h, snippets[i]));
  const items = hits.map((h, i) => hitItem(h, snippets[i], groupOf[i] === LIVE_TAIL ? null : groupOf[i]));
  const grouped = (k) => {
    const order = [];
    const members = new Map();
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i += 1) {
      if (!members.has(groupOf[i])) { members.set(groupOf[i], []); order.push(groupOf[i]); }
      members.get(groupOf[i]).push(lines[i]);
    }
    return order.map((g) => [headerOf(g), ...members.get(g)].join('\n'));
  };
  const size = (k) => (a.json ? JSON.stringify(items.slice(0, k)).length : grouped(k).join('\n').length);
  let k = 1;
  while (k < hits.length && size(k + 1) <= budget) k += 1;
  const end = page.pos + k;
  const next = end < pool.length ? grepArgv(rc, a, encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'grep', q: page.key, pos: end })) : null;
  const beyondPool = next === null && page.total > pool.length;
  return {
    exit: EXIT.OK, header: null, blocks: grouped(k), items: items.slice(0, k), shown: Math.min(k, items.length), total: page.total, next,
    ...(beyondPool ? { hint: `ranking covers the top ${RANK_POOL} in-scope matches; narrow the words, or add --since or --before` } : {}),
  };
}
```

Replace Task 12's whole `runGrep` function (its doc comment included) with:

```js
/** `grep <words>` (§8.4). In order:
 *  1. regex syntax in plain search refuses BEFORE any statement is prepared (C7);
 *  2. a --cursor that does not belong to this query refuses;
 *  3. the index gate;
 *  4. `--node`, resolved in scope;
 *  5. the ranked pool and the true count;
 *  6. one grouped, capped page. */
export function runGrep(rc, a, deps = {}) {
  if (a.regex !== null) return refusal('bad-args', '--regex is not served by this build');   // Task 14 replaces this line
  const raw = a.words.join(' ');
  const syntax = regexSyntaxIn(raw);
  if (syntax !== null) {
    return refusal('regex-syntax', hintLine(regexSyntaxHint(escapeXmlText(redactField(raw, rc.pairIdx)), syntax)));
  }
  const key = grepKey(rc, a);
  const pos = cursorPos(a.cursor, key);
  if (pos === null) return refusal('bad-args', STALE_CURSOR);
  const gate = indexGate(rc);
  if (!gate.ok) return refusal(gate.reason);
  let nodes = null;
  if (a.node !== null) {
    const ne = nodeEntries(rc, a.node);
    if (!ne.ok) return ne.result;
    nodes = ne.entries;
  }
  const found = rankedAndCounted(rc, FTS_MATCH, a.sort, grepParams(rc, a, nodes, { q: sanitizeFtsQuery(raw) }));
  if ('result' in found) return found.result;
  if (found.total === 0) return notFound();
  const terms = queryTerms(raw);
  return renderHits(rc, found.pool, () => terms, a, { pos, total: found.total, key }, deps);
}
```

### Task 14: grep --regex: the guard refusal with zero spawns, the literal prefilter, regex-worker.mjs over redacted text with paged iterate() and held statements, the 5 s wall-clock kill

**Files:**
- Create: `ccd/history/regex-worker.mjs`. It is L4 and imports lib.mjs and store.mjs. It ends in its own entry guard, and has no `.d.mts` (an L4 module, like sweep.mjs and cli.mjs).
- Modify: `ccd/history/recall.mjs`.
  - Append the regex block of Step 3 at the END of the file.
  - Replace the first line of `runGrep`'s body (the `--regex` placeholder Task 12 wrote) in place.
  - Merge new names into the import lines, and add `import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';` and `import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';` if recall.mjs lacks them.
- Test: `server/test/history-recall.test.ts`. Append one describe.
- `ccd/history/PROVENANCE` is NOT edited. The regex child's scan loop is written fresh against ccrc's schema: it steps the in-scope blobs in blob_id order through one held `iterate()` over a scope union, and keeps upstream `searchRegex`'s limit-and-first-match shape in no line. The P10 guard's entry is Task 2's.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 2 (lib): `guardRegex(pattern)` (answers `{ ok: true; source }` or `{ ok: false; why: 'too-long' | 'nested' | 'invalid' }`), `regexPrefilter(pattern)` (an exact-token FTS5 MATCH text such as `"word"`, never a prefix query, or null for a full in-scope scan), `REGEX_BUDGET_MS`, `REGEX_MAX_LEN`.
  - Tasks 12 and 13 (recall.mjs): `runGrep`, `refusal`, `notFound`, `grepKey`, `cursorPos`, `STALE_CURSOR`, `indexGate`, `nodeEntries`, `grepParams`, `rankedAndCounted` (it binds only the parameters a statement holds, so `:blobs` replaces `:q`), `renderHits`.
  - Task 12: store `blobPlainText(z, isSidecar, idx, rawLen)` (a sidecar's text redacted with `idx` before its cut; `''` for a sidecar whose `rawLen` passes `SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX`); in history-recall.test.ts, `GRX`, `GrepMod`, `GrepDeps`, `CliRun`.
  - B1 lib: `makePairIndex(pairs)`, `redactField(text, idx)`, `historyPaths`, `EXIT`. B1 store: `openReader(dbPath)`.
  - The type `PairIndex = { byLen: ReadonlyMap<number, ReadonlySet<string>> }` (B1 Task 9).
- Produces:
  - `regex-worker.mjs`:
    - `export function scanRegexJob(job: RegexJob): { matches: { blob_id: number; match: string }[]; scanned: number }`
    - `RegexJob = { dbPath: string; transcriptPks: number[]; provenance: string[]; prefilter: string | null; pattern: string; pairs: { len: number; sha256: string }[] }`
    - stdin: one `RegexJob` as JSON. stdout: one JSON line `{ blob_id, match }` per matching blob, then `{ done: true, scanned, matched }`. Exit 0, or 1 with `history-regex: <message>` on stderr.
  - recall.mjs:
    - `export const WORKER_PATH: string`
    - `export function runRegex(rc: ReadContext, a: GrepArgs, deps?: { cap?: number; budgetMs?: number; spawn?: typeof spawnSync }): VerbResult`
    - `runGrep` dispatches to `runRegex` when `a.regex !== null`.

**Spec:**
- Sections: §8.4 `--regex`; §9.1 (statements held through `iterate()`, CT9); §11 P10 and refuted candidate 1 (`(.*a){8}$` passes upstream's guard); §6.2 (a secret known when indexed is "never a term, a prefix hit or a regex match").
- Pins: C8a, C8b.
- Departures: ⟦D:history-fts-indexes-redacted-text⟧ ⟦D:history-test-seams-not-env⟧. The 50 ms budget and the spawn spy are in-process `deps`, never an env word.

**Choices** (also in open_issues):
- **`--regex` passes the same index gate as plain grep.** Exit 7 means one thing for every grep form, and the prefilter needs the index.
- **One match per blob.** The child reports each blob's first match, cut to 200 characters; it seeds the hit's snippet window.
- **A sidecar is matched over its first 512 KB**, the window plain grep indexes (DM29), through `blobPlainText`, which redacts that window before its cut. One past `SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX` is not decompressed and not scanned (⟦D:history-read-skips-oversize-sidecar⟧).
- **Regex hits are newest first.** They have no rank.
- **The child scans the in-scope blobs by provenance.** The parent then applies `--role`, `--tool`, `--since`, `--before` and `--node` to the referrers.
- **The pattern takes no flags.** It is case-sensitive, as JavaScript's default is.
- **The child runs its candidate statement ONCE.** One `iterate()` steps the rows lazily; that is the spec's "paged `iterate()`" (§8.4, and the module table's `regex-worker.mjs` row). A loop that re-runs the statement per 64-blob page (`blob_id > :after … LIMIT 64`) re-materialises the whole candidate union every page. That is quadratic: measured on Node 24.14.1 with B1's indexes, 5.3 s of SQL alone for 20,000 in-scope entries, against 181 ms for one iteration. Nothing would be left of the 5 s budget for the scan itself. The ordered statement names blob ids only, so its sorter never carries a compressed body. Each body is read by a second held statement, `SELECT z, raw_len FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?` (`raw_len` is `blobPlainText`'s sidecar bound): measured, with `z` alone, 0.85 s for 20,000 blobs of 20 KB with flat memory, against 1.6 s and a temp-file spill when `b.z` rides the sort.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the child and the parent.**

Create `ccd/history/regex-worker.mjs`:

```js
// ccd/history/regex-worker.mjs — the `grep --regex` child (spec 2026-10-05 §8.4, §9.1; W1-B2 Task 14).
//
// The parent (recall.mjs runRegex) admits a pattern through lib's guardRegex, spawns this file with
// `node --no-warnings`, writes one JSON job to its stdin, and kills it at a wall-clock budget (REGEX_BUDGET_MS,
// 5 s chosen). A kill is the parent's exit 2 `regex-timeout`, never "no match". This child:
//  - opens the store through store.mjs's read-only handle (readOnly + query_only) and writes nothing;
//  - steps the in-scope candidate blobs in blob_id order through ONE iterate() of one statement. SQLite steps that
//    cursor lazily, row by row: the spec's "paged iterate()" (§8.4). It never re-runs the statement per page of blobs:
//    a `blob_id > :after … LIMIT` window re-materialises the whole candidate union every page, which is quadratic
//    (measured: 5.3 s of SQL alone for 20,000 in-scope entries, against 181 ms for one iteration). The ordered
//    statement names blob ids only, so its sorter never carries a compressed body; a second statement reads each
//    body by its key;
//  - HOLDS both statements until it exits (§9.1, CT9: Node 22.15.1 finalises an unreferenced statement mid-iterate
//    when the GC runs, M; the floor is 22.16.0, and the hold costs nothing);
//  - matches the pattern against each blob's plain text AFTER redaction with the parent's pair index, so a
//    secret known to the store is never a regex hit (§6.2, DM31). It is the text plain grep indexes: a sidecar's first
//    512 KB (DM29), redacted inside blobPlainText before that cut (B1's sidecarIndexText), and a body's text through
//    redactField. A sidecar whose raw_len passes SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX is not decompressed, so it is not scanned
//    (⟦D:history-read-skips-oversize-sidecar⟧);
//  - prints one JSON line per matching blob, {blob_id, match}, then {done, scanned, matched}.
// It reads no environment variable and trusts only its job. Every column it names exists at schema v1, and
// migrations are additive (§6.11), so it needs no version-aware select.
import { readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { makePairIndex, redactField } from './lib.mjs';
import { blobPlainText, openReader } from './store.mjs';

/** Every statement this child iterates, or reads through while it iterates, referenced until it exits (CT9). */
const HELD = [];
/** A match is reported cut to this many characters: it only seeds the parent's snippet window. */
const MATCH_MAX = 200;
/** One candidate's compressed body and its recorded size (blobPlainText's sidecar bound), by its key. */
const BODY_SQL = 'SELECT z, raw_len FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?';

/** The in-scope candidate blobs in blob_id order, ids only, each with a stored body (z not pruned): those an in-scope
 *  entry of a listed provenance references (its first body or a variant), and those an in-scope sidecar holds when
 *  `tool` is listed. A prefilter is lib's regexPrefilter: the exact-token MATCH text of a whole-word literal the
 *  pattern must contain (never a prefix query); it narrows the candidates without changing the answer. */
function candidateSql(withPrefilter) {
  return `WITH cand(blob_id) AS (
      SELECT e.blob_id FROM entries e
        WHERE e.transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:tpks)) AND e.provenance IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:provs))
      UNION
      SELECT v.blob_id FROM entry_variants v JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = v.entry_id
        WHERE e.transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:tpks)) AND e.provenance IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:provs))
      UNION
      SELECT s.blob_id FROM sidecars s
        WHERE s.transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:tpks)) AND 'tool' IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(:provs)))
    SELECT c.blob_id AS blob_id, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sidecars s2 WHERE s2.blob_id = c.blob_id) AS is_sidecar
      FROM cand c JOIN blobs b ON b.blob_id = c.blob_id
      WHERE b.z IS NOT NULL${withPrefilter ? '\n        AND c.blob_id IN (SELECT rowid FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH :pre)' : ''}
      ORDER BY c.blob_id`;
}

/** Scan one job: every candidate blob, in one lazily stepped iterate(), redacted, then matched. The iterate()'s read
 *  transaction also covers each body read, so a body the candidate row saw stored is still stored; the null check is
 *  belt only. */
export function scanRegexJob(job) {
  const re = new RegExp(job.pattern);
  const idx = makePairIndex(job.pairs);
  const db = openReader(job.dbPath);
  try {
    const stmt = db.prepare(candidateSql(job.prefilter !== null));
    const bodyOf = db.prepare(BODY_SQL);
    HELD.push(stmt, bodyOf);
    const base = {
      tpks: JSON.stringify(job.transcriptPks), provs: JSON.stringify(job.provenance),
      ...(job.prefilter === null ? {} : { pre: job.prefilter }),
    };
    const matches = [];
    let scanned = 0;
    for (const row of stmt.iterate(base)) {
      scanned += 1;
      const body = bodyOf.get(row.blob_id);
      const z = body?.z;
      if (z === undefined || z === null) continue;
      const m = re.exec(redactField(blobPlainText(z, row.is_sidecar === 1, idx, Number(body.raw_len)), idx));
      if (m !== null) matches.push({ blob_id: row.blob_id, match: m[0].slice(0, MATCH_MAX) });
    }
    return { matches, scanned };
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}

function main() {
  const job = JSON.parse(readFileSync(0, 'utf8'));
  const { matches, scanned } = scanRegexJob(job);
  const out = matches.map((m) => JSON.stringify(m));
  out.push(JSON.stringify({ done: true, scanned, matched: matches.length }));
  process.stdout.write(`${out.join('\n')}\n`);
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href) {
  try {
    main();
  } catch (e) {
    process.stderr.write(`history-regex: ${e && e.message ? e.message : String(e)}\n`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
}
```

- Append to the END of the file:

```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// grep --regex (spec §8.4, §9.1; W1-B2 Task 14). A separate path:
//  1. the guard (lib's guardRegex): too long, nested or invalid is a discriminated refusal, and no child is spawned
//     (C8a);
//  2. the same cursor check and index gate as plain grep;
//  3. regex-worker.mjs, over redacted text, killed at a wall-clock budget. A kill is exit 2 regex-timeout, never
//     "no match" (C8b);
//  4. the matching blobs go through grep's own referrer join: scope, provenance and filters, a true count, and Task
//     13's grouped and capped page. Hits are newest first: a regex hit has no rank.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The regex child, beside this file. */
export const WORKER_PATH = fileURLToPath(new URL('./regex-worker.mjs', import.meta.url));
/** The child's stdout bound: one short JSON line per matching blob. */
const WORKER_MAX_BUFFER = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
/** The child's matches as the (blob_id, rank) rows referrerSql reads. */
const REGEX_MATCH = 'SELECT value, 0 FROM json_each(:blobs)';

/** The parent's pair index as the pairs the child rebuilds it from: (len, sha256) only, never a value. */
function pairsOf(idx) {
  const out = [];
  for (const [len, shas] of idx.byLen) for (const sha256 of shas) out.push({ len, sha256 });
  return out;
}

/** exit 1: the child failed for a reason other than its budget. */
function childFailed(detail) {
  return { exit: EXIT.INTERNAL, header: null, blocks: [], items: [], shown: 0, total: 0, next: null, hint: `the --regex child failed: ${detail}` };
}

/** `grep --regex <pattern>`. `deps.budgetMs` and `deps.spawn` are in-process test seams (history-test-seams-not-env). */
export function runRegex(rc, a, deps = {}) {
  const guard = guardRegex(a.regex);
  if (!guard.ok) {
    return refusal('regex-refused', `--regex refused (${guard.why}): keep the pattern under ${REGEX_MAX_LEN} characters, valid, and with no repeated group over a variable quantifier or an alternation`);
  }
  const key = grepKey(rc, a);
  const pos = cursorPos(a.cursor, key);
  if (pos === null) return refusal('bad-args', STALE_CURSOR);
  const gate = indexGate(rc);
  if (!gate.ok) return refusal(gate.reason);
  let nodes = null;
  if (a.node !== null) {
    const ne = nodeEntries(rc, a.node);
    if (!ne.ok) return ne.result;
    nodes = ne.entries;
  }
  const job = {
    dbPath: historyPaths(rc.home).dbFile,
    transcriptPks: rc.scope.transcriptPks,
    provenance: [...(a.includeRecall ? INDEXED_PROVENANCE : SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE)],
    prefilter: regexPrefilter(a.regex),
    pattern: guard.source,
    pairs: pairsOf(rc.pairIdx),
  };
  const budgetMs = deps.budgetMs ?? REGEX_BUDGET_MS;
  const spawn = deps.spawn ?? spawnSync;
  // No `env` option: the child inherits this process's environment, and no env is ever passed whole.
  const r = spawn(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', WORKER_PATH], {
    input: JSON.stringify(job), encoding: 'utf8', timeout: budgetMs, killSignal: 'SIGKILL', maxBuffer: WORKER_MAX_BUFFER,
  });
  if (r.error && r.error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT') {
    return refusal('regex-timeout', `--regex ran past ${budgetMs} ms and was stopped; add a literal word to the pattern, or narrow the scope`);
  }
  if (r.error || r.status !== 0) {
    return childFailed(r.error ? r.error.message : `exit ${r.status}${r.signal ? ` (${r.signal})` : ''}: ${String(r.stderr ?? '').trim().slice(0, 300)}`);
  }
  const lines = String(r.stdout).split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '').map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
  const done = lines.at(-1);
  if (done === undefined || done.done !== true) return childFailed('it ended without its done line');
  const matched = new Map(lines.slice(0, -1).map((m) => [m.blob_id, m.match]));
  if (matched.size === 0) return notFound();
  const found = rankedAndCounted(rc, REGEX_MATCH, 'recency', grepParams(rc, a, nodes, { blobs: JSON.stringify([...matched.keys()]) }));
  if ('result' in found) return found.result;
  if (found.total === 0) return notFound();
  return renderHits(rc, found.pool, (h) => [matched.get(h.blob_id) ?? ''], a, { pos, total: found.total, key }, deps);
}
```

  - §11 P13 (a cost row per child or source, in characters, against the output cap) and P28 (pasted-line ids).

**Choices** (also in open_issues):
- **`chars=` per item.**
  - A source's `chars=` is its blob's `raw_len`: the bytes of its canonical JSON, an upper bound on its text that is cheap to read.
  - A child's is its `src_chars` (a leaf) or `desc_chars` (a condensed node).
  - `fits` is `costRow`'s answer against OUTPUT_CAP.
- **The child or source lines fit the cap after the fixed parts.** Those parts are the node line, the gist and the fields, and the excerpt. A line that does not fit is left out, and the list's header says `K of N listed`. `expand` reads them all.
- **The producer of a condensed node is its newest leaf's**, found by descending through each level's last child.
- **The producer is re-derived exactly as derivation derives it (Task 8).**
  - The holding copy: lib's `pickHoldingCopy` (Task 8's one rule) over the node's transcript's files: among those that hold the boundary, a live copy (`source_key ''`) first, then the lowest `file_id`, with no status preference.
  - The count starts after the summary row lib's `summaryRowFor` picks: the row the boundary's `anchor_uuid` names; when the anchor is the boundary itself, the first compact summary after it; never a `<local-command-stdout>` echo. With no pick, it starts after the boundary.
  - Every assistant row after that line is a witness, to the end of the copy, read lazily through one `iterate()`; B1's `producerOf` stops at the first backend that is not `unknown`. There is no row cap, so a first real reply far past the summary still counts.
  - recall.mjs spells the pick a second time, in SQL, so it never loads the whole copy; see open_issues.
- **An astral character is never split at a cut.** The excerpt's 4,000-character cut and every `--full` page end move off the middle of a surrogate pair (`pairSafeEnd`), so no page ends with half a character.
- **`nodes.topics`** is read as the JSON array derivation writes. A value that is not a JSON array is read one topic per line.
- **`--full` pages the redacted summary** in pages that fit the cap once escaped (human) or JSON-encoded. Its cursor is bound to the node. `--cursor` without `--full` is `bad-args`.
