  try { return getMeta(db, k); } finally { db.close(); }
};
const offsetsOf = (box: HistoryBox): Array<Record<string, unknown>> =>
  rows(box, 'SELECT file_id, "offset" AS at FROM ingest_files ORDER BY file_id');
/** A recovery step registered on the box's store, as a restore's commit leaves one (§8.4). */
const registerRecovery = (box: HistoryBox, version: number): void => {
  const db = openWriter(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
  try {
    db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(version);
  } finally {
    closeWriter(db);
  }
};
/** A journal file under journal/<storeId>/, written by hand: a head, then `lines` as given (journalRecord output, or
 *  a line broken on purpose). The head names `headStore`, which is `storeId` unless a case plants a foreign one. */
const plantJournalFile = (box: HistoryBox, storeId: string, month: string, writer: string, headT: number, lines: string[],
  headStore: string = storeId): void => {
  const dir = path.join(box.root, 'journal', storeId);
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const head = journalRecord('head', headT, { store_id: headStore, month, writer });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `${month}.${writer}.jsonl`), `${[head, ...lines].join('\n')}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
};
interface StatusView {
  recovering: { step: string; cursor: string } | null;
  health: { pass: string | null; warn: Array<{ word: string }>; fail: Array<{ word: string }> };
}
/** `ccrc history status --json`, as doctor reads it. */
const status = (box: HistoryBox): StatusView => {
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', CLI, 'status', '--json'], {
    cwd: box.home, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 120_000, killSignal: 'SIGTERM',
    env: { ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: preloadOptions([PRELOADS.statfs]) },
  });
  const last = String(r.stdout).trim().split('\n').pop() ?? '';
  return JSON.parse(last) as StatusView;
};
/** The families, epochs, receipts, recall rows and candidates of `id`, compared by name (§8.4 "what comes back
 *  equal"): no surrogate key, no cwd_real. */
const familyState = (box: HistoryBox, id: string): Record<string, Array<Record<string, unknown>>> => ({
  sessions: rows(box, 'SELECT ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms, merged_into IS NOT NULL AS merged FROM sessions WHERE ccrc_id = ? ORDER BY generation', id),
  epochs: rows(box, 'SELECT e.seq, e.cc_session_uuid, e.cause, e.declared_by, e.confirmed_ms FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? ORDER BY e.seq', id),
  receipts: rows(box, 'SELECT event_key, lower(hex(payload_sha)) AS sha, received_ms, ts_ms, ts_source FROM spool_receipts ORDER BY event_key'),
  recall: rows(box, 'SELECT event_key, ccrc_id, generation, ts_ms, verb, rc, ms, arm FROM recall_calls ORDER BY event_key'),
  candidates: rows(box, 'SELECT cc_session_uuid, ccrc_id, generation, cause, ts_ms, first_seen_ms FROM epoch_candidates ORDER BY cc_session_uuid'),
});
/** The journal's records counted by kind, a verdict by its kind: what a pass appended, measured. */
const journalKinds = (box: HistoryBox): Record<string, number> => {
  const out: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const r of journalRecords(box)) {
    const k = r['k'] === 'verdict' ? `verdict:${String(r['kind'])}` : String(r['k']);
    out[k] = (out[k] ?? 0) + 1;
  }
  return out;
};

/** Every entry under ~/.ccrc, files with their size and mtime: "writes nothing", measured. The shim's lock (opened on
 *  every run) and SQLite's -wal and -shm (a read-only open may make them) are left out. Directories are listed by
 *  name only, since a sidecar's create-and-remove moves a directory's mtime. */
function ccrcSnapshot(box: HistoryBox): string[] {
  const root = path.join(box.home, '.ccrc');
  const out: string[] = [];
  const visit = (d: string): void => {
    for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (e.name === 'history-sweep.lock' || /-(wal|shm)$/.test(e.name)) continue;
      const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) { out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)}/`); visit(p); continue; }
      const st = fs.lstatSync(p);
      out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)} ${st.size} ${Math.trunc(st.mtimeMs)}`);
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return out.sort();
}

/** A command on a REAL terminal (node-pty), so stdin IS a TTY: the irreversible forms refuse without one (§8.4). A
 *  pty merges stdout and stderr. The timer is a safety net, never the assertion. A pty child leads its own process
 *  group, so the timer kills the whole group: the shim and the sweep under it die too, and none outlives its case
 *  holding the history lock. */
function onPty(box: HistoryBox, argv: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<{ code: number; out: string }> {
  const full: Record<string, string> = {};
  const merged: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
    ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: preloadOptions([PRELOADS.statfs]), ...env,
  };
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(merged)) if (v !== undefined) full[k] = v;
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const p = pty.spawn(argv[0]!, argv.slice(1), { name: 'xterm-color', cols: 200, rows: 40, cwd: box.home, env: full });
    let out = '';
    let done = false;
    const finish = (code: number): void => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code, out });
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      try { process.kill(-p.pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { p.kill(); }
      finish(-1);
    }, 40_000);
    p.onData((d) => { out += d; });
    p.onExit(({ exitCode }) => finish(exitCode));
  });
}
/** `ccrc history <args>` (the CLI door) and the shim's `--op` (the direct door), each on a terminal. */
const cliOnPty = (box: HistoryBox, args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<{ code: number; out: string }> =>
  onPty(box, [process.execPath, '--no-warnings', CLI, ...args], env);
const shimOnPty = (box: HistoryBox, args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<{ code: number; out: string }> =>
  onPty(box, ['bash', path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep'), ...args], env);
/** The --op pass's one JSON result, its LAST `{"rc"` line (§8.4), with a pty's \r stripped. */
function lastRc(out: string): { rc: number; reason?: string } {
  const lines = out.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{"rc"'));
  expect(lines.length, `no {"rc":…} line in:\n${out}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  return JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]!) as { rc: number; reason?: string };
}
/** The CLI door's --json envelope, read as `{exit, reason?}`: the last line that parses as an object with a numeric
 *  `exit`. On a terminal the sweep's relayed lines (stderr under --json) come before it. */
function lastEnvelope(out: string): { exit: number; reason?: string } {
  const lines = out.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{'));
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    let o: { exit?: unknown; reason?: unknown };
    try { o = JSON.parse(lines[i]!) as { exit?: unknown; reason?: unknown }; } catch { continue; }
    if (typeof o.exit === 'number') return typeof o.reason === 'string' ? { exit: o.exit, reason: o.reason } : { exit: o.exit };
  }
  throw new Error(`no --json envelope in:\n${out}`);
}

    // The pass's own probe (the first statfs call) has room; the step's probe before its first chunk does not.
    pass(box, { HISTORY_TEST_STATFS_AFTER: `1:${low}` });
    expect(counters(box)['capture_paused_low_disk']).toBe(2);
    expect(recoverRow(box)).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, completed_ms: null });
    pass(box);
    expect(recoverRow(box)!.completed_ms).not.toBeNull();
  }, 120_000);

  it('in-process: history-off set between two passes holds the step with its cursor; removed, the step replays a family and an operator mapping at their positions, completes and drops its scratch tables', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-inproc-');
    const P = historyPaths(box.home);
    const { storeId, writer } = createStore(box.home);
    const U = u(0x71);
    const G = u(0xc1);
    const t0 = Date.now() - 10 * MIN;
    plantJournalFile(box, storeId, new Date(t0).toISOString().slice(0, 7), 'feedbeef', t0, [
      journalRecord('verdict', t0 + 1, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'family', ccrc_id: ID, generation: G, project: 'demo', first_seen_ms: t0 + 1 }),
      journalRecord('verdict', t0 + 2, {
        event_key: 'none', kind: 'mapping', ccrc_id: ID, generation: G, cc_session_uuid: U, declared_by: 'operator',
        path: path.join(box.accountHome['claude-a']!, 'projects', SLUG, `${U}.jsonl`),
      }),
    ]);
    const version = Date.now();
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    try {
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(version);
      const ctx = stepCtx(box, { storeId, writer });
      fs.writeFileSync(P.off, '');
      expect(await SW.recoveryStep(db, ctx)).toEqual({ moved: false, done: false, held: true });
      expect({ ...db.prepare("SELECT cursor FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover'").get() }).toEqual({ cursor: null });
      fs.rmSync(P.off);
      expect(await SW.recoveryStep(db, ctx)).toEqual({ moved: true, done: true, held: false });
      expect(db.prepare('SELECT ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms FROM sessions').all().map((r) => ({ ...r })))
        .toEqual([{ ccrc_id: ID, generation: G, project: 'demo', first_seen_ms: t0 + 1 }]);
      expect(db.prepare('SELECT seq, cc_session_uuid, cause, declared_by, confirmed_ms FROM epochs').all().map((r) => ({ ...r })))
        .toEqual([{ seq: 1, cc_session_uuid: U, cause: 'import', declared_by: 'operator', confirmed_ms: t0 + 2 }]);
      expect({ ...db.prepare("SELECT completed_ms IS NOT NULL AS done FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover'").get() }).toEqual({ done: 1 });
      expect(db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE name IN ('recover_verdicts', 'recover_drained')").all()).toEqual([]);
      expect(getMeta(db, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks)).toBe('0');
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  });

  it('in-process: two writers\' overlapping files of one month replay as ONE time-merged group (each file\'s order kept, a tie to the earlier file), and the ordinal cursor resumes that group across passes', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-merge-');
    const P = historyPaths(box.home);
    const ids = createStore(box.home);
    const t0 = Date.now() - 10 * MIN;
    const M = new Date(t0).toISOString().slice(0, 7);
    const [GA, GB, UA, UB] = [u(0xf1), u(0xf2), u(0xf3), u(0xf4)];
    const family = (id: string, g: string, project: string, firstSeen: number, t: number): string =>
      journalRecord('verdict', t, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'family', ccrc_id: id, generation: g, project, first_seen_ms: firstSeen });
    const mapping = (id: string, g: string, uuid: string, t: number): string =>
      journalRecord('verdict', t, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'mapping', ccrc_id: id, generation: g, cc_session_uuid: uuid, declared_by: 'operator' });
    // A (head t0, last record t0 + 30) and B (head t0 + 1) overlap, so lib's orderJournalFiles makes them ONE group,
    // A first. The first record to name a family makes its row (ensureFamily never rewrites one), so the order shows:
    //   - ID: A's family and B's mapping share t0 + 10. The tie goes to A: project demo, first seen t0 + 5. B first
    //     (a pick by <=) would make the row from the mapping: project '', first seen t0 + 10.
    //   - ID2: B's family (t0 + 20) comes before A's mapping (t0 + 30) by time. A's records first (the group
    //     concatenated, not merged) would make the row from the mapping: project '', first seen t0 + 30.
    // The order is the one Task 7's planReplay gives over the same two files (O56).
    plantJournalFile(box, ids.storeId, M, 'aaaaaaaa', t0, [family(ID, GA, 'demo', t0 + 5, t0 + 10), mapping(ID2, GB, UB, t0 + 30)]);
    plantJournalFile(box, ids.storeId, M, 'bbbbbbbb', t0 + 1, [mapping(ID, GA, UA, t0 + 10), family(ID2, GB, 'demo2', t0 + 20, t0 + 20)]);
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    try {
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(Date.now());
      // Every record is longer than chunkBytes, so each chunk is one record, and each call (a fresh budget, and a
      // fresh run with an empty merge cache, as a new pass has) takes two or three: the six-record group spans
      // calls in both journal phases.
      const cursors: string[] = [];
      let r = { moved: false, done: false, held: false };
      for (let i = 0; i < 20 && !r.done; i += 1) {
        r = await SW.recoveryStep(db, stepCtx(box, ids, { maxBytes: 300, chunkBytes: 100 }));
        cursors.push(String(cursorOn(db)));
      }
      expect(r.done, cursors.join(' | ')).toBe(true);
      const mid = new RegExp(`^apply:${M}\\.aaaaaaaa\\.jsonl:[1-5]$`);
      expect(cursors.some((c) => mid.test(c)), `an apply call stopped inside the group, at an ordinal: ${cursors.join(' | ')}`).toBe(true);
      expect(db.prepare('SELECT ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms FROM sessions ORDER BY ccrc_id').all().map((x) => ({ ...x })))
        .toEqual([
          { ccrc_id: ID, generation: GA, project: 'demo', first_seen_ms: t0 + 5 },
          { ccrc_id: ID2, generation: GB, project: 'demo2', first_seen_ms: t0 + 20 },
        ]);
      // UA sorts before UB (u() pads the number).
      expect(db.prepare('SELECT cc_session_uuid, cause FROM epochs ORDER BY cc_session_uuid').all().map((x) => ({ ...x })))
        .toEqual([{ cc_session_uuid: UA, cause: 'import' }, { cc_session_uuid: UB, cause: 'import' }]);
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  });

  it('in-process: a file whose head names another store is dropped and counted once; a file with no head is kept, as planReplay keeps it; an undrained spool record counts journal_spool_undrained_gone only when its file is gone from .draining/, .draining/rejected/ and every .draining/planted/<area>/', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-files-');
    const P = historyPaths(box.home);
    const ids = createStore(box.home);
    const ID3 = 'claude-c-demo';
    const t0 = Date.now() - 10 * MIN;
    const M = new Date(t0).toISOString().slice(0, 7);
    const [GA, GB, GC, S] = [u(0xe1), u(0xe2), u(0xe3), u(0xe9)];
    const family = (id: string, g: string, t: number): string =>
      journalRecord('verdict', t, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'family', ccrc_id: id, generation: g, project: 'demo', first_seen_ms: t });
    // Four journaled spool files with no `drained` record: GONE has left .draining/, HELD is still there (the live
    // drain decides it after the step), and B1 set REJECTED aside into .draining/rejected/ (the store refused its rows,
    // ⟦D:history-permanent-failures-classified⟧) and DISPLACED into .draining/planted/<area>/ (a directory stood at its
    // sidecar name, ⟦D:history-planted-entries-never-wedge⟧). Only GONE is gone.
    const GONE = `${ID}.${t0 + 5}.4242.jsonl`;
    const HELD = `${ID}.${t0 + 6}.4242.jsonl`;
    const REJECTED = `${ID}.${t0 + 7}.4242.jsonl`;
    const DISPLACED = `${ID}.${t0 + 8}.4242.jsonl`;
    const stop = (t: number): Record<string, unknown> => ({ v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: ID, sid: S, ts: t });
    plantJournalFile(box, ids.storeId, M, 'feedbeef', t0, [
      family(ID, GA, t0 + 1),
      journalRecord('file', t0 + 5, { name: GONE }), journalRecord('spool', t0 + 5, { ord: 1, rec: stop(t0 + 5) }),
      journalRecord('file', t0 + 6, { name: HELD }), journalRecord('spool', t0 + 6, { ord: 1, rec: stop(t0 + 6) }),
      journalRecord('file', t0 + 7, { name: REJECTED }), journalRecord('spool', t0 + 7, { ord: 1, rec: stop(t0 + 7) }),
      journalRecord('file', t0 + 8, { name: DISPLACED }), journalRecord('spool', t0 + 8, { ord: 1, rec: stop(t0 + 8) }),
    ]);
    // In this store's directory, a head naming ANOTHER store: never replayed.
    plantJournalFile(box, ids.storeId, M, '77777777', t0 + 2, [family(ID2, GB, t0 + 3)], u(0x77));
    // A file whose first line is no head at all: kept, and sorted last in its month (lib orderJournalFiles).
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(box.root, 'journal', ids.storeId, `${M}.cccccccc.jsonl`), `${family(ID3, GC, t0 + 4)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    fs.mkdirSync(P.draining, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(P.draining, HELD), `\n${JSON.stringify(stop(t0 + 6))}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(P.draining, 'rejected'), { mode: 0o700 });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(P.draining, 'rejected', REJECTED), `\n${JSON.stringify(stop(t0 + 7))}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    // An empty area first, as another drain's would stand beside it.
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(P.draining, 'planted', `${t0 + 1}.4241`), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(P.draining, 'planted', `${t0 + 2}.4242`), { mode: 0o700 });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(P.draining, 'planted', `${t0 + 2}.4242`, DISPLACED), `\n${JSON.stringify(stop(t0 + 8))}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    try {
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(Date.now());
      expect(await SW.recoveryStep(db, stepCtx(box, ids))).toEqual({ moved: true, done: true, held: false });
      expect(db.prepare('SELECT ccrc_id FROM sessions ORDER BY ccrc_id').all().map((x) => x['ccrc_id']),
        'the foreign head\'s family is not replayed; the head-less file\'s is').toEqual([ID, ID3]);
      expect(countersOn(db, 'journal_head_mismatch', 'journal_spool_undrained_gone', 'journal_line_malformed'))
        .toEqual({ journal_head_mismatch: 1, journal_spool_undrained_gone: 1, journal_line_malformed: 0 });
      expect({ ...db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM spool_receipts').get() }, 'an undrained spool record is never a receipt').toEqual({ n: 0 });
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  });

  it('in-process: a stored cursor that does not parse fails the chunk instead of restarting the step; an executor that neither moves nor finishes ends the step for the pass after ONE call', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-stuck-');
    const P = historyPaths(box.home);
    const ids = createStore(box.home);
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    try {
      // Month 13 is outside lib's cursor grammar: never a guess at where to resume.
      const bad = 'apply:2026-13.aaaaaaaa.jsonl:7';
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, ?, NULL)").run(Date.now(), bad);
      expect(await SW.recoveryStep(db, stepCtx(box, ids))).toEqual({ moved: false, done: false, held: false });
      expect(cursorOn(db), 'the cursor is kept as it was').toBe(bad);
      expect(countersOn(db, 'recover_chunk_failed')).toEqual({ recover_chunk_failed: 1 });

      db.prepare("UPDATE derivation_state SET cursor = NULL WHERE step = 'recover'").run();
      let calls = 0;
      const stuck = (_db: unknown, _run: unknown, cursor: unknown): { cursor: unknown; moved: boolean; phaseDone: boolean } => {
        calls += 1;
        return { cursor, moved: false, phaseDone: false };
      };
      // A 5 s budget bounds the red: without the rule the stuck executor is called again until the budget is spent.
      const r = await SW.recoveryStep(db, stepCtx(box, ids, { maxMs: 5_000 }), { index: stuck, apply: stuck, reindex: stuck });
      expect(r).toEqual({ moved: false, done: false, held: false });
      expect(calls, 'one call, then the step ends for this pass').toBe(1);
      expect(cursorOn(db)).toBeNull();
    } finally {
      closeWriter(db);
    }
  });

  it('a chunk that throws rolls back with its cursor, counts recover_chunk_failed and recover_unmoved_ticks, and status FAILs recovery-stalled at RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-stall-');
    pass(box);
    registerRecovery(box, Date.now());
    const seam = { HISTORY_TEST_THROW_SQL: "SET cursor = ? WHERE step = 'recover'" };
    pass(box, seam, [PRELOADS.faults]);
    pass(box, seam, [PRELOADS.faults]);
    expect(counters(box)['recover_chunk_failed']).toBe(2);
    expect(recoverRow(box)).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, completed_ms: null });
    expect(metaOf(box, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks)).toBe('2');
    expect(status(box).health.fail.map((f) => f.word)).not.toContain('recovery-stalled');
    // The count as RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS - 3 more stalled passes would leave it; the next one reaches the threshold.
    const db = openWriter(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    try { setMeta(db, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks, String(RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS - 1)); } finally { closeWriter(db); }
    pass(box, seam, [PRELOADS.faults]);
    expect(metaOf(box, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks)).toBe(String(RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS));
    expect(status(box).health.fail.map((f) => f.word)).toContain('recovery-stalled');
    pass(box);   // the seam lifted: the step completes
    expect(recoverRow(box)!.completed_ms).not.toBeNull();
    expect(metaOf(box, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks)).toBe('0');
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('RB6: while a recovery step is registered, every writing --op form but restore and rebuild is refused (W1-B2 Task 25)', () => {
  // ⟦D:history-ops-refused-while-recovering⟧: Task 6's decideOpGate row, measured by Task 19 in both halves (the
  // sweep's is authoritative). The store is bound and at the code's version, so neither conditional exemption
  // applies: migrate is refused as RB13 rules (its exempt arm is Task 19's), and adopt's two RB14 arms are Task 26's
  // C55 cases. restore and rebuild are never refused (Tasks 27, 28).
  it('each form this tree runs answers exit 2 recovering at both doors and writes nothing; the dry runs answer 0; tree and grep read lag=unmeasured; once the step completes a writing form runs again', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-history-recover-ops-');
    const { transcript } = seedFamily(box, {
      id: ID, project: 'demo', uuid: u(0x31), generation: u(0xa3), workdir: WORK,
      rows: [userRow({ uuid: u(0x3001), ts: new Date(Date.now() - 5 * MIN).toISOString(), text: 'zqrecover words' })],
    });
    registerRecovery(box, Date.now());
    const forms: ReadonlyArray<{ form: string; cli: string[]; op: string[] }> = [
      { form: 'import-apply', cli: ['import', '--apply'], op: ['--op', 'import', '--apply'] },
      {
        form: 'import-session-apply',
        cli: ['import', '--session', ID, '--file', transcript, '--apply'],
        op: ['--op', 'import', '--session', ID, '--file', transcript, '--apply'],
      },
      { form: 'prune-apply', cli: ['prune', '--older-than', '90d', '--apply'], op: ['--op', 'prune', '--older-than', '90d', '--apply'] },
      { form: 'reparse-apply', cli: ['reparse', '--apply'], op: ['--op', 'reparse', '--apply'] },
      { form: 'repair', cli: ['doctor', '--repair'], op: ['--op', 'repair'] },
      { form: 'backup', cli: ['doctor', '--backup'], op: ['--op', 'backup'] },
      { form: 'migrate', cli: ['doctor', '--migrate'], op: ['--op', 'migrate'] },
    ];
    // CONTROL: every WRITING_FORMS form but the three binding verbs and W2's recall-off pair.
    expect(forms.map((f) => f.form).sort())
      .toEqual(Object.keys(WRITING_FORMS).filter((k) => !WRITING_FORMS[k]!.binding && !k.startsWith('recall-off')).sort());
    // No spool line is pending, so a sweep half that refuses after its lock-take journal half writes nothing either.
    const before = ccrcSnapshot(box);
    for (const f of forms) {
      // Every form runs on a terminal, so no irreversible one stops at needs-tty first: recovering is the bump left.
      const cli = await cliOnPty(box, [...f.cli, '--json']);
      expect(lastEnvelope(cli.out), `${f.form}, the CLI door:\n${cli.out}`).toEqual({ exit: 2, reason: 'recovering' });
      expect(cli.code).toBe(2);
      const direct = await shimOnPty(box, f.op);
      expect(lastRc(direct.out), `${f.form}, the direct door`).toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'recovering' });
    }
    for (const dry of [['import'], ['prune', '--older-than', '90d'], ['reparse']]) {
      const c = runCli(box, [...dry, '--json']);
      expect(c.code, `${dry.join(' ')} (a dry run), the CLI door: ${c.stdout}${c.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(lastRc(runShim(box, ['--op', ...dry]).stdout), `${dry.join(' ')} (a dry run), the direct door`).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    }
    expect(ccrcSnapshot(box), 'a refusal and a dry run write nothing').toEqual(before);
    expect(recoverRow(box)).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, completed_ms: null });
    // The read verbs still answer (a read writes its recall line, so they run after the snapshot).
    const tree = runCli(box, ['tree'], { env: withPane(box, ID) });
    expect(tree.code, `${tree.stdout}${tree.stderr}`).toBe(0);
    expect(tree.stdout.split('\n')[0]).toMatch(/^scope=family\(.* lag=unmeasured$/);
    const grep = runCli(box, ['grep', 'zqrecover'], { env: withPane(box, ID) });
    expect(grep.stdout.split('\n')[0], `${grep.stdout}${grep.stderr}`).toMatch(/^scope=family\(.* lag=unmeasured$/);
    pass(box);   // the step completes
    expect(recoverRow(box)!.completed_ms).not.toBeNull();
    expect(lastRc(runShim(box, ['--op', 'import', '--apply']).stdout), 'the refusal lifts with the step').toEqual({ rc: 0 });
  }, 300_000);
});

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the recovery section of `ccd/history/sweep.mjs`.** Insert this section above the `/**` that opens `What one tick of a bound, open store carries` (immediately before `tick`'s two docblocks), never directly above `export async function tick(db, ctx) {`: B1 puts the `@typedef {object} TickCtx` block and `tick`'s own doc comment directly above that line, so a section inserted there would take `tick`'s doc comment as its own. The line before the insert point is the blank line after the function above it (B1's `discoverAndPlan`); end the section with a blank line. That keeps it above the entry guard, which stays the file's last statement:

```js
// ── The recovery step (spec §9.14 "Recovery: one step for --restore and --rebuild"; §9.2; W1-B2) ──────────────
//
// `doctor --restore` and `doctor --rebuild` register ONE derivation step, ('recover', <bind ms>), inside the store
// before it is linked (store.mjs; slug history-binding-facts-before-link).
//
// While that step is registered, and once the store is at this build's version (planRun decides the migration
// first, §6.11), a scheduled pass runs:
//   1. the outbox;
//   2. the migration verdict;
//   3. the secrets;
//   4. this step, within the run budget;
//   5. the journal half (⟦D:history-tick-order⟧).
// The drain and the ingest wait, and no ingest cursor moves, so replayed epochs keep their order before new ones.
// Every writing --op form but restore and rebuild is refused `recovering` meanwhile, by lib's decideOpGate as Task
// 19's runOpPass measures it (RB6; ⟦D:history-ops-refused-while-recovering⟧), so no operator verb moves a cursor
// either. Three exemptions move none: W2's recall-off (RB12), migrate on a store not yet at this build's version,
// which the step waits for (RB13), and adopt on an unbound store, which no pass opens until it is bound (RB14). A dry
// run and a read verb still answer.
//
// The step walks the phases lib's RECOVER_PHASES names, each run by RECOVER_EXECUTORS:
//   index    Reads every journal file of this store, in lib orderJournalFiles' order. Each `redact` record goes
//            into redact_hashes, before any blob is replayed or indexed (⟦D:history-redaction-journaled⟧). Each
//            drain-time verdict goes into a scratch table by event_key, and each `drained` record by file
//            (⟦D:history-recovery-scratch-tables⟧).
//   apply    Reads the same records again through lib replayStep (⟦D:history-recovery-replay⟧):
//            - a receipt is applied with its drain-time verdicts, at the spool record's own position;
//            - a verdict with no event_key is applied at its own position;
//            - a spool record of a file with no `drained` record is skipped (⟦D:history-journal-drained-record⟧),
//              and counted journal_spool_undrained_gone only when B1 keeps its file nowhere: not in .draining/,
//              .draining/rejected/ (⟦D:history-permanent-failures-classified⟧) or .draining/planted/<area>/
//              (⟦D:history-planted-entries-never-wedge⟧).
//            It never reads $REG and writes no journal record.
//   reindex  W1-B2 Task 29's FTS re-derivation, for pairs the index pass added. A no-op until then.
// W1-B4 inserts its export phases between apply and reindex, in RECOVER_PHASES and here (⟦D:history-b4-after-b2⟧).
//
// THE CURSOR is lib's RecoverCursor, kept in derivation_state.cursor. It advances in the SAME transaction as the
// records it covers, so a kill never re-applies or skips a chunk (DI4). Within a phase it names the first file of the
// current replay group and a position in it:
//   - for a group of one file, a byte offset;
//   - for a merge group of several (two writers whose files overlap in time, against §6.9's rule), the ordinal of
//     the next record in their time-merged order.
// A chunk stops only before a record that is not a `spool` record, so a file's spool records never part from their
// `file` record across two passes.
//
// Before every chunk, the step checks the run budget, history-off and the free-space floor (§9.3):
//   - low disk pauses the step and counts capture_paused_low_disk, never recovery-stalled;
//   - a chunk that throws rolls back, counts recover_chunk_failed and ends the step for this pass with its cursor
//     unmoved, and so does a stored cursor lib's grammar refuses (never a silent restart);
//   - an executor that answers neither a moved cursor nor a finished phase ends the step for this pass too.
//   A step that cannot progress reaches doctor's recovery-stalled through meta recover_unmoved_ticks
//   (⟦D:history-recovery-chunk-failure-counted⟧).

const RECOVER_ROW_SQL = "SELECT version, cursor FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' AND completed_ms IS NULL ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1";
const RECOVER_CURSOR_SQL = "UPDATE derivation_state SET cursor = ? WHERE step = 'recover' AND version = ?";
const RECOVER_DONE_SQL = "UPDATE derivation_state SET cursor = ?, completed_ms = ? WHERE step = 'recover' AND completed_ms IS NULL AND version <= ?";
/** The index pass's results, which must survive the several passes a large replay spans; schema v1 has no table for
 *  them. Made by the step and dropped when it completes, as the FTS tables are made by derivation: never part of a
 *  schema version (⟦D:history-recovery-scratch-tables⟧). A duplicate verdict line (an outbox appended twice after a
 *  crash, §9.14) is indexed once. */
const RECOVER_SCRATCH_DDL = Object.freeze([
  'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recover_verdicts (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_key TEXT NOT NULL, rec TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE (event_key, rec))',
  'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recover_drained (file TEXT PRIMARY KEY)',
]);
const RECOVER_SCRATCH_TABLES = Object.freeze(['recover_verdicts', 'recover_drained']);
const RECOVER_VERDICT_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO recover_verdicts (event_key, rec) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (event_key, rec) DO NOTHING';
const RECOVER_VERDICTS_AT = 'SELECT rec FROM recover_verdicts WHERE event_key = ? ORDER BY seq';
const RECOVER_DRAINED_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO recover_drained (file) VALUES (?) ON CONFLICT (file) DO NOTHING';
const RECOVER_DRAINED_HAS = 'SELECT 1 AS x FROM recover_drained WHERE file = ?';
const RECOVER_REDACT_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO redact_hashes (len, sha256, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (len, sha256) DO NOTHING';
const RECOVER_RECEIPT_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO spool_receipts (event_key, payload_sha, received_ms, ts_ms, ts_source) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (event_key) DO NOTHING';
const RECOVER_TICK_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO ticks (ts_ms, lag_ms, bytes, files_behind, bytes_behind) VALUES (?, ?, 0, 0, 0)';
/** One read of a journal file while replaying it. */
const RECOVER_READ = 1 << 20;
/** journal/<store_id>/<YYYY-MM>.<writer>.jsonl, B1's month files: never the dot-named temps a month file is linked
 *  from (B1 Task 15). The month is 01-12, as lib's cursor grammar reads it, so a listed file can always be a cursor's
 *  file. */
const JOURNAL_NAME_RE = /^([0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))\.([0-9a-f]{8})\.jsonl$/;
const JOURNAL_HEAD_PROBE = 4096;
const JOURNAL_TAIL_PROBE = 64 * 1024;
/** The observation replay decides a verdict-less epoch line with: nothing read from $REG, ever (§9.14). Under it,
 *  decideEpochLine confirms only a line whose own `reg` names its sid. */
const NO_OBSERVATION = Object.freeze({
  v: 1,
  observedMs: 0,
  uuid: Object.freeze({ state: 'absent' }),
  generation: Object.freeze({ state: 'absent' }),
  project: Object.freeze({ state: 'absent' }),
  workdir: Object.freeze({ state: 'absent' }),
  journaled: null,
  heldMatches: Object.freeze({}),
});

/** Whether a restore or a rebuild registered a recovery step that has not completed: planRun's `recovering` input. */
export function isRecovering(db) {
  return db.prepare(RECOVER_ROW_SQL).get() !== undefined;
}

/** A journal file's ends, measured as Task 7's planReplay measures a file (which the executor must agree with):
 *  - `headT` and `headStore` from a first line that is a `head` record, both null when it is not one. Such a file is
 *    kept and sorts last in its month, alone, as planReplay keeps it;
 *  - `lastT`, the latest record time in the last JOURNAL_TAIL_PROBE bytes (the head's own time included). B1's
 *    writer appends in time order, so the tail holds the file's latest record.
 *  Null only when the name cannot be opened as a regular file without following a link (O_NOFOLLOW), which no
 *  writer in the tree makes. */
function journalEnds(path) {
  let fd;
  try { fd = openSync(path, constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK); } catch { return null; }
  try {
    const st = fstatSync(fd);
    if (!st.isFile()) return null;
    if (st.size === 0) return { headT: null, headStore: null, lastT: null };
    const headBuf = Buffer.alloc(Math.min(JOURNAL_HEAD_PROBE, st.size));
    readSync(fd, headBuf, 0, headBuf.length, 0);
    const nl = headBuf.indexOf(0x0a);
    const first = parseJournalRecord(headBuf.toString('utf8', 0, nl === -1 ? headBuf.length : nl));
    const head = first.kind === 'record' && first.rec.k === 'head' ? first.rec : null;
    const tailLen = Math.min(JOURNAL_TAIL_PROBE, st.size);
    const tailBuf = Buffer.alloc(tailLen);
    readSync(fd, tailBuf, 0, tailLen, st.size - tailLen);
    let lastT = head === null ? null : head.t;
    for (const line of tailBuf.toString('utf8').split('\n')) {
      if (line === '') continue;
      const p = parseJournalRecord(line);
      if (p.kind === 'record') lastT = lastT === null ? p.rec.t : Math.max(lastT, p.rec.t);
    }
    return { headT: head === null ? null : head.t, headStore: head === null ? null : head.store_id, lastT };
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd);
  }
}

/** This store's journal files, measured for lib orderJournalFiles. A file whose head names another store (or a name
 *  that is no regular file) is `foreign`: never replayed, and counted journal_head_mismatch once when the index phase
 *  ends, as planReplay drops and counts it. A file with no head is kept. */
function journalListing(P, storeId) {
  const dir = `${P.journalDir}/${storeId}`;
  let names;
  try {
    names = readdirSync(dir);
  } catch (e) {
    if (e && e.code === 'ENOENT') return { dir, files: [], foreign: [] };
    throw e;
  }
  const files = [];
  const foreign = [];
  for (const name of names.sort()) {
    const m = JOURNAL_NAME_RE.exec(name);
    if (m === null) continue;
    const ends = journalEnds(`${dir}/${name}`);
    if (ends === null || (ends.headStore !== null && ends.headStore !== storeId)) {
      foreign.push(name);
      continue;
    }
    files.push({ name, month: m[1], writer: m[2], headT: ends.headT, lastT: ends.lastT });
  }
  return { dir, files, foreign };
}

/** A journal file's lines from byte `start`, each with the offset just past it (`next`) and its size with its
 *  newline. A last fragment with no newline (a torn tail, §9.14) is a line too, ending at end-of-file. When the next
 *  append adds the newline B1's writer puts before it, a resumed read starts at that newline and meets an empty
 *  line, which every caller skips. */
function* fileLines(path, start) {
  const fd = openSync(path, constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  try {
    const size = fstatSync(fd).size;
    let pos = start;
    let carry = Buffer.alloc(0);
    let carryAt = start;
    while (pos < size) {
      const want = Math.min(RECOVER_READ, size - pos);
      const piece = Buffer.allocUnsafe(want);
      const n = readSync(fd, piece, 0, want, pos);
      if (n <= 0) break;
      pos += n;
      const buf = carry.length === 0 ? piece.subarray(0, n) : Buffer.concat([carry, piece.subarray(0, n)]);
      let from = 0;
      for (let i = buf.indexOf(0x0a); i !== -1; i = buf.indexOf(0x0a, from)) {
        yield { raw: buf.toString('utf8', from, i), next: carryAt + i + 1, bytes: i + 1 - from };
        from = i + 1;
      }
      carry = Buffer.from(buf.subarray(from));
      carryAt += from;
    }
    if (carry.length > 0) yield { raw: carry.toString('utf8'), next: carryAt + carry.length, bytes: carry.length };
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd);
  }
}

/** One replay group's lines from position `at`.
 *  - A group of one file is read by byte offset.
 *  - A merge group is read whole and merged exactly as Task 7's planReplay (mergeJournalByTime) merges it, so the
 *    executor applies the order O56 pins: each file's own order kept, the earliest head record next, a tie to the
 *    earlier file in the group. A line that is not a record takes the latest record time before it in its own
 *    file. The merged list is cached for the pass, and a position is an ordinal into it. */
function* groupLines(run, group, at) {
  if (group.length === 1) {
    yield* fileLines(`${run.dir}/${group[0]}`, at);
    return;
  }
  let merged = run.merged.get(group[0]);
  if (merged === undefined) {
    const files = group.map((name) => {
      const recs = [];
      let lastT = null;
      for (const { raw } of fileLines(`${run.dir}/${name}`, 0)) {
        const r = raw === '' ? null : parseJournalRecord(raw);
        const t = r !== null && r.kind === 'record' ? r.rec.t : (lastT ?? 0);
        if (r !== null && r.kind === 'record') lastT = lastT === null ? t : Math.max(lastT, t);
        recs.push({ raw, t });
      }
      return recs;
    });
    merged = [];
    const pos = files.map(() => 0);
    for (;;) {
      let pick = -1;
      for (let f = 0; f < files.length; f += 1) {
        if (pos[f] >= files[f].length) continue;
        if (pick < 0 || files[f][pos[f]].t < files[pick][pos[pick]].t) pick = f;
      }
      if (pick < 0) break;
      merged.push(files[pick][pos[pick]]);
      pos[pick] += 1;
    }
    run.merged.set(group[0], merged);
  }
  for (let i = at; i < merged.length; i += 1) {
    yield { raw: merged[i].raw, next: i + 1, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(merged[i].raw) + 1 };
  }
}

/** Where the cursor points in this pass's listing. A cursor naming a file this listing does not lead a group with
 *  restarts the phase. Journal files are never removed, so only a group that changed shape since the last pass can
 *  do that, and every record applies idempotently. */
function locateGroup(groups, cursor) {
  if (cursor.file === null) return { gi: 0, at: 0 };
  const gi = groups.findIndex((g) => g[0] === cursor.file);
  return gi === -1 ? { gi: 0, at: 0 } : { gi, at: cursor.offset };
}

/** One chunk of a journal phase. From the cursor's position, the records of ONE replay group are handed to
 *  `onRecord` in order, in ONE transaction that also advances the cursor past them.
 *  - The chunk takes at least one line.
 *  - Once budget.chunkBytes of journal are read, it stops before the next line that is not a `spool` record.
 *  - Empty lines (the fence a torn tail leaves) are skipped uncounted.
 *  It answers the cursor it committed, whether that moved, and whether the phase has no record left. */
function journalChunk(db, run, cursor, onRecord) {
  const { gi, at } = locateGroup(run.groups, cursor);
  if (gi >= run.groups.length) return { cursor, moved: false, phaseDone: true };
  const group = run.groups[gi];
  let bytes = 0;
  let pos = at;
  let ended = true;
  const next = withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    for (const line of groupLines(run, group, at)) {
      const r = line.raw === '' ? null : parseJournalRecord(line.raw);
      if (bytes >= run.budget.chunkBytes && !(r !== null && r.kind === 'record' && r.rec.k === 'spool')) {
        ended = false;
        break;
      }
      if (r !== null) onRecord(r, line.raw);
      bytes += line.bytes;
      pos = line.next;
    }
    const c = ended && gi + 1 < run.groups.length
      ? { ...cursor, file: run.groups[gi + 1][0], offset: 0, pairsAdded: run.pairsAdded }
      : { ...cursor, file: group[0], offset: pos, pairsAdded: run.pairsAdded };
    db.prepare(RECOVER_CURSOR_SQL).run(formatRecoverCursor(c), run.version);
    return c;
  });
  run.budget.bytes += bytes;
  return {
    cursor: next,
    moved: formatRecoverCursor(next) !== formatRecoverCursor(cursor),
    phaseDone: ended && gi + 1 >= run.groups.length,
  };
}

/** The index pass's one record: a learned pair into redact_hashes first (a pair the store lacked marks the cursor
 *  `+pairs`, which Task 29's reindex phase reads); a drain-time verdict, by its event_key, and a `drained` record, by
 *  its file, into the scratch tables. Skips are counted by the apply pass alone, so each is counted once. */
function indexJournalRecord(db, run, r, raw) {
  const x = indexRecord(r);
  if (x.redact !== undefined) {
    const changes = db.prepare(RECOVER_REDACT_INSERT).run(x.redact.len, Buffer.from(x.redact.sha256, 'hex'), x.redact.t).changes;
    if (Number(changes) > 0) run.pairsAdded = true;
  }
  if (x.verdictKey !== undefined) db.prepare(RECOVER_VERDICT_INSERT).run(x.verdictKey, raw);
  if (x.drainedFile !== undefined) db.prepare(RECOVER_DRAINED_INSERT).run(x.drainedFile);
}

/** The drain-time verdicts indexed under one event_key, in journal order. */
function verdictsAt(db, key) {
  return db.prepare(RECOVER_VERDICTS_AT).all(key).flatMap((row) => {
    const p = parseJournalRecord(String(row.rec));
    return p.kind === 'record' ? [p.rec] : [];
  });
}

/** The apply pass's one record. replayStep (lib, L1) decides; this applies its actions. Before the step:
 *  - a `file` record's name is looked up in the drained index;
 *  - a `spool` record's verdicts are looked up by its event_key.
 *  The replay state's maps then hold exactly what the step reads. A `head` starts a file, so no spool record
 *  after it can borrow the previous file's name. */
function applyJournalRecord(db, run, r) {
  if (r.kind === 'record') {
    const rec = r.rec;
    if (rec.k === 'file' && db.prepare(RECOVER_DRAINED_HAS).get(rec.name) !== undefined) run.drained.add(rec.name);
    if (rec.k === 'spool' && run.state.file !== null) {
      const key = eventKey(run.state.file, rec.ord);
      if (!run.verdicts.has(key)) run.verdicts.set(key, verdictsAt(db, key));
    }
  }
  const step = replayStep(run.state, r);
  run.state = { ...step.state, drained: run.drained, verdictsByKey: run.verdicts };
  if (r.kind === 'record' && r.rec.k === 'head') run.state = { ...run.state, file: null };
  for (const a of step.actions) applyReplayAction(db, run, a);
}

/** The observation a replayed recall or steer line is decided with: the generation its `generation-joined` verdict
 *  named, else none. A line that carried its own gen joined it without a verdict (via 'line'). */
function replayObservation(verdicts) {
  const j = verdicts.find((v) => v.kind === 'generation-joined');
  if (j === undefined) return NO_OBSERVATION;
  const generation = j.via === 'registry' ? { state: 'value', value: j.generation }
    : j.via === 'unreadable' ? { state: 'unreadable' } : { state: 'absent' };
  return { ...NO_OBSERVATION, generation };
}

/** One verdict, applied by an idempotent upsert on its natural key (§9.14), so a record the restored backup already
 *  holds changes nothing.
 *  - A re-key is a merge, which a replayed `family(X, '')` lands in (ensureFamily follows merged_into;
 *    ⟦D:history-rekey-merges⟧).
 *  - Counters fold only where the record proves the event happened, and only once:
 *    - a join's counters only for an epoch line's own verdicts, which apply once, with the line's fresh receipt;
 *    - a re-key only when it merged;
 *    - a drop only when it removed a waiting candidate.
 *    A verdict with no event_key (a later-tick join) has no key to prove it new, so its join is not counted again.
 *  - `bind` and `drained` change nothing in the store. */
function replayVerdict(db, v, countJoins) {
  switch (v.kind) {
    case 'family':
      ensureFamily(db, v.ccrc_id, v.generation, v.project, v.first_seen_ms);
      return;
    case 'generation-joined':
      if (countJoins && v.via === 'absent') bump(db, 'family_gen_absent');
      if (countJoins && v.via === 'unreadable') bump(db, 'family_gen_unreadable');
      return;
    case 'rekeyed': {
      const legacy = db.prepare("SELECT session_pk, project FROM sessions WHERE ccrc_id = ? AND generation = '' AND merged_into IS NULL")
        .get(v.ccrc_id);
      if (legacy === undefined) return;
      const to = ensureFamily(db, v.ccrc_id, v.generation, legacy.project, v.t);
      mergeFamily(db, legacy.session_pk, to.sessionPk);
      bump(db, 'family_rekeyed');
      return;
    }
    case 'epoch-confirmed': {
      const f = ensureFamily(db, v.ccrc_id, v.generation, '', v.t);
      chainEpoch(db, f.sessionPk, v.cc_session_uuid, v.cause, v.declared_by, v.t);
      db.prepare(DELETE_CANDIDATE).run(v.cc_session_uuid, v.ccrc_id);
      return;
    }
    case 'epoch-chained': {
      const f = ensureFamily(db, v.ccrc_id, v.generation, '', v.t);
      chainEpoch(db, f.sessionPk, v.cc_session_uuid, 'clear', 'hook', null);
      return;
    }
    case 'epoch-unconfirmed':
      if (Number(db.prepare(DELETE_CANDIDATE).run(v.cc_session_uuid, v.ccrc_id).changes) === 0) return;
      bump(db, 'epoch_unconfirmed');
      if (v.superseded === true) bump(db, 'epoch_unconfirmed_superseded');
      return;
    case 'mapping': {
      const f = ensureFamily(db, v.ccrc_id, v.generation, '', v.t);
      chainEpoch(db, f.sessionPk, v.cc_session_uuid, 'import', v.declared_by, v.t);
      db.prepare(DELETE_CANDIDATE).run(v.cc_session_uuid, v.ccrc_id);
      return;
    }
    default:
      return;
  }
}

/** A SessionStart line, replayed at its own position (§9.14; ⟦D:history-epoch-confirmation⟧).
 *  - With drain-time verdicts: each is applied in journal order. A clear that was chained but not confirmed
 *    re-enters epoch_candidates as the drain left it, aged by its journal time, so the live tick goes on deciding
 *    it within the same 7 days.
 *  - With none: the drain either kept the line as a candidate, or found its epoch already in place. lib's
 *    decideEpochLine, under an observation that read nothing, tells the candidate. A candidate whose uuid some
 *    family already holds confirmed is the in-place case, and is not re-added. */
function replayEpochLine(db, a, tsMs) {
  const { rec } = a;
  if (a.verdicts.length === 0) {
    const line = rec.reg === undefined ? { src: rec.src, sid: rec.sid } : { src: rec.src, sid: rec.sid, reg: rec.reg };
    if (decideEpochLine(line, NO_OBSERVATION).kind !== 'candidate') return;
    if (db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM epochs WHERE cc_session_uuid = ? AND confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1').get(rec.sid) !== undefined) return;
    db.prepare(INSERT_CANDIDATE).run(rec.sid, rec.id, rec.gen ?? '', rec.src, tsMs, a.recvMs);
    return;
  }
  let chained = null;
  let confirmed = false;
  for (const v of a.verdicts) {
    replayVerdict(db, v, true);
    if (v.kind === 'epoch-chained') chained = v;
    if (v.kind === 'epoch-confirmed') confirmed = true;
  }
  if (chained !== null && !confirmed) db.prepare(INSERT_CANDIDATE).run(rec.sid, rec.id, chained.generation, 'clear', tsMs, a.recvMs);
}

/** One drained spool line's receipt, as drainFile writes it: event_key from the draining name and the ordinal,
 *  received_ms the file's journaling time, ts_ms the line's ts else that time.
 *  - payload_sha hashes the record's re-serialisation: the journal keeps the parsed object, and every writer in the
 *    tree writes exactly that compact text (⟦D:history-replay-receipt-sha-from-record⟧).
 *  - A duplicate is a no-op, never a collision: the bytes a restored backup's receipt hashed are not in the journal.
 *  - A fresh receipt's effects follow it: an epoch line through its verdicts; a recall or steer line through the
 *    drain's own applyEventLine, with the generation its verdict named. `run.ectx.replay` is true, so applyEventLine
 *    reads no switch whose state is today's, not the drain's: Task 11's recall_off_stale count is the drain's alone
 *    (§9.14 "never re-decides"). */
function replayReceipt(db, run, a) {
  const fromLine = typeof a.rec.ts === 'number';
  const tsMs = fromLine ? a.rec.ts : a.recvMs;
  const fresh = Number(db.prepare(RECOVER_RECEIPT_INSERT)
    .run(a.key, sha256Bytes(JSON.stringify(a.rec)), a.recvMs, tsMs, fromLine ? 'line' : 'received').changes) > 0;
  if (!fresh) return;
  if (a.rec.ev === 'SessionStart') {
    replayEpochLine(db, a, tsMs);
    return;
  }
  if (a.rec.ev === 'recall' || a.rec.ev === 'steer') {
    applyEventLine(db, run.ectx, { key: a.key, rec: a.rec, recvMs: a.recvMs, tsMs, obs: replayObservation(a.verdicts) });
  }
}

/** Whether a journaled spool file with no `drained` record is still kept. In `.draining/` it was held, or drained by the
 *  lost store before its verdicts were flushed, and the live drain decides it after the step. B1 also sets a journaled
 *  file aside with no `drained` record, its bytes kept and its lines in no store: into `.draining/rejected/<name>` when
 *  the store refused its rows (⟦D:history-permanent-failures-classified⟧), and into `.draining/planted/<area>/<name>` when
 *  a directory at its sidecar name displaced it (⟦D:history-planted-entries-never-wedge⟧). Replay skips all three, as
 *  the lost store held none of a set-aside file's lines; only a file kept in none of them is gone. */
function undrainedFileKept(draining, name) {
  if (existsSync(`${draining}/${name}`)) return true;
  if (existsSync(`${draining}/${REJECTED_DIR}/${name}`)) return true;
  let areas;
  try { areas = readdirSync(`${draining}/${PLANTED_DIR}`); } catch { return false; }
  return areas.some((area) => existsSync(`${draining}/${PLANTED_DIR}/${area}/${name}`));
}

/** One replayStep action. A `tick` record is the lag series' copy. replayStep answers it only when it is newer than
 *  the ticks the store held below the bind (ReplayState.ticksAfter) and older than the bind itself
 *  (ReplayState.ticksBefore): a recovery pass journals its own tick record, whose row it already wrote
 *  (⟦D:history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks⟧). lib decides that bound; this executor applies every tick it answers. */
function applyReplayAction(db, run, a) {
  switch (a.do) {
    case 'receipt':
      replayReceipt(db, run, a);
      return;
    case 'verdict':
      replayVerdict(db, a.rec, false);
      return;
    case 'redact':
      db.prepare(RECOVER_REDACT_INSERT).run(a.len, Buffer.from(a.sha256, 'hex'), a.t);
      return;
    case 'tick':
      db.prepare(RECOVER_TICK_INSERT).run(a.t, a.lagMs);
      return;
    case 'skip':
      bump(db, a.counter);
      return;
    case 'skip-undrained':
      // Its file was held, or drained by the lost store before its verdicts were flushed: either way it is still in
      // .draining/ with its sidecar, and the live drain decides it after the step. Or B1 set it aside after journaling
      // it (undrainedFileKept). Counted only when it is gone.
      if (typeof a.file !== 'string' || !undrainedFileKept(run.P.draining, a.file)) bump(db, 'journal_spool_undrained_gone');
      return;
    default:
      return;   // 'file': the replay state carries it
  }
}

/** index: the first pass. At the phase's start, any rows a killed earlier step left are cleared. */
function recoverIndexChunk(db, run, cursor) {
  if (cursor.file === null) {
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { for (const t of RECOVER_SCRATCH_TABLES) db.exec(`DELETE FROM ${t}`); });
  }
  return journalChunk(db, run, cursor, (r, raw) => indexJournalRecord(db, run, r, raw));
}

/** apply: the second pass. The per-chunk lookups start empty, except the current file's drained flag, which a
 *  spool record continuing that file still needs. */
function recoverApplyChunk(db, run, cursor) {
  run.verdicts.clear();
  run.drained.clear();
  const f = run.state.file;
  if (f !== null && db.prepare(RECOVER_DRAINED_HAS).get(f) !== undefined) run.drained.add(f);
  return journalChunk(db, run, cursor, (r) => applyJournalRecord(db, run, r));
}

/** reindex: W1-B2 Task 29 replaces this body with the FTS re-derivation the index pass's new pairs owe. */
function recoverReindexChunk(_db, _run, cursor) {
  return { cursor, moved: false, phaseDone: true };
}

/** One executor per RECOVER_PHASES phase, keyed by its name. The contract each keeps:
 *  - it is `(db, run, cursor) => { cursor, moved, phaseDone }`, or a Promise of it, and does ONE bounded chunk;
 *  - it commits its cursor, at its own phase, in the transaction that applies the chunk;
 *  - `phaseDone` hands the move to the next phase to recoveryStep;
 *  - `{ moved: false, phaseDone: false }` ends the step for this pass: recoveryStep calls it no more until the next
 *    pass, which counts toward recovery-stalled.
 *  W1-B4 adds its export phases here and to RECOVER_PHASES together; history-recover.test.ts holds the two equal. */
export const RECOVER_EXECUTORS = Object.freeze({
  index: recoverIndexChunk,
  apply: recoverApplyChunk,
  reindex: recoverReindexChunk,
});

/** The step's end, in one transaction:
 *  - every open recover row up to this one is completed: a replay of the whole journal subsumes an older one;
 *  - the scratch tables are dropped;
 *  - the unmoved count is reset. */
function finishRecovery(db, run, cursor) {
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    db.prepare(RECOVER_DONE_SQL).run(formatRecoverCursor(cursor), run.now(), run.version);
    for (const t of RECOVER_SCRATCH_TABLES) db.exec(`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ${t}`);
    setMeta(db, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks, '0');
  });
}

/** The registered recovery step, advanced chunk by chunk within `ctx.budget`.
 *  - It answers `held` when history-off or the free-space floor stopped it before a chunk.
 *  - It answers `moved` when any cursor advanced this pass, and `done` when the step completed.
 *  - A chunk that throws rolls back and ends the pass's step, and so does a stored cursor lib's grammar refuses.
 *    Busy rethrows, so the pass ends as a busy tick ends (O22).
 *  - An executor answer that neither moved nor finished its phase ends the pass's step: the executor is not called
 *    again until the next pass.
 *  `executors` is an in-process seam (history-recover.test.ts); every caller in the tree passes none. */
export async function recoveryStep(db, ctx, executors = RECOVER_EXECUTORS) {
  const row = db.prepare(RECOVER_ROW_SQL).get();
  if (row === undefined) return { moved: false, done: true, held: false };
  // A NULL column is the step's start (lib parseRecoverCursor); a stored text lib refuses is never a guess at where
  // to resume: restarting would read as progress on every pass and hide a stall from doctor.
  const storedCursor = parseRecoverCursor(row.cursor === null ? null : String(row.cursor));
  if (storedCursor === null) {
    process.stderr.write(`history-sweep: the recovery cursor ${JSON.stringify(String(row.cursor))} does not parse; the step waits\n`);
    countOutside(db, 'recover_chunk_failed');
    return { moved: false, done: false, held: false };
  }
  for (const sql of RECOVER_SCRATCH_DDL) db.exec(sql);
  const version = Number(row.version);
  const listing = journalListing(ctx.paths, ctx.ids.storeId);
  const run = {
    version,
    P: ctx.paths,
    storeId: ctx.ids.storeId,
    budget: ctx.budget,
    now: ctx.now,
    dir: listing.dir,
    groups: orderJournalFiles(listing.files),
    foreign: listing.foreign,
    merged: new Map(),
    // replay: true: applyEventLine reads no switch whose state is today's (Task 11's recall_off_stale, §9.14).
    ectx: { home: ctx.home, paths: ctx.paths, ids: ctx.ids, now: ctx.now, homes: ctx.homes, out: ctx.out, deps: ctx.deps, replay: true },
    pairsAdded: false,
    drained: new Set(),
    verdicts: new Map(),
    state: null,
  };
  const ticksAfter = Number(db.prepare('SELECT COALESCE(MAX(ts_ms), 0) AS t FROM ticks WHERE ts_ms < ?').get(version).t);
  // ticksBefore: the step's bind ms. replayStep answers no tick at or after it, so this executor bounds no tick itself.
  run.state = { storeId: run.storeId, file: null, recvMs: 0, drained: run.drained, verdictsByKey: run.verdicts, ticksAfter, ticksBefore: version };
  let cursor = storedCursor;
  run.pairsAdded = cursor.pairsAdded;
  const floorProbe = floorProbeFor(ctx.paths.dbDir, ctx.deps.statfs);
  let moved = false;
  for (;;) {
    if (!budgetLeft(ctx.budget)) return { moved, done: false, held: false };
    if (existsSync(ctx.paths.off)) return { moved, done: false, held: true };
    const floor = await floorProbe();
    if (floor !== 'ok') {
      if (floor === 'low-disk') countOutside(db, 'capture_paused_low_disk');
      return { moved, done: false, held: true };
    }
    try {
      const exec = executors[cursor.phase];
      if (exec === undefined) throw new Error(`the recovery cursor names a phase this build does not run: ${cursor.phase}`);
      const r = await exec(db, run, cursor);
      moved = moved || r.moved;
      cursor = r.cursor;
      if (!r.phaseDone) {
        // Neither moved nor finished: calling it again this pass would spin out the budget on the write lock.
        if (!r.moved) return { moved, done: false, held: false };
        continue;
      }
      const at = RECOVER_PHASES.indexOf(cursor.phase);
      if (at === RECOVER_PHASES.length - 1) {
        finishRecovery(db, run, cursor);
        return { moved: true, done: true, held: false };
      }
      const next = { phase: RECOVER_PHASES[at + 1], file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: run.pairsAdded };
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
        if (at === 0 && run.foreign.length > 0) bump(db, 'journal_head_mismatch', run.foreign.length);
        db.prepare(RECOVER_CURSOR_SQL).run(formatRecoverCursor(next), version);
      });
      cursor = next;
      moved = true;
    } catch (e) {
      if (isBusy(e)) throw e;
      process.stderr.write(`history-sweep: a recovery chunk failed and was rolled back: ${e && e.message ? e.message : String(e)}\n`);
      countOutside(db, 'recover_chunk_failed');
      return { moved, done: false, held: false };
    }
  }
}

/** A scheduled pass on planRun's `recover` arm (§9.2 "While a recovery step is registered"). It runs:
 *  1. the tick's prefix: the secrets with their redact records, the FTS probe, and any re-index a learned pair owes;
 *  2. the step within the run budget. Below the free-space floor the step does not start, and
 *     capture_paused_low_disk +1;
 *  3. meta recover_unmoved_ticks (lib nextUnmovedTicks: reset by a move, kept by a hold, else one more);
 *  4. a ticks row, its lag unmeasured;
 *  5. the journal half.
 *  The drain and the ingest never run here, so no ingest cursor moves. It exits 0, as a tick does: status and doctor
 *  read the step's progress. */
export async function recoverPass(db, ctx, failedAtStart) {
  let busy = false;
  try {
    const ictx = makeIngestCtx(ctx.home, ctx.homes, ctx.now(), ctx.ids, floorProbeFor(ctx.paths.dbDir, ctx.deps.statfs));
    const secrets = secretsStep(db, ictx, ctx.parsed.secrets);
    ictx.pairIdx = secrets.pairIdx;
    ictx.fts = ftsPrepare(db, ictx.nowMs).tables;
    // B1's reindexForValues is async and takes the load's `complete` flag (B1's ⟦D:history-reindex-by-units-and-complete-loads⟧: the durable mark advances only
    // on a complete load), as B1's own tick calls it; un-awaited, the pass would close the writer under it.
    await reindexForValues(db, ictx, secrets.values, secrets.complete);
    let r = { moved: false, done: false, held: true };
    if (ctx.pause === 'low-disk') bump(db, 'capture_paused_low_disk');
    else r = await recoveryStep(db, ctx);
    if (!r.done) {
      const prev = Number(getMeta(db, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks) ?? '0');
      const n = nextUnmovedTicks({ prev: Number.isSafeInteger(prev) && prev >= 0 ? prev : 0, moved: r.moved, held: r.held });
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { setMeta(db, HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks, String(n)); });
    }
    recordTick(db, ictx, null);
  } catch (e) {
    if (isBusy(e)) busy = true;
    else {
      if (!(e instanceof JournalError)) throw e;
      countOutside(db, 'journal_write_failed');
    }
  }
  if (busy) return EXIT.OK;
  const unwritable = runJournalHalf(ctx.home, ctx.ids, ctx.now);
  try {
    if (unwritable) {
      bump(db, 'journal_write_failed');
      ctx.out('history-sweep: journal-unwritable');
    }
    setMeta(db, 'journal_unwritable', counterOf(db, 'journal_write_failed') > failedAtStart ? String(ctx.now()) : '');
  } catch (e) {
    if (!isBusy(e)) throw e;
  }
  return EXIT.OK;
}
```

// ── W1-B2 Task 26: doctor --adopt (C55) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
/** A store made unbound as a moved volume or a rebuilt home leaves it (§6.9): created by a pass, then store.id and
 *  store.writer gone. */
function unboundBox(prefix: string): { box: HistoryBox; storeId: string; oldWriter: string } {
  const box = makeHistoryBox(prefix);
  pass(box);
  const P = historyPaths(box.home);
  const storeId = fs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim();
  const oldWriter = fs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim();
  fs.rmSync(P.storeId);
  fs.rmSync(P.writer);
  return { box, storeId, oldWriter };
}
/** A session and its transcript, for "the next tick ingests" after the adopt. */
const plantWork = (box: HistoryBox, uuid: string, rowUuid: string): void => {
  plantSession(box, ID, { uuid, generation: u(0xd1), project: 'demo', workdir: WORK });
  plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', SLUG, uuid, [userRow({ uuid: rowUuid, ts: new Date(Date.now() - MIN).toISOString(), text: 'adopted' })]);
};

describe('C55: doctor --adopt (W1-B2 Task 26; spec §8.4)', () => {
  it('DB present, store.id absent → doctor --adopt on a terminal binds it under a new writer, journals the bind before answering 0, and the next tick ingests', async () => {
    const { box, storeId, oldWriter } = unboundBox('ccrc-history-adopt-');

    const r = await cliOnPty(box, ['doctor', '--adopt']);
    expect(r.code, r.out).toBe(0);
    // RB11: adopt prints the carry remedy itself, naming where each directory goes on this box.
    expect(r.out.replace(/\r/g, '')).toContain(
      `copy each to the same path here (~/.ccrc/history/journal/${storeId}/, ~/.ccrc/history/export/${storeId}/)`);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(storeId);
    const writer = fs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim();
    expect(writer).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/);
    expect(writer, 'a fresh token at every binding').not.toBe(oldWriter);
    expect(metaOf(box, 'writer')).toBe(writer);
    expect(rows(box, "SELECT k, v FROM meta WHERE k LIKE 'bound:%'")).toEqual([{ k: expect.stringMatching(/^bound:[0-9]+$/), v: 'adopt' }]);
    expect(countOf(box, "derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover'"), 'adopt registers no recovery step').toBe(0);

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the binding section of `ccd/history/sweep.mjs`.** Insert it directly after Task 25's recovery section and above the `/**` that opens `What one tick of a bound, open store carries` (immediately before `tick`'s two docblocks; never between them and `export async function tick(db, ctx) {`, which would detach `tick`'s doc comment), ending it with a blank line:

```js
// ── The binding verbs: doctor --adopt here; --restore and --rebuild from W1-B2 Tasks 27 and 28 (spec §8.4) ──────
// They run as --op passes under the shim's lock, and BEFORE openStore, which refuses exactly the states they exist to
// repair (store-unbound, store-missing, store-recoverable). By then runOpPass has already run:
//   - decideOpGate: CLAUDECODE, a TTY, not a cc- pane. The three binding forms alone pass under history-off
//     (⟦D:history-op-gate-in-sweep⟧);
//   - the role check;
//   - the lock-take journal half and the statfs probe;
//   - decideOpGate again with a registered recovery step measured (recoverStepAt): adopt is refused `recovering` on a
//     bound store and passes on an unbound one, store.id absent, which no pass can open until it is bound (RB14);
//     restore and rebuild are never refused, and they replace the step (RB6; ⟦D:history-ops-refused-while-recovering⟧).
// Each verb then:
//   1. removes the writer temps a killed pass left. The lock is held, so every temp is stale (§9.4);
//   2. measures the store's facts, its stored user_version among them, and lets lib's decideBind decide (L1). A
//      store newer than this build is decideBind's refusal too (RB17): no arm compares versions itself;
//   3. writes the op marker and runs store.mjs's sequence (L3). Every DB-side binding fact is committed before a
//      binding file names the store (⟦D:history-binding-facts-before-link⟧);
//   4. finishBind: opens the store as any pass does, then flushes its outbox, so the `bind` record lands in
//      journal/<store_id>/<YYYY-MM>.<new writer>.jsonl (⟦D:history-journal-writer-token⟧). Then the release
//      journal half. An exit 0 therefore means the bind is in the fsynced journal (§8.4 "Every writing form
//      flushes its outbox before it exits 0").

/** decideBind's inputs (lib BindFacts): measureStoreFacts, measured afresh on every call, plus this build's schema
 *  version, history.db's own user_version (storedVersionAt, a Presence: absent with no DB, unreadable when it will
 *  not read; RB17's fact), and what the verb names. measureStoreFacts goes first: its -wal/-shm reads must come before
 *  any read-only open, which creates both. `extra` carries what the verb names: a backup (restore, Task 27), a
 *  --store-id and the journal directories (rebuild, Task 28). adopt names none of them, so they stay empty. */
function bindFactsOf(home, role, deps, extra = {}) {
  return {
    ...measureStoreFacts(home, role),
    codeVersion: (deps.migrations ?? MIGRATIONS).length,
    storedVersion: storedVersionAt(historyPaths(home).dbFile),
    storeIdArg: null,
    journalDirs: [],
    backup: null,
    ...extra,
  };
}

/** A binding verb's close, once history.db is visible and bound:
 *  - the ordinary open, which also finishes a pending marker, removes stale temps and syncs meta.writer;
 *  - the `bind` record, flushed into journal/<store_id>/ under the new writer token;
 *  - the release journal half.
 *  A store that does not open answers its word when the word is an exit-5 REASONS word, else exit 1, as runOpPass
 *  answers it; the bind waits in the outbox for a pass that opens the store. A newer schema never gets here:
 *  decideBind refuses it before any write, adopt's newer store from bindFactsOf's storedVersion (RB17) and restore's
 *  newer backup from the staged copy, and rebuild creates at this build's version. A journal that cannot be appended is exit 1, as runOpPass answers it; the bind row stays in the
 *  outbox, and the next pass flushes it. */
function finishBind(home, P, role, deps, out, now) {
  const opened = openStore(home, P, role, deps);
  if ('word' in opened) {
    out(`history-sweep: the store is bound but does not open yet: ${opened.word}`);
    return REASONS[opened.word] === EXIT.DB ? { rc: EXIT.DB, reason: opened.word } : { rc: EXIT.INTERNAL };
  }
  const { db, ids } = opened;
  try {
    if (ids === null) {
      out('history-sweep: store.writer cannot be read, so the bind record could not be journaled');
      return { rc: EXIT.DB, reason: 'store-unmeasured' };
    }
    flushOutbox(db, home, ids, now());
    if (runJournalHalf(home, ids, now)) throw new JournalError('append-failed');
    return { rc: EXIT.OK };
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof JournalError)) throw e;
    bump(db, 'journal_write_failed');
    out('history-sweep: journal-unwritable');
    return { rc: EXIT.INTERNAL };
  } finally {
    closeWriter(db);
  }
}

/** `doctor --adopt` (§8.4; ⟦D:history-adopt-verb⟧): bind a store that is present without store.id to this box.
 *  It is the only binding of an unbound store; the sweep never adopts (⟦D:history-store-unbound-refused⟧).
 *  decideBind refuses (rc 2 adopt-refused) when:
 *  - store.id is present, whether equal (nothing to adopt) or not (two stores claim this box);
 *  - a pending marker names the DB's own id (the next tick finishes that creation);
 *  - the DB has no readable meta.store_id;
 *  - the DB's user_version is newer than this build's: refused before the op marker or any write, as openStore
 *    refuses it before ITS writer's open (G9; DM17 "no write"). The comparison is decideBind's (L1, RB17), over
 *    bindFactsOf's storedVersion; this arm only measures and relays.
 *  It refuses with rc 5 store-unmeasured when a binding input, the user_version included, cannot be read.
 *  On success, store.mjs's adoptStore commits `bound:<ms>` = adopt, a new writer token and the `bind` row, then
 *  writes store.writer, then store.id (⟦D:history-store-writer-file⟧). Adopt registers no recovery step: the store
 *  is whole, it only moved (RC16). The carry line repeats §8.4's remedy, because the journal and the export are
 *  keyed by the store's id, not by this box; adopt prints it itself (RB11), and HEALTH_REMEDIES is unchanged. */
export async function adoptArm(home, P, args, deps, out) {
  const now = deps.now ?? Date.now;
  const role = readRole(P);
  removeStaleTemps(home);
  const d = decideBind('adopt', bindFactsOf(home, role, deps));
  if (!d.ok) {
    out(`history-sweep: ${d.reason}: ${d.detail}`);
    return { rc: d.rc, reason: d.reason };
  }
  writeOpMarker(P, 'adopt', now());
  try {
    const bound = adoptStore(home, { nowMs: now() });
    const id = bound.storeId;
    out(`history-sweep: adopt: store ${id} is this box's now, under writer ${bound.writer}`);
    out(`history-sweep: if the box this store left still has ~/.ccrc/history/journal/${id}/ or ~/.ccrc/history/export/${id}/, copy each to the same path here (~/.ccrc/history/journal/${id}/, ~/.ccrc/history/export/${id}/); their file names never collide with this box's`);
    return finishBind(home, P, role, deps, out, now);
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof StoreError)) throw e;
    out(`history-sweep: adopt stopped: ${e.message}`);
    return REASONS[e.word] === undefined ? { rc: EXIT.INTERNAL } : { rc: REASONS[e.word], reason: e.word };
  } finally {
    rmSync(P.op, { force: true });
  }
}

/** The binding verbs' one entry from runOpPass. It is called for every BINDING_OPS member, after the gate and the
 *  lock-take journal half, before openStore. `args` is the op's parsed OpArgs (lib parseOpVerbArgs, Task 6); adopt
 *  takes none. W1-B2 Tasks 27 and 28 put their `restore` and `rebuild` dispatch lines first in this body. */
export async function bindingPass(home, P, op, args, deps, out) {
  if (op === 'adopt') return adoptArm(home, P, args, deps, out);
  out(`history-sweep: ${op} is not a binding verb this build runs`);
  return { rc: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: 'bad-args' };
}
```
